fp: The female lacks the crimson spot on the nape, otherwise resembling the male with glossy black upper parts and white shoulder patches.

mp: Males have a black cap, back, wings, and tail, with yellow undersides and prominent white wing bars.
fp: Females have greenish wings, an olive tail, and yellow undersides.

mp: Breeding males have black upperparts and head, a conspicuous white collar, scapular patch and rump, and a restricted area of orange on the throat.
fp: Females have pale brown upperparts and head, white neck patches, and a pale, unstreaked pinkish-yellow rump.

mp: Breeding males have a blue frontal shield.
fp: The female has a green frontal shield.

mp: Breeding males exhibit rufous or white plumage with a dark head, small triangular crest, blue eye-ring, and elongated central tail streamers nearly twice the body length.
fp: Females resemble non-breeding rufous males but typically have a less vibrant blue eye-ring and a slightly paler head.

mp: The male has a pinkish breast, bluish-grey cap, and greenish-brown back.
fp: The female has a cream breast and brownish back with subdued colouring.

mp: Adult males have golden-green upperparts, a glittering golden- to turquoise-green throat, and a rufous lower breast and belly.
fp: Adult females have almost the same plumage but with some white on the chin and throat and a paler rufous belly.

mp: Males have black heads, backs and tails, black and white wings, a scarlet red breast, and white belly, forehead and rump.
fp: Females match the male in pattern but are duller, with brown plumage instead of black, a washed-out red breast, and a buff belly.

mp: Adult males have a mostly blackish head and neck with a blue-green gloss, blackish upperparts with a blue-green gloss, and sooty gray-brown underparts.
fp: Females are duller overall than males, with brown tips on their undertail coverts instead of dark metallic blue.

mp: Adult males have a plain grey back, whitish underparts, a dark grey head, black eye mask, and white throat.
fp: Females have a paler head, buff underparts, and a grey back with a brownish tinge.

mp: Males have a black bill with a red tip, a bright golden to golden green crown, brilliant metallic golden green underparts, and a long deeply forked blue-black tail.
fp: Females have a black maxilla and red mandible, bright metallic green upperparts, a white stripe behind the eye, blackish cheeks, light gray underparts, and a shorter less forked tail.

mp: Males have red tips on their secondary wing feathers.
fp: Females lack the red tips on their secondary wing feathers.

mp: The male has black upper parts glossed with a purplish sheen, an inconspicuous black crest, and white underparts.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a crest barred with white.

mp: The male has a red crown.
fp: The female has a black crown.

mp: The nominate male has bright shiny green upperparts, pure white underparts, glittering purple ear coverts, and a black patch below the eye.
fp: The female is similar but lacks purple on the face, has grayish dots on the throat and breast, and black bands on the outer tail feathers.

mp: The male has iridescent green and purple upperparts with chestnut on the wing-coverts and scapulars, and is primarily yellow below.
fp: The female is olive-green above and yellowish below.

mp: Adult males have shining bronzy-green upperparts, warm buffy-cinnamon underparts with irregular green spotting, and a small pinkish to lilac gorget patch on the lower throat.
fp: Females have duller plumage, more extensive green spotting on the underparts, and a smaller or absent throat patch.

mp: The adult male has dark metallic green upperparts, brighter metallic green underparts, a blue-black forked tail with bluish green gloss, and white thigh tufts.
fp: The adult female has bright metallic green to bronze green upperparts, pale gray underparts, dusky cheeks, a white or grayish white spot behind the eye, and a blue-black tail with dull green central feathers.

mp: The male has a black cape with ochre spots, grey finely patterned body plumage, red wattles and combs, red legs with spurs, and long sickle-shaped central tail feathers.
fp: The female is duller with black and white streaking on the underparts and yellow legs that usually lack spurs.

mp: The adult male has a black face, wings, mantle, belly and tail, with bright red plumage elsewhere and a silver-sheened bill.
fp: The female resembles the male but has a brownish belly and duller plumage overall.

mp: Males have reddish-orange uppertail coverts and a less curved bill compared to females.
fp: Females have a more curved bill than males.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely shiny black with a wide white wing band and some whitish on the lower flanks.
fp: Adult females have a grayish brown head and upperparts with a rufous rump, buffy underparts with streaks, and two wing bars.

mp: Mature males have yellow, comb-like feathers above each eye and long head feathers that reveal pinkish-red Gular sacs during mating displays.
Unpatterned and mainly wine-purple in colour, becoming browner on the belly and more olive-brown on the back, with blackish tail and primary flight feathers, black bill, and purple-red legs and eyes.
fp: Slightly duller and browner than the male.

mp: The male has a shimmering violet blue breast and belly, with a metallic green back, crown, and throat, and bronze green rump.
fp: The female is duller, with a metallic bronze green back, crown, and throat, but a pale gray belly instead of bright violet.

mp: The male has a glittering golden green crown, bronzy green upperparts, dark violet-blue throat and chest, dark gray underparts with green spots, bronze-green central tail feathers, and dark blue rest of the tail.
fp: The female has entirely emerald green upperparts, gray underparts, and a blue-green tail with whitish gray feather tips.

mp: The male is bright raspberry pink with a reddish brown underparts, mauve breast and upper belly, white lower belly, and a "browed" facial pattern with an eyestripe.
fp: The female is mostly brown with streaked buffy underparts, broad white eyebrows, lightly streaked pale cheeks and throat, and lacks the male's pink coloration.

mp: The adult male has bright yellow underparts and bright yellow wing bars.
fp: The adult female has similar plumage to the male but is less brightly coloured.

mp: The cock has all-black plumage apart from red eyebrows and a long, deeply forked tail.
fp: The female is grey with dark barring.

mp: The male has a face and underside bright pink.
fp: The female is brown streaked all over with paler underparts.

mp: Males are almost entirely glittering emerald green with a grayish lower belly dotted with green and a long, forked black tail with green tips.
fp: Females have white underparts with glittering green spots and a shorter tail.

mp: Males have a glittering blue to greenish blue crown, dark bronzy green upperparts, a black face, dark metallic purple gorget, and gray breast with bronzy green sides.
Adult males have a distinguishable red crown.
fp: Females do not have a red crown.

mp: Adult males have a yellow forehead with light black flecks, olive-green upperparts with a bluish gray gloss, and bright yellow underparts.
fp: Adult females have a rufous-chestnut forehead, dark olive-green upperparts with a grayish blue tinge, and a yellow lower back and tail.

mp: Unpatterned and mainly wine-purple in colour, becoming more rufous on the back, with dark brown tail and primary flight feathers, black bill, purple-red legs, and typically red iris.
fp: Slightly duller and browner than the male.

mp: Breeding males have black upperparts and head, a conspicuous white collar, scapular patch and rump, and a restricted area of orange on the throat.
fp: Females have pale brown upperparts and head, white neck patches, and a pale, unstreaked pinkish-yellow rump.

mp: Adult males have a broad, well-marked eye stripe, a grey throat and breast, finely barred abdomen and flanks, and a prominent whitish vent.
fp: Females have a pale eye stripe, a barred throat and breast that extends further down, and lack the prominent whitish vent of the male.

mp: Mainly green with short yellow longitudinal streaks, red lores, forehead, and crown, mauve upper breast, white eye-rings, and orange-yellow irises.
fp: Has less extensive red on the head and duller colours on the breast compared to the male.

mp: The male has a shining golden green forehead, crown, upperparts, and underparts, with coppery green uppertail coverts and a golden coppery tail.
fp: The female has coppery green forehead, crown, upperparts, flanks, and uppertail coverts, with smoky gray underparts and greenish coppery tail feathers.

mp: The male has a black crown and forehead, and a black eyestripe, separated from the crown by a broad, sharp white supercilium.
fp: In females, the crown and eyebrow line are the same grey as the back.

mp: The male is mostly all black with a white patch on the flank extending to the underwing, a pale bar on the upper wing, and a striking red gular sac.
fp: The female has a black head and neck with a white collar and breast, a spur on the underwing, and a narrow red ring around the eye.

mp: Males have metallic bronze green to golden bronze upperparts, a metallic magenta purple to bluish purple gorget, light reddish cinnamon flanks, and a tail with reddish cinnamon and black feathers.
The male has a throat that is streaked and underparts that are darker than the female's.
fp: The female has a uniform pale yellow throat, paler underparts than the male, and a yellowish patch in front of the eyes.

mp: The male has a red spot on the base of the bill.
fp: The female is smaller but otherwise similar, with the red spot absent or inconspicuous.

mp: The adult male has mainly black plumage with a white belly, throat patch, tail sides, and trailing edge to the wings, and lacks white orbital skin.
fp: The adult female has mainly black plumage with a white belly, throat patch, tail sides, and trailing edge to the wings, and possesses white orbital skin.

mp: Males have a dark brown crown and upper back, lilac-gold to silvery green lower back and rump, rufous throat dotted with dusky gray, patchy buff breast, and reddish brown belly.
fp: Females are similar to males but the gold and green of the lower back and rump are duller or absent.

mp: Males have glossy iridescent black plumage with orange patches on the outer wing.
fp: Females are duller with a greyish head and lack the plumage gloss.

mp: Males have full yellow heads, bright greenish-yellow bodies, and orange under their chins and upper breast.
fp: Females have duller coloring with yellow only on the forehead, while sharing dull brown wings and yellow lower portions.

mp: Adult males have longer tail streamers compared to females.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have shorter tail streamers.

mp: The male has a black head with a broad white stripe above each eye and down the neck, black upperparts with a white wing patch, a rich chestnut tail, and rich orange-red underparts.
fp: The female has a pale brown head and upperparts, and paler orange underparts than the male.

mp: Glossy green with a brilliant sulfur-yellow belly and long tail streamers adding about five centimeters to his length.
fp: Tiny, pale grey above and washed-out yellow below, with a long, slender and slightly down-curved bill.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and back with white streaks, a white interscapular patch, deep rufous rump, and white face, throat, and breast with heavy black streaks.
fp: Females have a cinnamon-rufous and black streaked crown, lack the white interscapular patch, and have rufous-buff areas where the male has white, with paler flanks.

mp: The adult male has a black head, neck, and underparts, chestnut wings and tail, a prominent white wingbar, and very long tail streamers.
fp: The female has a browner tint to the underparts, lacks the wingbar and tail streamers, and is less showy and glossy than the male.

mp: Males are mostly shining green with a buff belly accented by green spots, cinnamon underwing coverts, and central tail feathers that are bronzy.
fp: Females have more buff on the underparts and less extensive bronze on the tail compared to males.

mp: The adult male has a maroon red head and chest, bright red lower back and abdomen, black wings and tail, and a silver sheen on its lower mandible.
fp: The female is duller with blackish underparts.

mp: The male has a pale grey crown and tail with a darker grey tear-mark.
fp: The female has a pale rufous crown and finely barred rufous tail.

mp: Males have an iridescent gorget ranging from rosy violet to purple, a longer white stripe behind the eye, and a deeply forked tail with purplish brown outer feathers.
fp: Females lack the colorful gorget, have a small white dot behind the eye, pale gray to buff underparts with darker flanks, and a shorter, slightly forked tail.

mp: The nominate male has an iridescent green forehead and crown with gold highlights, a bright green face, shining bronzy green upperparts, a steel blue tail, glittering emerald green underparts, and white thigh tufts.
fp: The female has a bronzy green forehead and crown, a blackish face with a pale gray spot behind the eye, metallic grass green upperparts, a blue-black tail with white tips, and pale gray to white underparts.

mp: The male has a black head with bright blue feather tips, a whitish or buff neck patch and chin, rufous breast and belly with a dark blackish-blue patch, and an entirely black bill.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a red base to the lower mandible.

mp: Adult males have a red patch on the back of the head.
fp: Adult females lack the red patch on the back of the head.

mp: The adult male has a faintly streaked light brown back, yellow underparts, and a bright yellow throat.
fp: The female has similar but duller upperparts with no yellow, and buff head and underparts with fine dark brown streaks.

mp: The male has a blackish head and back streaks, a purer white supercilium, white neck sides, and a light orangey-chestnut breast.
fp: The female is a washed-out version of the male, with a brown, black-streaked head and no white neck patches.

mp: The male has a grey head and tail, lacks dark spotting on the back and black malar stripe, and has grey patches in the wings.
fp: The female is slightly paler than the male and relative, with a brown back and barred grey underparts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black head with a whitish chin, a throat streaked with black and cinnamon-rufous, and a wide collar of cinnamon-rufous or chestnut-rufous on the nape and neck extending to the breast.
fp: Adult females have a pattern similar to the male's but with lighter and duller colors, featuring a brownish crown with darker streaks, grayish brown upperparts, and a buffy cinnamon or tawny collar and breast.

mp: The adult male has a very black crown and a clear black eyestripe.
fp: The adult female has a crown that is blue-grey like the back, or at most dark grey when worn.

mp: The male has a dark blue-grey mantle, lighter pink face and breast, and whiter belly and undertail.
fp: The female is duller brown.

mp: The male has a brilliant orange-red chest and throat, a white forehead patch, iron-grey upper parts with white bars, and a black tail with white tips.
fp: The female is plainly coloured with pale brown overall plumage and a lighter buff underside.

mp: The male has a metallic coppery green head, upperparts, and chest band, with a bluish green tail, white throat, and reddish chestnut belly.
fp: The female is similar but has a buff throat and duller, paler underparts.

mp: The adult male has a black nape, cheeks, ear and eye coverts, and front crown, with pale bluish-grey upperparts and white underparts suffused with pink.
fp: The female has similar plumage but with a dark grey head rather than black, brownish-black ear coverts, brownish-grey upperparts, and less pink underparts.

mp: Adult males have dark grey to black plumage with small white flecks and a culmen base that takes on various shades of red, particularly during the breeding season.
fp: Adult females have dark grey to black plumage with small white flecks but lack the red coloring on the base of the culmen seen in males.

mp: The adult male has blue-grey underparts and a large, crescent-shaped rufous pectoral patch.
fp: The adult female has buff-grey underparts and a large, crescent-shaped rufous pectoral patch.

mp: The male has an orange bill, a black bar across the white forehead, fine black lines on the nape, a white eye patch, a black and white chest band, pinkish-brown breast and belly, and brown back, wings, and tail with black and white transverse bars.
fp: The female is duller, appearing greyish brown and barred and speckled with darker brown and white.

mp: Adult males have drab brown upperparts, a shiny green gorget with a black border, a white breast and belly with a rufous stripe, and a forked tail with bronzy black central feathers.
fp: Adult females are dull brown above and below, with a pale throat speckled with fine dark spots and a greenish black tail.

mp: Adult males display a brick red plumage along its crown, breast, and belly, while its flight feathers have a brown colour.
fp: Adult females have an overall dull green or olive-yellow colour, with brown flight feathers.

mp: The male has a light blue-grey head, neck, and breast.
fp: The female has a less vivid eye ring and more brown plumage.

mp: The male is glossy metallic bluish to purplish black on the upper parts with dark brown wings and may show yellow underparts in non-breeding plumage.
fp: The female is olive above and yellowish below.

mp: The male has a pink face and breast with a whitish forehead and crown.
fp: The female is pale gray-brown overall with a whitish belly.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely white with black primaries, primary coverts, and tail tip.
fp: Females are almost identical to males but have a gray tinge on their back.

mp: The male has deep brick-red rear flanks that are deeper and less orange than the undertail coverts.
fp: The female has rufous flanks concolorous with the undertail coverts and duller underparts.

mp: The adult male is mainly glossy purple with a grey-brown belly and has pectoral tufts of yellow mixed with crimson.
fp: The female has yellow-grey upperparts and yellowish underparts, but lacks the purple's faint supercilium.

mp: The male has all-black plumage with a white shoulder patch.
fp: The female has a grey-brown crown, back and tail, grey-breast and throat, and rufous wings and rump.

mp: The adult male has blackish upperparts with a short white supercilium, a white wing-patch, and an orange-red breast and throat.
fp: The female is grey-brown above with a pale orange-brown breast and throat, lacking white in the tail and having pale wingbars.

mp: Adult males have a black crown, white supercilium, black eye band, speckled white cheeks, olive-brown spotted back, and rufous rump and tail.
fp: Females have a rufous-brown crown and nape, whitish supercilium, buff cheeks, and buff underparts without the male's black spots or interscapular patch.

mp: Breeding males have a black head edged by chestnut, black bill, black and yellow upperparts and wings, and yellow underparts.
fp: Adult females have streaked olive upperparts, yellow and black wings, and pale yellow underparts.

mp: Males have black and white head stripes and a uniformly black throat patch.
fp: Females have less dark, browner head stripes and a smaller, grayish, densely blotched throat patch.

mp: The male has a fairly uniform chocolate-brown body with rufous flanks, white undersides, and striking white eyes.
fp: The female has a fairly uniform chocolate-brown body with rufous flanks, white undersides, and brown eyes.

mp: The adult male has a metallic green head and back with a steely-blue sheen, a scarlet breast, and a narrow purple collar.
fp: The adult female is more drab with dark olive green upper parts, a dark brown tail, and greyish-olive underparts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly brownish black head and body with sooty black lores and an orange eye-ring, and sooty black wings and tail.
fp: Adult females resemble males but are browner overall and sometimes have some darker streaks on the throat.

mp: Has a large grey casque on the bill.
fp: Has a smaller grey casque on the bill.

mp: Males have a velvety black head with a glittering purplish blue crown, shining bluish green upperparts, velvety black throat, and glittering purplish blue breast and belly.
fp: Females are similar to males but duller overall, with breast and belly feathers having buff to grayish brown fringes.

mp: Adult males have a glossy bluish black crown, gray upperparts, black wings with white edges, and whitish to pale gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a chestnut-brown crown with a wide black band below it and a white stripe from above the lores to a partial white eye-ring.

mp: Adult males have a red forehead and crest, gray ear coverts, and a red malar stripe with a bit of black at its back end.
fp: Adult females have a black malar stripe and a blackish lower forehead but are otherwise the same as males.

mp: The adult male has a glossy, metallic green head, throat, upper breast, and back, with a broad brilliant red band across the chest separated by a narrow metallic blue band, and pale grey underparts.
fp: The female has pale grey plumage, which is darker in the wings.

mp: Adult males are dark ashy-grey above with a brown, almost black, tail that is whitely spotted and tipped, and have an ash-grey chin to breast with a white barred abdomen.
fp: Females are almost the same but have a rufous tinge to the breast, and sometimes rufous rump and upper tail-coverts with dark bars, along with off-white sides of the head to breast with dark bars.

mp: Adult males have a red crown patch.
fp: Adult females lack the red crown patch.

mp: Adult males have grass green upperparts, iridescent emerald green throat and breast, and a velvet black belly.
fp: Adult females have grass green upperparts and buff underparts with iridescent green spots.

mp: Adult males have a white face, a black bar on the forecrown, a black strip behind the eye, black patches on the sides of the breast, a pale chestnut crown, hindneck, and breast band, with dull brown upperparts and white underparts.
fp: Adult females are duller than males, with a grayish breast band and brownish areas where the male has black markings.

mp: The adult male has a red throat.
fp: Females lack the red bib but have black-streaked underparts.

mp: Adult males have dark green upperparts, iridescent violet-blue throat, chest, and belly, and an intensely rufous chin.
fp: Adult females have grayish underparts with large glittering blue-green spots on the throat and chest, and a paler rufous chin.

mp: The adult male has a bright golden-yellow forehead and underparts with a prominent black crescent breast band, grey-olive crown and nape, yellowish-brown back, and black tail with yellow tips.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a paler yellow colour and lacks the breast band.

mp: The adult male has a distinctive black cap and deep green upperparts with black and yellow coloration on the wings and tail.
fp: The female lacks the black cap, is generally a duller olive color, and has white from the belly to the undertail-coverts.

mp: Adult males have black lores, forehead, and crown, with an olive or green face, a bright yellowish supercilium, and olive green nape and back.
The adult male has rich brown upper parts and tail, a white hind collar, mainly white underparts, and a solidly black head and central breast.
fp: The adult female has a dull grey head, is dark-streaked on the head and upper parts, and has a rich brown wing bar.

mp: Adult males are fawny grey with a small but conspicuous pink crest on the nape of the neck.
fp: Adult females are fawny grey.

mp: The adult male has entirely scarlet plumage apart from brown wings, with a pink bill and yellow eye-ring.
fp: Females have uniformly brown upperparts and buff underparts, with a small red patch in front of both eyes and a pink bill.

mp: Males have glossy black-blue feathers, a white belly, and a small crest on their head.
fp: Females are dusty brown-grey with a bright orange chest and throat, and a white belly.

mp: Has a chestnut ear, black lores, dark metallic blue head and throat, bronze olive back and breast, and white lower belly.
fp: Lacks the chestnut ear found in males, otherwise similar in appearance with dark metallic blue head and bronze olive body.

mp: Males have red from forehead to hindneck and on the cheek, with a bright golden-yellow chin and throat.
fp: Females have red only on the nape, with the rest of the crown being golden-yellow with green feather tips.

mp: Males have a shimmering metallic violet forehead patch and a shimmering green throat.
fp: Females are slightly lighter green overall with a dull throat containing some white and a slightly smaller chest-patch.

mp: The male is lustrous azure with white underparts and darker grey lores.
fp: The female has a leaden head, mantle, and back with a rufous or orange-tan throat and breast.

mp: The nominate male has a large black mask with a thin white line below it, blue-gray upperparts, and a mostly black tail with white outer feathers.
fp: The nominate female lacks a mask, having a black crescent down from the eye, and has duller, less bluish upperparts.

mp: The male has black upperparts, head, and tail, with brownish-black wings featuring white scapulars, a distinct white collar and throat, a black breast-band, and a white belly.
fp: The female has less distinct and smaller white areas on the throat and collar, which is incomplete around the neck, and a less distinct blue eye-ring.

mp: The breeding male has a black bill, while the non-breeding male has a horn-coloured bill.
fp: The female has a yellowish bill with a dark tip.

mp: The bare patch of skin surrounding the red eyes is reddish.
fp: The bare patch of skin surrounding the red eyes is more yellow.

mp: Males have bronze-and-green undertones but most often look black in light, lacking any purple tones.
fp: Females have a pale eyebrow and a yellowish patch below the belly with fine streaking.

mp: The male has a forecrown that is brown in front, yellow in the center, and red at the rear with a black rear neck.
fp: The female has a whole crown that is yellow.

mp: A medium-sized pied woodpecker with yellow neck sides, black upperparts with large white scapular patches, white barred flight feathers and tail sides, a red nape patch, white cheeks, a long black moustache extending to the upper breast, black-streaked yellow-buff below, and a red vent.
Males have longer topknots, less brown on the dorsal side, darker red undersides, and narrower white barring on the flank compared to females.
fp: Females have shorter topknots, greater brown coloring on their dorsal side, paler red undersides, and wider white barring on the flank than males.

mp: The adult male has a black face, head, nape, throat and upper breast, with olive green upper parts streaked with black and yellowish-green underparts.
fp: The adult female lacks the black of the male, with its head and upper parts being mainly yellowish-olive.

mp: The adult male has a buffy white forehead, a rufous chesnut hindcrown, mostly shining green upperparts, and a rusty lower back and uppertail coverts.
fp: Females have a whole brownish crown, unlike the male's buffy white forehead and rufous chesnut hindcrown.

mp: Adult males have a black superciliary stripe that runs above the eye and over the head towards the nape.
fp: Females lack the supercilium and have a warmer underpart colour.

mp: The male has glossy, iridescent blue upperparts, and black underparts and flight feathers.
fp: The female is entirely dull blue-green.

mp: Males in breeding plumage have a glossy black cap, blue-gray upperparts, and white underparts.
fp: Females have gray upperparts with less bluish tint and are otherwise similar to non-breeding males.

mp: Adult males are mostly iridescent golden-green, with a pale rufous chin and a glittering golden-bronze tail.
fp: Adult females are almost the same but duller overall and with a grayish lower belly.

mp: The adult male has a pinkish gray forehead and face, dark brown crown and nape, iridescent grayish purple hindneck, olive-brown upperparts, white throat, reddish gray breast, reddish belly, yellow eyes, and red legs.
fp: The adult female is essentially alike to the male but is darker overall.

mp: The adult male has a whitish forehead and throat with a narrow black stripe in front of the eye, gray crown and nape, pinkish fawn folded wings with two white bands bordered by black, and a pinkish gray neck and breast.
fp: The adult female is duller with less pink than the male.

mp: Adult males have a shining green head with a golden green or emerald green gorget, reddish purple back and rump, mostly green underparts, and a long deeply forked tail.
fp: Adult females are overall duller with a shorter tail, shining green head and back, reddish purple rump, and pale buff throat and underparts with small green speckles.

mp: The adult male has a very large cream-colored casque on the beak, a silver-grey head, and iridescent black plumage with a white rump and tail tips.
fp: The adult female has a smaller casque and reddish skin around the eyes, while sharing the same general plumage pattern as the male.

mp: Adult males have a cinnamon rufous crown, upperparts, wings, and tail, with black sides of the head, throat, and upper breast bordered with slate gray, and a white lower breast and belly.
fp: Adult females have similar upperparts to males with black bars near the end of their wing coverts, dark brown sides of the head, and an ochraceous buff chin, throat, and upper breast.

mp: The male has shiny golden to bronzy green upperparts, iridescent golden-green underparts, and a tail with mostly green feathers featuring white tips and broad white edges on the outer pairs.
fp: The female has buffy streaks on the face, a whitish chin, and buff underparts with green spots on the throat and breast.

mp: The adult male has brown to chestnut brown upperparts with buff or tawny spots, a chesnut brown tail, and tawny to tawny buff underparts with darker streaks.
fp: The adult female has less chestnut cast, a grayer crown, olive to brown upperparts, and buff to cinnamon-buff underparts with darker streaks.

mp: The conspicuous male is black above and white below in breeding plumage.
fp: The female is similarly patterned but in dull fawns and white.

mp: Adult males have a bright yellow head, throat, neck, and upper breast with black lores, and glossy black plumage.
fp: Adult females have a yellow supercilium, throat, and upper breast, citrine face, and dull grayish olive upperparts with dusky streaks.

mp: The adult male has longer tail-streamers compared to the female.
fp: The adult female has shorter tail-streamers than the male.

mp: The mature male has a brilliant rosy-carmine head, breast and rump, a heavy bill, dark brown wings with two indistinct bars, and a white belly.
fp: Females are dull-colored with yellowish-brown above, brighter on the rump and greyer on the head, and buff below.
