mp: The male has a brown back marked with dark streaks and yellow underparts and face with less of a green tinge, along with greyish uppertail coverts.
fp: The female has duller colours than the male.

mp: Males have a dark brown forehead and crown, a blackish green broad collar, whitish sides of the head and neck, and dark brown back with green and purple gloss.
fp: Females have a duller cap, a brown line through the eye, spots instead of a collar, and a flecked face with a finely vermiculated neck.

mp: Adult males have a crest with entirely red head, crest, and neck except for a small black and white spot on the ear coverts.
fp: Adult females have a longer crest, lack the covert spot, and feature a creamy band from bill to ear coverts with a black line below it.

mp: Adult males have a bright red malar stripe.
fp: Females have no red.

mp: The male has a bluish-black cap, white lores and supercilium, dark slate blue upperparts, and pale yellowish underparts transitioning to white on the lower belly.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has slate gray crowns instead of bluish-black.

mp: Males have more developed orange crescents on their chests compared to females.
fp: Females have less developed crescents on their chests compared to males.

mp: The male is mostly dark grey with clear yellow wing-patches, a broad black crescent outlined in white on the breast, and a white streak above the eye.
fp: The female is duller and more olive-brown than grey, with duller yellow wing-patches and faded crescent-shaped markings.

mp: Adult males have a mostly dark grayish to almost black crown, upperparts, wings, and tail, with a whitish gray throat and pale smoky grayish underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dark grayish brown crown, bright rufous nape and upperparts, dusky wings with rufous edges, and a yellowish cinnamon throat.

mp: Adult males have grey heads with a raised black crest, a white forehead and throat, and a prominent black breast, while the rest of the body is grey or brown.
fp: Females lack the black breast and have a smaller, unraised black crest, with less prominent coloration than males.

mp: Males have a black body plumage contrasting with rufous flight feathers of the wing and tail, a prominent crest, and a yellowish beak.
fp: Females have an overall dull-olive brown colour with dark brown streaks, cinnamon-fringed wing and tail feathers, a shorter crest, and a grey beak.

mp: The male has a dark brown crown, grey head sides, black moustachial and throat stripes, and pale underparts patterned with rufous streaks on the breast and bars on the belly.
fp: The larger female has a browner head and brown underpart streaks and bars.

mp: Males have rufus-orange feathers on the breastband and lack bright pink-cinnamon underwing coverts.
fp: Females have bright pink-cinnamon underwing coverts washed with pale rufous.

mp: Adult males are mostly glossy black with a chestnut rump, uppertail coverts, and undertail coverts, and have long nape feathers forming a crest.
fp: Adult females are overall duller, brownish tinged rather than pure black, and have a minimal crest.

mp: Adult males have metallic green heads and upperparts, red breast and belly, a short orange crest, and a white vent.
fp: Adult females have brown heads and upper breast and lack a crest.

mp: The male has a greenish-black crown, breast, primaries, and tail, with a brownish-black face, dark grey belly, white upper wing coverts, and an iridescent green speculum.
fp: The female has a white eye ring, black crest, white face and neck, white upper wing coverts, and a dark brown body with white striations.

mp: The adult male has orange cheeks and ear coverts with a narrow streak of white under the eye and a trace of a white supercilium.
fp: The female has a thin white stripe below the eye running below the grey cheek and ear coverts.

mp: Breeding males have a grey head with orange moustaches, brown heavily streaked upperparts, rusty orange underparts, and a pink bill.
fp: Females have a weaker head pattern, a warm brown rump, and a white eye-ring.

mp: The male has a greyer cast across the nape.
fp: The female is pale buffy rufous on the upperparts with black streaks on the crown, a pale yellow rump, a white supercilium, and whitish cream underparts.

mp: The adult male is velvety red on the mantle and wing coverts with a broad red breast band, shiny green crown, pink-violet throat and rump patches, and yellowish underside.
fp: The female is olive-brown with a distinctly red rump.

mp: Males have a buff band between the black eye band and chin.
fp: On females the rear of the band extends down the side of the neck to the upper breast.

mp: Males are blackish above with a bright red coronal patch, red throat, and crimson breast fading to red on the belly.
fp: Females are overall dull greyish-buff, pale brownish above, and resemble a dull, unmarked Sporophila finch.

mp: The male has a crimson red head and throat.
fp: The female has a yellow head and throat.

mp: Adult males have brown feathers, red crowns and underparts, a black mask around their eyes, and white throats.
fp: Females are colored similarly to males but with paler markings and are usually less brightly colored.

mp: Mature males have black plumage with a dull red or pinkish red collar on the nape, shoulders, and belly, with a mottled black belly.
fp: Mature females have a black head and breast like males but greenish upperparts and yellowish underparts.

mp: Adult males have a bright crimson coat with white specks and grey neck shades, and possess longer tails and bills than females.
fp: Adult females have the same bright crimson coat with white specks and grey neck shades but are slightly paler in color.

mp: Adult males have a dark blackish body with crimson red heads, necks, breasts, and undertail coverts, and a yellowish bill.
fp: Adult females have duller brownish-black plumage, orangish-red heads and breasts, and a brownish-black bill.

mp: Adult males have an orange-yellow face and throat, a crimson head, nape, and breast, with mostly black plumage and creamy to whitish thighs.
fp: Adult females have a mostly olive-green head, upperparts, wings, and tail, with a streaked olive-green breast and grayish underparts.

mp: Adult males have a red crown, a mostly pale yellow face with a dark red malar stripe, and a black chin and throat.
fp: Adult females have a black crown and malar stripe.

mp: The adult male has a crimson breast and maroon back, with black malar stripes, a yellow rump, an olive belly, and a long green-blue tail.
fp: The female has an olive-green back, a yellowish breast, and white tips to the outer tail feathers.

mp: The male has a velvety black head and neck, iridescent crimson to gold back, golden green throat with a black band, bright red underparts, and brown wings.
fp: The female has a dark green head and back.

mp: The adult male has a bluish gray head, brownish gray upperparts, mauve pink underparts, and red eyes with bare yellow skin.
fp: The adult female has a brown head and wing markings that are less intense than the male's.

mp: Adult males have a dark brown crown, yellow forecrown, dark brown upperparts, and a whitish gray throat with a dark gray breast.
fp: Adult females have a lighter crown and more cinnamon-buff on their underparts than males.

mp: A medium-sized bird with a white belly, black back and wings, white tail tips, yellow eyes, and a red beak with a stocky casque.
fp: Similar to the male but with a smaller casque on the beak.

mp: The adult male has a black mask and lacks any grey tones on the neck and breast.
fp: The female lacks the black mask and has dark vermiculations across the breast and all of the belly.

mp: Adult males have a violet forehead, crown, upper back, and belly, with a dark bronzy green nape, glittering green throat and chest, and a blue-black tail.
fp: Adult females have bright green upperparts, a pale gray throat and chest, a darker gray belly, and a blue-black tail with white tips on the outer feathers.

mp: Males have dark shining green upperparts with a bronze tinge, iridescent metallic green underparts, and a deeply forked tail.
fp: Females have similar upperparts to males, brownish gray underparts with metallic green flanks, and a less forked tail.

mp: Blue-gray above and white below with a unique black crescent behind the eye and a long black tail with white outer feathers.
fp: Similar to the male but paler overall, with a thinner facial crescent.

mp: Males have a red crown.
fp: Females have black crowns with white stripes.

mp: Adult males are a glossy blue-black with contrasting white lower underparts.
fp: Females are duller than the male, with grey-brown breast and flanks and white lower underparts.

mp: Males have a mostly velvety grey chest and head, changing to white on the remaining underparts, with dark iridescent green back, tail, and wing-coverts, and a black crown and eye-stripe.
fp: Females are mostly brown, with strongly dark-spotted pale underparts.

mp: The adult male has a bright red band across its throat.
The adult male is a small warbler with a grey back, black head, white malar streaks, and underparts heavily streaked with black.
fp: The female is mainly grey above, with a greyer head, and whitish with only light spotting.

mp: The male has a white belly with a broad black breastband, a dark grey crown, grey back, black face-mask, and black wings with a white stripe.
fp: The female has a greyish crown, brownish back, dark mask, slight white supercilium, a narrow rufous wing stripe, and a rufous chin-spot and breast.

mp: The adult male has grey-brown upperparts, dull reddish-brown underparts with a dirty white belly patch, light throat speckles, and a red eye-ring.
fp: The adult female is usually less grey above and paler below, with smaller and less marked white spots on the throat compared to the male.

mp: Has a sandy-orange face, a beard, pale slate-grey head and underparts with a buff chest line and a black belly patch.
fp: Similar to the male but has a smaller black belly patch and is slightly duller in coloration.

mp: Breeding males have a grey crown and nape, black face and chin, brownish mantle and wings with a large white wing patch, orange chest and rump, and a black tail with orange sides.
fp: Females are warm brown above and paler below, with an orange rump and tail sides, and a large white wing patch similar to males.

mp: The male has a grey crown, rear neck and cheeks, a small black bib, pale supercilium, yellow neck sides, dark-streaked reddish brown upperparts, and grey-white underparts.
fp: The female resembles a small house sparrow with a streaked brown back, greyish head, buff-white underparts, and is paler with a smaller bill than the male.

mp: The male is larger with a darker, plainer brown back and shows more white in flight than the female.
fp: The female is much smaller with a lighter brown back and less white in flight compared to the male.

mp: Male birds have a red upper mandible with a yellow tip, while the lower mandible is black.
fp: Females have an all-black beak.

mp: Has a stout black bill, black and white remiges and rectrices, and a slash of rosy-pink on each wing.
fp: More dull in color than the male, but otherwise similar in color pattern.

mp: The male has black on the face and throat extending to the shoulders, with a distinct white superciliary stripe and buff upper parts.
fp: The female is greyer above and buffer below, lacking the black on the throat found in males.

mp: The adult male has a black head and upper breast with a purplish-blue eye ring, pink hind collar and breastline, bright red belly and vent, and pale brown upperparts.
fp: The adult female has a muted brownish head and upper breast with more earthy tones and softer hues, while lower underparts display a br

mp: Adult males are glossy green above with copper-sheened areas on the back and whitish underparts.
fp: Females show more copper above, have coppery barring on the flanks, and underparts often washed brownish.

mp: Males have a mostly yellowish olive head with rufescent tinge, grayer olive wings, and bright yellow throat and underparts.
fp: Females have similar plumage to males but are duller, with duller yellow throat and underparts.

mp: Adult males have a dark rufous-brown crown, nape, and mantle with a white patch between scapulars, black back and rump with large white feather tips, mostly white face, black throat, and white underparts with heavy black spots.
fp: Adult females are overall paler than males.

mp: Males have an olive to gray-brown forehead with many white spots and are red from the crown to the nape.
fp: The female is olive-brown from forehead to nape with white spots throughout.

mp: Adults are mostly black with a partly concealed white patch between shoulders, large white tips on greater wing coverts, and black central tail feathers with progressively larger white tips on others.
fp: Adult females have a blackish gray head and upperparts, a black throat, and rufous-chestnut underparts darkest on the breast, with a wing and tail pattern like the male's.

mp: During breeding season, males display more dominantly shown dark bands on their chest compared to females.
fp: Females have less prominently shown chest bands during the breeding season compared to males.

mp: The male has light brown plumage with a conspicuous black-and-white band on his forehead, a chestnut-coloured throat delineated by another black-and-white band, and an orange beak.
fp: The female is smaller and a more dull-brown in colour.

mp: The male has a gray head and back, a black-collared throat, and a black band across the upper whitish breast.
fp: The female is less colorful.

mp: Males have more red facial markings and less silvery and blue on the face compared to females.
fp: Females have less red facial markings and more silvery and blue on the face compared to males.

mp: Adult males have similar markings to females but lack the lines of black feathers on the white side patch.
fp: Adult females have similar markings to males but possess lines of black feathers on the white side patch.

mp: The male has a dark grey head with a thin white supercilium and a broad white moustache, dark grey back and wings, orange underparts, and a rufous red rump.
fp: The female has a paler grey head, upperparts and wings, a duller head pattern, an orange rump, and buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have a blackish gray to slate-black head, neck, and upper mantle, with dark reddish brown upperparts and a usually hidden white interscapular patch.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have gray areas that are somewhat less blackish, a much smaller interscapular patch, and median wing coverts with a cinnamon tinge.

mp: Males of the nominate subspecies are mostly slate gray with darker wings and tail, lighter underparts, a white interscapular patch, and narrow white tips on wing coverts and tail feathers.
fp: Females have a tawny-tinged dark olive-gray crown, upperparts, and wings, a very small white interscapular patch, cinnamon-edged wing coverts, and tawny-buff supercilium, throat, and underparts.

mp: The male has dark greenish black upper parts, chest, and flanks, sooty cheeks, a white or whitish throat, and a cinnamon belly and breast.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a buff throat instead of a white or whitish one.

mp: Has a predominantly brown base colour with fine pale streaking over the head, breast, and mantle, richer chestnut on the back, and pale to almost buff on the belly and vent.
fp: Identical to the male except for the bright rusty-brown spot on the fore-flanks.

mp: The adult male has sooty black upperparts with fine reddish cinnamon spots and bars, and wide white tips on the outer tail feathers.
fp: The adult female is similar but has larger reddish buff markings giving a more reddish overall appearance and narrow buff tips on the outer tail feathers.

mp: Adult males have a head and neck streaked with black and whitish gray, gray upperparts with a white patch between the scapulars, and a throat and breast streaked black and white.
fp: Females have a crown, nape, and neck sides with heavy dark brown and buff to olive-brown streaks, warm brown upperparts and tail, and flight feathers with rufous edges.

mp: Adult males are mostly darkish gray with a lighter belly, sometimes featuring a small white patch between scapulars and black feathers on the throat.
fp: Adult females have dark olive-brown upperparts with more rufous wings and tail, a buff-white throat, and pale buffy ochraceous underparts.

mp: A large flightless bird with hard and stiff black plumage, a low triangular casque, pink cheek and red patches of skin on its blue neck.
fp: Larger in size with longer casques and brighter bare skin colour compared to the male.

mp: The adult male has a blackish head, iridescent green breast, and geranium red belly and undertail coverts.
fp: The adult female has a gray head, breast, and upper belly and less extensive red on the lower belly.

mp: The lower throat and breast are dark brownish with buffy spots.
fp: The lower throat and breast are dark brownish with whitish spots.

mp: The breeding male has a white or nearly white forehead, crown, and mantle with a buff tinge, black wings, white underparts tinged with buff, and a black mask extending from the ear coverts to the bill.
fp: The female is a more gray-brown bird with the characteristic white lower back and less marked seasonal changes.

mp: The male has a dark grey mantle and a glossy black breast band.
fp: The female has a greyer mantle and a dark reddish brown breast band.

mp: The adult male has metallic green upper parts, dark wings and tail, a red breast band, and an olive belly.
fp: The adult female is olive above, with brown on the wings and yellowish-green underparts.

mp: The male has a blackish head, breast, back, and wing-coverts with pale streaks, grey wings with black tips and a white front edge, a grey tail, white rump, and mostly white underparts.
fp: The female is dark brown with buff streaking on the head and underparts, often has a whitish rump, and a tail with dark bars.

mp: Adult males have a plain grey back, dark grey head, black eye mask, and white throat.
fp: Females have a paler head, reddish underparts, and a grey back with a brownish tinge.

mp: Breeding males have black heads and back, a rusty breast, buffy-yellow nape, white abdomen, and elongated black tail feathers up to 36 cm.
fp: Females have greyish-brown feathers with blackish streaks, a grey bill, and more white under tail feathers.

mp: The male has a black head, white throat with a chestnut patch, red iris, brownish-red nape, grey-brown back, and pale cinnamon underparts.
fp: The female is smaller with an olive-grey crown and is similar in colouring to the male but slightly duller.

mp: The adult male has a grey back and head, brick-red underparts, and white malar streaks.
fp: The female is mainly brown above, with a greyer head, and whitish below with a pink flush.

mp: Males have a white patch below the throat and white tips on the outer tail feathers.
fp: Females have light brown throat patch and light brown tips on the outer tail feathers.

mp: Breeding adult males are basically olive-green above and yellow below, with heads varying in color and pattern by subspecies.
fp: Females often have yellow diluted by white, similar to first-winter birds.

mp: The male is lighter overall with one black and one pink neck collar and blue suffusion above it.
fp: The female is darker overall with an indistinct black collar and a green collar that becomes dark green across the cheeks.

mp: The male has a grayish pink forehead and face that darkens to deep mauve pink on the breast and underparts, with a bluish gray crown and nape.
fp: The female is browner than the male with less of a pink wash.

mp: The male has a glittering violet purple hood bordered below by a horizontal black chest stripe, dark olive green above, white below, and blue-green central tail feathers.
fp: The female is duller dusty olive green above with a whitish throat speckled with brown spots, a dark tail, and pale grayish underparts.

mp: The male has a black face and throat with a red eye ring, iridescent green crown, nape, upperparts, and upper breast, and a deep red lower breast, belly, and vent.
fp: The female replaces the male's green parts with shades of gray.

mp: The male is mainly blue-black with a crest.
fp: The female is a drab brown bird.

mp: Adult males have a rufous forehead, bright turquoise-blue crown and nape, black head and throat, glossy purplish black upperparts, and tawny-orange underparts.
fp: Adult females have a rufous forehead, bright sky-blue crown and nape, olive head with cinnamon throat, bright olive-green upperparts, and dusky flight feathers with olive-green edges.

mp: Predominantly golden olive with a dark blue frontal band above, lighter blue, and yellow abdomen and vent.
fp: A duller shade of olive all over with a narrower blue frontal band.

mp: The male has a distinctive long, straight, golden-buff crest.
fp: The female has a grey crest.

mp: Males are brown and white with a black throat, chestnut-brown upper parts, white belly, nape and wing bars, red bare facial skin, and long rusty-barred whitish tail.
fp: Females are rufous brown with a blackish throat, whitish belly, and less barred tail.

mp: The male has dark shining green upperparts, a narrow glittering bluish green forehead, a large white patch with green spots on its upper breast, and glittering bluish green underparts.
fp: The female is similar but lacks the bluish green forehead and has somewhat shorter wings and tail.

mp: The adult male has metallic bronze green to greenish bronze upperparts, a brilliant metallic emerald green chin and upper throat, and a velvety black to dusky metallic bronze green lower throat.
fp: The adult female is similar to the male but lacks the metallic throat, and her underparts are entire.

mp: Adult males are mostly bright light green with black streaking on the upperparts, black loral area and auricular patch, and dark yellow center and rear of the crown.
fp: Females are duller than males and have yellow-green in place of the yellow on the head.

mp: The adult male has a glittering dark green forehead, face, and breast with a square pale violet throat patch, dark bronzy green upperparts, and a glittering golden green belly.
fp: The adult female has bronzy green upperparts, a grayish throat and breast with bronzy green flecking, solid bronzy green flanks, and a golden green belly.

mp: The male is black, with white-tipped undertail coverts.
fp: Female and immature birds range in color from dull gray to matte black, and frequently show white edges to the feathers of their underparts.

mp: The male is brown-and-black-streaked with a broad white eye stripe and orange-red chest band in breeding plumage, and is less colourful than the female.
fp: The female is more colourful and brighter than the male, featuring a chestnut breast bordered above with white and a black belly in summer.

mp: The male is striking in typical oriole black and yellow plumage.
fp: The female is a drabber green bird.

mp: The summer male has a grey nape, red head-patch and red breast.
fp: Females lack the red and have white underparts, the breast streaked buff.

mp: The male has a white wing patch across three primary feathers and white tips to the two outer tail feathers.
fp: Females do not show any white in flight.

mp: The adult male has black and white plumage with a yellow crown.
fp: The adult female has black and white plumage without a yellow crown.

mp: The breeding male has a chestnut head with a creamy crown, pink breast, white belly, grey flanks and back, black rear end, and dark green speculum.
fp: The female is light brown, though it can be a rufous morph with a redder head or a gray morph with a grayer head.

mp: The male has a blue-grey head.
fp: The female has a brown head and is slightly larger and darker than the male.

mp: The breeding male has finely vermiculated grey body plumage, long sickle-shaped tertials, a dark green head with white throat, and a bronzed crown.
fp: The female is dark brown with plumage similar to a female wigeon and has a long grey bill.

mp: The male has brown to grey plumage with a contrasting light grey-white head and a distinctive orange bill.
fp: The female is darker with a brown neck and head and an olive green beak.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead and crown with thin white bars, and the rest of their plumage is thin black and white bars.
fp: Females have a rufous crown and plumage of thin dark brown and pale yellowish brown bars with a tail barred with dark brown and pale buff.

mp: The male has a medium blue crown and nape, a deep black mask, dull blue mantle and back, bright turquoise-blue lower back and rump, dusky blue tail, and cinnamon throat and underparts.
fp: The female has similar coloration to the male but is usually duller.

mp: Males have a distinctive black malar stripe.
fp: Females have a black malar stripe heavily streaked with white.

mp: The breeding male is a rich, dark chestnut on the head, breast and flanks with contrasting pure white undertail coverts and a yellow eye.
fp: The females are duller and browner than the males and have a dark eye.

mp: Adult males have an iridescent green forehead with a band of stiff black feathers, green cheek tufts tipped with white, and a glittering green ruff around the bill and chin.
fp: Adult females have blackish cheeks without tufts but with a white moustache, a pale buff chin with a dark spot, and brownish underparts with whitish scaling.

mp: Adults have a black head, neck, and throat with a chestnut collar on the nape, blue-green back, red rump, bright yellow underparts with a red belly band, and chestnut thighs.
fp: Females differ from males only in having a darker chestnut collar and a shorter bill.

mp: The male has a glossy black head and mantle with an orange-red back, wings, and underparts, and a black and orange-red tail.
fp: The female has a grey head with orange lores and eye-rims, a lead grey back, orange-red rump, and yellow underparts.

mp: The male has white spots on the four outermost wing feathers.
The adult male has green upperparts, a shiny emerald green throat and belly with a black center, and a violet tail top with all-green central feathers.
fp: The adult female has green upperparts, white underparts with a black stripe down the middle, and a bluish black tail with white-tipped outer feathers.

mp: The adult male has a bright green head and upper parts with white tertial tips, and a bright orangish-red throat and chest contrasting with green underparts.
fp: The adult female has upper parts similar to the male, with a green breast and a belly barred with green and yellow.

mp: Males have a shining orange-red back and belly, velvet black head, iridescent green and orange-red throat, and two elongated central tail feathers.
fp: Females are shining green above with a coppery red gorget bordered by a narrow orange-yellow-green band.

mp: The adult male has a red crown and red moustachial stripes.
fp: The female has a dark forecrown with red on the rear half and lacks red moustaches.

mp: In summer, the male is a white and black bird with a white crown, central back, and belly contrasting with a black face, throat, and wings.
fp: The female is brown-grey above, becoming dirty white below, with a tail pattern similar to the male's.

mp: The male has glossy blue-black upperparts, a buffy underside with a bright red breast patch, and a short black stripe down the belly.
fp: The female is dark olive above and buff below, with olive sides and a bill that has a pale base.

mp: Breeding males have a scarlet nape and mantle, yellow-orange breast, olive-green belly, and a long scarlet tail.
fp: Females have a grey-olive head and throat, a yellow belly, and are about two-thirds the length of males.

mp: The adult male has fiery orange upper tufts of feathers at the base of the beak.
fp: The adult female lacks the fiery orange upper tufts, sharing the general green plumage, brownish-maroon nape, and grey lores.

mp: The adult male is black above and white below with white wing patches and white sides to the tail.
fp: The female is brown above, somewhat like an immature fiscal shrike, not black.

mp: The male has a black head, small orangeish-red bib, moderate-sized orangish crest, slatey-black upper parts with golden-buff rump and white wing-coverts, and dark brownish-black underparts.
fp: The female is more brown above with buff-ochre underparts and resembles the white-winged shrike-tanager.

mp: Males have velvety black plumage with a scarlet-red spot on the back, orange to red chest and rump, bright yellow belly, and a cobalt blue to silver or whitish beak with a black tip.
fp: Females have an olive-brown back with dark spots, a reddish-orange rump, and a light yellow chest and belly.

mp: Males have an orange centre to the crown stripe.
fp: Females have a pure yellow crown stripe.

mp: Adult males have an olive crown with a mostly hidden yellow or orange patch in the middle.
fp: Females lack the yellow or orange crown patch found in males but share other olive and yellow plumage features.

mp: The adult male has a black head with a white forehead, throat patch, and broken eye-ring, reddish sandy brown upperparts, and grey primaries tipped white.
fp: The adult female has a sandy-brown crown and forehead, duller black and white facial markings than the male, and primaries not tipped white.

mp: Males have darker gray bills with slight yellow accents and are heavier but have smaller cranial elements and wingspans than females.
fp: Females have smaller orange bills with black tips and possess brown head and neck feathers with white stripes stretching from their eyes to the napes of their necks.

mp: The male has yellow feathers with a slight green tint on the back and wings, and a black mask with black streaks on the upper parts.
fp: The female has a greenish-gray color with yellow on its underparts, and a black mask with black streaks on the upper parts.

mp: The male has a white nape, blue wings, head and tail, with a white breast, abdomen, and a white patch in front of the eyes.
fp: The female is distinguished by having a blue rather than white nape, while sharing the blue wings, head, tail, and white breast.

mp: The male has black and white bands on its forehead and separating the breast from the heavily barred belly.
fp: The female lacks the head and breast bands and is heavily barred on the back and flanks.

mp: Adult males have a long, rufous-orange erectile crest, green and white fan-shaped cheek feathers, iridescent green forehead and throat, grayish green underparts, and a tail with central bronzy green feathers and rufous rest.
fp: Adult females lack the male's crest and cheek tufts, have a whitish throat with rufous discs and dark crescents, grayish green underparts, and an overall dark bronze tail with rufous ends.

mp: The male has a red crown with an orange forehead.
fp: The female has a black crown.

mp: Adult males have a lemon-yellow forehead, glossy blue-black crown, face, and upperparts, with golden-yellow breast and sides.
fp: Adult females have a rufous forehead, bronzy olive-green crown and upper back, and lack the male's bright colors.

mp: The breeding male is patterned grey with a black rear end, light chestnut wings, and a brilliant white speculum.
fp: The female is light brown with plumage much like a female mallard, distinguished by a dark orange-edged bill and white belly.

mp: The male has a bright red head and crest, with mostly mild grey body feathers.
fp: The female has a small fluffy grey crest and dark grey head, with lighter scalloping on her grey body.

mp: The adult male has a brown head and breast with a broad white crescent over the eye, grey plumage, and a pale blue speculum with a white border.
fp: The female is brown with stronger face markings, a pale eyebrow, dark eye line, and a pale lore spot bordered by a second dark line.

mp: The adult male has iridescent green upperparts, a black face with a white spot, a shining rosy pink gorget, iridescent violet-blue breast, blackish underparts with mottled green flanks, rufous wings, and a dark purple tail.
fp: The adult female has iridescent green upperparts, dusky gray underparts with small pinkish throat dots, and wings and tail similar to the male but with white tips on the outer tail feathers.

mp: Males have bronzy green upperparts, glittery violet throat patches, white chest patches, and an elongated white patch behind the eye.
fp: Females have white throats with green speckles but are otherwise like the male.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead, crown, and crest, with a back, wings, and tail barred with black and white, and neutral gray face, nape, throat, and underparts.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crest with some black feather tips, a back, wings, and tail barred with cinnamon-buff and dark brown, and mostly olive face, nape, throat, and underparts.

mp: The male giant cowbird is iridescent black with a long tail, long bill, small head, and a neck ruff which is expanded in display.
fp: The female is smaller, less iridescent than the male, and lacks the neck ruff, making her look less small-headed.

mp: The male has a chestnut breast band and otherwise white underparts with dark flank barring.
fp: The female has a white-spotted black breast band and a chestnut belly.

mp: The male has a deep black eyestripe that is faintly glossed blue and off-white cheeks.
fp: The female has duller eye features and less contrast between the crown, nape, and lower back.

mp: It has mainly black upperparts, tail, wings, and mask with yellow spotty bars and edging, a pale yellow belly with black flank streaking, and a throat ranging from red to orange with a crown from deep yellow to reddish-orange.
fp: The female resembles the male but has extensive orange-yellow edging on the wing-coverts, yellowish streaking on the auriculars and back, and black streaking on the flanks that extends over the chest.

mp: The male is generally dark sky blue that is lighter on the forehead and rump and is grayish on the lower belly, with a small black mask.
fp: The female is brown overall, warm and dark above and orange-tinged below.

mp: The male has a dull bronzy green forehead and crown, slightly golden green upperparts, grass green uppertail coverts, a dark steely blue tail, a blue-green throat and upper breast, and a bronze to bronzy green belly.
fp: The female has a slightly golden green forehead, crown, and upperparts, grass green uppertail coverts, and tail feathers with green inner and blue outer halves on the innermost pair and steel blue on the others.

mp: Adult males have golden- to bronze-green upperparts, a dark bronze-green to blackish bronze tail, a glittering golden-green throat and breast, and a white belly with white undertail coverts.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have white bars near the end of their throat feathers and greenish-gray tips on their outermost tail feathers.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely black with dark gray lower back, rump, lower belly, and crissum, and some concealed white.
fp: Adult females resemble males but have a deep chestnut-brown forehead and crest.

mp: Predominantly black with a chocolate-brown head and striking caudal red patches.
fp: Duller dark brown with flecks of yellow in the tail and collar, and a barred tail.

mp: Adult males of the nominate subspecies are almost entirely glossy black with a yellow eye-ring and a yellow bill.
fp: Adult females have a dark olive-brown head and upperparts, slightly paler and redder underparts, a brownish bill, and no eye-ring.

mp: The male has shining dark green upperparts, a glittering purple throat patch, shining blackish green throat and upper breast, glittering golden green belly, white leg puffs, and a dark steel blue forked tail.
fp: The female has shining golden green upperparts, a throat patch of bluish purple discs on a buffy background, buff throat and breast, and a grayish white belly with golden green discs.

mp: The male has a black beak, green plumage, yellow moustaches, a blue throat, and small blue and red spots on the head.
fp: The female appears similar to the male but has a beak that is paler with a dusky bluish color.

mp: Bright yellow body with black head, orange-brown stomach, and dark green on wing feathers.
fp: Completely covered in dull yellow feathers with a bit of green on wings.

mp: Adult males have an olive forecrown, grayish crown and nape, ashy whitish gray lores, chin, and cheeks, olive-green upperparts with a bluish gray gloss, and mostly yellow underparts with a clear yellow belly.
fp: Adult females are overall duller than males and have less white on their face.

mp: Males have a blackish crown with a glittering green forehead, shining dark green upper back, glittering green throat with a small violet patch, and variable glittering copper to reddish gold underparts.
fp: Females have a plain green forehead, duller upperparts similar to males, a plain buff throat with green spots, a mottled buff and green breast, and mostly cinnamon underparts with a reddish gold belly.

mp: The male has a brown head and wings with bright yellow-gold underparts, tail, crest, and nape.
fp: The female is olive brown with ash-gray underparts.

mp: Adult males have a grass-green head, upperparts, and tail with bright yellow throat and middle breast, and lemon-yellow lower breast.
fp: Adult females have the same head, upperparts, tail, and wings as males, but their underparts are green with yellow streaks.

mp: Adult males have a pale violet-blue crown and nape, golden-yellow forehead and wide supercilium, turquoise eye-ring, emerald-green face and throat, and bright yellow lower breast and belly.
fp: Adult females have a yellow forehead and a light blue central crown.

mp: Males have a brownish olive tone on their backs with a bright yellow-orange tone on their underside.
fp: Females have the same color patterns as males but are duller and less vibrant.

mp: Adult males have a jet black crown, back, wings, and tail, with a deep glossy golden-yellow chin, throat, and breast forming a collar, plus olive green lower parts.
fp: Adult females are mostly olive green with a paler yellow-olive wash on the lower breast and belly, and dusky wings and tail with olive edges.

mp: Adult males have a black head, nape, and shoulders, a narrow yellow band on the back, mostly black underparts with gold-yellow flanks, and red undertail coverts.
fp: Adult females replace the male's black with chestnut, have duller facial tufts and flanks, and a narrower yellow band on the back.

mp: The adult male has a brilliant golden green crown, duller golden green to bronzy green upperparts, and underparts transitioning from pure green to brilliant golden green at the vent.
fp: The adult female has light gray underparts, dusky cheeks with a grayish white streak behind the eye, and a shorter forked tail with bluish green to bronze green central feathers.

mp: The male has bright golden-yellow body feathers that appear almost iridescent, with a slightly duller head having a greenish tinge, bluish-green bill and legs, and yellow underwings and tail coverts.
fp: The female is a dark green bird with bare parts resembling those of the male.

mp: Green-bodied with a black face and throat bordered with yellow, yellowish orange forehead, and blue moustachial line.
fp: Similar to the male but the black of the face and throat appears slightly duller.

mp: Males have red from forehead to nape, olive green around the eye and neck, a pale yellow stripe, a short red malar band, and an olive green stripe below.
fp: Females have no red on the head, with olive from forehead to nape and an olive-brown malar area.

mp: Males are bright yellow with a black wing and back, featuring white spots on wing-coverts that wear over time.
fp: Females have brown wings and brown streaks covering the head, flanks, back and rump.

mp: During breeding season, the male has a golden body colour, a golden-orange head, a dull chin, and a shorter tail.
fp: Females are similar to males outside the breeding season, characterized by a cream-coloured underside and a brown back.

mp: The adult male is entirely black apart from a golden head, yellow bill, white and red thighs, and pink legs.
fp: The female is olive-green with pink legs.

mp: The male has iridescent golden-green wings and breast, a gold-bronze head, and yellow bills.
fp: The female is less brightly coloured with duller brownish breast, duller golden-brown head, and brownish greyish bills.

mp: The adult male has a golden head with a black eyemask edged with violet blue, black upperparts with turquoise shoulders, blue flanks, and a white central belly.
fp: Females have a greenish tinge to the head, sometimes with black speckling on the crown, and more extensively white underparts.

mp: The male is a bright golden colour with sharply delineated black cheeks, throat, wings, and tail, and a distinctive white teardrop pattern under the eye.
fp: The female lacks black colouring, appearing olive-greenish with more yellowish underparts, and also has a black bill and a white teardrop pattern under the eye.

mp: Primarily blue with black facial masking and a golden or reddish crown patch or nape.
fp: Similar pattern to males but with duller colors and a narrower nape patch.

mp: The male has a yellow fore-crown and a red central-crown.
fp: The female has a whole yellow crown except for a narrow central transverse black band.

mp: The adult male is yellow below and yellow in the wings, with a yellow throat and breast and a dark band.
fp: The female is a fairly typical brown pipit but has a yellow underside to the wing.

mp: Adult males have a bright turquoise-blue crown and nape, black face and throat, black back with a blue gloss, golden-yellow rump, and deep yellow underparts.
fp: Adult females have a tawny to yellowish buff forehead and a turquoise-blue crown and nape that curves forward like the male's.

mp: The adult male is mainly blue with a yellow shoulder area, black cap, pale yellow frontal band, and dark salmon pink lower belly.
fp: Adult females are mainly dull greenish-yellow with a broad cream bar on the underside of the wings and a charcoal grey cap.

mp: Adult males have a violet-blue head and throat, a bright green back transitioning to coppery coverts and a copper-bronze tail, with a glittering green breast and bronze-green belly.
fp: Adult females have a blue crown, green back, and copper-bronze coverts and tail, with mostly whitish undersides featuring blue-green flecks on the throat and neck.

mp: Males have red and brown fore-crowns and red malar stripes.
fp: Females have black fore-crowns spotted white and mottled black and white malar stripes.

mp: The male has a bright yellow underside and nape, olive-green back and wings, a black head and chest-band, and a white throat.
fp: Females are overall dull brownish-grey, though some have yellowish undertail coverts.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with a bright golden-yellow forecrown, orange-red hindcrown patch, golden-yellow throat, and entirely yellow wings and tail feathers.
fp: Adult females are mostly olive-green with a yellow-olive throat, belly, and wing linings, lacking the male's showy forecrown feathers.

mp: The male has conspicuous metallic reddish-copper body feathers in breeding condition, brownish-black underparts, and long central tail feathers.
fp: The female is olive above and yellowish below, with yellow-edged feathers in the wings and tail.

mp: Male sunbirds have bright green feathers, a blue and black tail, and a yellow and red chest.
fp: Female Gorgeous Sunbirds are mainly brown with a pale yellowish stripe behind the eye and a light yellow belly.

mp: The male has a glittering rose to violet throat and upper breast gorget with a white pectoral band below it.
fp: The female has a dark gray-brown chin with white feather fringes and occasionally some glittering rosy feathers.

mp: The nominate male is mostly dark metallic blue-green with a pinkish purple gorget, grayish line behind the eye, grayish breast, and white spots on the flanks.
fp: The nominate female has bronzy green upperparts with a rufous rump, cinnamon-rufous underparts, and a rounded cinnamon tail with a black bar near the end.

mp: Adult males have a mostly velvety black head with a green forehead, golden green upperparts, and an orange upper breast collar.
fp: Adult females have a lighter black head with golden-green spots, a rufous collar, and a lower belly with a rufous wash and large golden green spots.

mp: Adult males have a black head, nape, chin, throat, and belly, with green upperparts, a yellow neck band, green tail with chestnut tips, yellow flanks, and red undertail coverts.
fp: Females have a shorter bill, paler skin around the eye, and chestnut plumage where the male has black.

mp: The male has a purple chest and is brightly coloured with black, green, yellow, and red markings.
fp: The female has a lighter mauve chest and tends to be less brightly coloured than the male.

mp: Adult males have a black face and throat with a pale blue eye ring, metallic green crown, back, and rump, and black and white patterned flight feathers and tail.
Slightly smaller than the Tenerife blue chaffinch with two white bands in the wings, a whiter belly, and less blue shades.
fp: A dull grey-brown.

mp: The male is overall glossy black with a white stripe along the front edge of the folded wing.
fp: The female is a lighter olive grey with a white stripe along the front edge of the folded wing.

mp: Males have a red forehead and a grey crest.
fp: Females have a grey forehead and a grey crest.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely bluish gray with lighter underparts, white-tipped wing coverts, a black bar above them, and a black center throat and upper breast.
fp: Adult females have olive-tinged gray upperparts, somewhat darker wings, a buff throat, and rich olive-buff underparts.

mp: The male has a grey crown, white supercilium, large black mask, medium grey upper parts, white rump, blackish wings with a white patch, and a long tail with a white base and black tip.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has patches of chestnut on the flanks that are visible during display and when preening.

mp: Males have a slate grey back and chest, a white chin and belly, and rufous flanks.
fp: Females have grey or brown backs with dark spots on the chest and similar plumage to males on the belly and flanks.

mp: The male has a blue throat, a deeply forked tail, and upperparts that are bronzy-green with orangeish tips on the long green tail feathers.
fp: The female has a shorter tail than the male, upperparts that are bronzy-green with orangeish tips on the green tail feathers, and grey underparts.

mp: Adults are mainly grey with a white lower belly and undertail, and a white patch on the wings.
fp: Some females are dark-barred reddish brown above with an unbarred tail and have strongly dark-barred whitish underparts.

mp: Glossy blue-black with a grey-brown throat, breast, and sides contrasting with white lower underparts.
fp: Duller than the male with a paler throat.

mp: The male has a gray head, neck, and upper breast with a white throat bordered in black, cinnamon buff vermiculate upperparts, and a white lower breast and belly.
fp: The female has a pale buff head and breast with heavy dark streaks.

mp: It has a dark grey crown with a red nape.
fp: It has a dark grey crown without a red nape.

mp: The adult male has a dark grey head and mantle, a pale grey chin, an orange-yellow throat, blackish wings, and orange underparts, lower back, and greater covert tips.
fp: In the female, the throat, underparts, lower back, and greater covert tips are bright yellow instead of orange.

mp: Adult males have a glossy black crown, light gray face and underparts, black back and wings with white markings, and a gray collar.
fp: Adult females have a blackish brown to glossy blackish crown, a pale cinnamon to tawny-buff face, and a collar of the same color.

mp: The male has a brighter and more extensive red on the face and brighter yellow on the wing.
fp: The female has less red on the face and duller yellow on the wing compared to the male.

mp: Adult males have a light gray crown and nape, pale brownish buff lores, a wide red stripe below the buff, and a dull white chin.
fp: Adult females have no red on their head and otherwise share the same plumage as males.

mp: Adult males have a mostly olive-gray head with a gray crown, black lores, white eye crescents, grayish olive-brown upperparts, and yellow throat, breast, and undertail coverts.
fp: Females have grayish lores, yellowish white eye crescents, a brownish olive wash on the head, and upper- and underparts like the male's.

mp: Males have a dark grey loreal patch and are a slightly darker shade of grey.
fp: Females have grey loreal patches and are a slightly lighter shade of grey.

mp: The male has a reddish mantle.
fp: The female has a green mantle.

mp: The adult male has a grayish white forehead darkening to gray on the head, a medium gray throat darkening on the breast with gossy purple sides, cream belly, rous vent, glossy purple shoulders, bluish purple lower back and rump, and a gray tail.
fp: The adult female is very similar to the male but duller in coloration.

mp: The adult male is similarly colored to the female but has an entire head and upper chest that are pale grey.
fp: The adult female is entirely green, with a dark green back and wings, a bright green rump, and a paler green chest.

mp: The male has a grey head with a red forecrown, a black line across the lores, a narrow black moustache stripe, green back and wing coverts, and pale grey breast and underbody.
fp: The female lacks the red forecrown but has fine black streaks on the crown, while otherwise sharing similar plumage features.

mp: The male has a distinctive white eye-ring contrasting with a grey hood, whitish pink chin and throat bordered by grey malar stripes, and pinkish brown underparts.
fp: The female is duller than the male, though her moustachial stripe can appear more noticeable.

mp: Adult males have a distinct dark grey throat and chest contrasting with a white belly, and dull orange-red or chestnut-colored ear coverts.
fp: Adult females lack the dull orange-red or chestnut coloration on the ear coverts.

mp: The male has rufescent-olive upperparts, including the crown and ear-coverts, and grey underparts becoming paler on the belly and vent.
fp: The female has a white throat and whiter centre to the breast and belly, some dark spots or streaks on the sides of the throat and upper breast and warm brownish fringes to the breast feathers.

mp: The adult male has a gray head, back, wings, and tail with a white supercilium, rose-red breast and vent, gray flanks, and white underparts.
fp: The female has a duller gray crown, nape, and upperparts, with a buff supercilium, face, breast, flanks, and vent area, and a white throat and belly.

mp: Males are black with faint pale fringes on the belly and a broad grey patch on the wing feathers.
fp: Females are plain brown with only a hint of paler brown on the wings.

mp: Adult males have a black head extending below the eye, mostly black upperparts with a hidden white patch, black wings with large white spots, and white underparts with a gray tinge on the flanks.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crown and browner lores and ear coverts.

mp: One of the largest pheasants with very long tail feathers and huge, broad secondary wing feathers decorated with large eyespots.
fp: Smaller and duller than males, with shorter tails and fewer eyespots.

mp: The male is deep sandy buff coloured with a black cap, crested crown, and a black breast band during the breeding season.
fp: The female is smaller than the male, with head and neck that are not pure white, and a rudimentary, broken, or absent breast band.

mp: The adult male has a bright metallic green chin, cheeks, and upper region with gold overtones, a white lower throat, and a deep rufous lower region.
fp: The female resembles the male but lacks the white spot on the throat.

mp: Males have dark shining blue-green upperparts, mostly shining blue wings, greenish black tail, and blue-green underparts.
fp: Females have mostly dark metallic green upperparts, dusky gray crown, blue wing coverts, dusky wings, and cinnamon underparts.

mp: Adult males have more strongly coloured legs and eye rings compared to females.
fp: Adult females have less strongly coloured legs and eye rings compared to males.

mp: The male is highly colourful with a profusion of yellow tail feathers, an iridescent-green face, iridescent yellow-and-silver crown, head, and nape, and maroon-brown body plumage.
fp: The female has unbarred, richly-hued maroon-brown plumage and is smaller than the male.

mp: The adult male always has a red crown.
fp: Females have a crown color varying between subspecies, such as black spotted with white, yellow, or brown with lighter dots.

mp: Has a black throat patch without a yellow border.
fp: Has a yellow throat and eye ring.

mp: The male has a black throat, pink bill, dark grey-brown upperparts, white underparts, whitish streaked wings, and a yellow shoulder patch.
fp: The female is duller, has a blackish bill, and a black throat.

mp: The male is black with an iridescent green crown, blue-green breast cover, and a long velvety black erectile cape covering his back.
fp: The female is a reddish-brown bird with brownish-barred buff below.

mp: The male is much paler and less uniform with barring on the scapulars and wing-coverts.
fp: The female has a black head with a buff stripe and a white eye-patch, dark rufous neck, and dark bronze-green upperparts finely barred with black.

mp: Adult males have orange comb-like feathers over their eyes, dark elongated head feathers, and a circular, un-feathered orange neck patch that can be inflated.
fp: Adult females have shorter head feathers and lack the male's yellow comb and orange neck patch.

mp: The adult male has a yellow patch over each eye, is grayish on top with a white breast, and has a dark brown throat and a black belly.
fp: The adult female is mottled gray-brown with a light brown throat and dark belly.

mp: Breeding males have sandy buff backs, white underparts, variably orange breast, forehead and nape in summer, and a black eye mask in summer.
fp: The female is duller and greyer compared to the male.

mp: The adult male has a grey head and a white throat.
fp: The female lacks the grey head, and the throat is duller.

mp: Adult males have a blackish green head and upper breast with a yellow collar, green upperparts, and yellow underparts with black streaks.
fp: Females have a green head instead of the male's black and lack the yellow collar.

mp: Adult males have glossy green upperparts with a pale yellowish collar, white-tipped upperwing coverts, small white spots on secondaries, tertials, and tail, a yellow-buff chin, buffy rufous throat, and rich dark rufous underparts.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have a wide band of green with white speckles across their upper breast and more pale underparts.

mp: Males have black crowns.
fp: Females have reddish brown crowns.

mp: The male has green above, yellow below, black and white bars on the flank, and a reddish bill.
fp: The female is slightly paler than the male.

mp: Adult males have a glossy black crown, whitish lores, thin yellowish eye-ring, pale gray face and nape, bright olive upperparts, whitish throat, bright yellow to olive yellow breast, and grayish white underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dull olive crown, grayish lores, grayer face, pale olive upperparts with rufous-chestnut wing coverts, muted yellow breast, and dusky underparts.

mp: Adult males have an iridescent red-yellow crown, larger size, and shorter bills.
fp: Adult females are smaller with longer bills and lack the male's red-yellow crown.

mp: The male has a dark blue head and upper breast, a green back, orange-yellow lower underparts, black wings vermiculated with white, and a black-and-white undertail.
fp: The female is duller with a grey back, head, and breast, and distinct black-and-white barring mainly on the outer webs of each tail feather.

mp: The male has an olive-blackish crown with indistinct reddish colour and a red nape.
fp: The female lacks red on the head and has buff spots on its crown and nape.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead and forecrown, a red hindcrown and nape, and a red malar stripe below white lores.
fp: Adult females have red only on the hindcrown and nape, with a black malar stripe streaked with white.

mp: The adult male has a long white crest, a mostly dark brown to black face with a white collar, bronzy upperparts, and a thin glittering green gorget with white edges that forms a beard.
fp: The adult female lacks the crest and beard, and its underparts are buffy white with some greenish mottling.

mp: Adult males have a dull golden-green head and back, olive green to brownish rump, dark purple brown wings, deep blue to violet blue tail, and dark shining green underparts.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have white fringes on the throat feathers and bronze or brownish edges to the tail feathers.

mp: Adult males have a metallic bronze green crown, nape, and upperparts, with a velvety black stripe down the chin, throat, and chest bordered by metallic bluish green.
fp: Nominate females have less bronzy metallic green on the crown, nape, and upperparts than males, while sharing similar tail feather coloration.

mp: Adult males have mostly metallic grass green underparts with white or grayish white feather margins, a white lower belly and vent area, and white leg tufts.
fp: Adult females have a buff chin and throat and gray underparts.

mp: The bird is about 17 cm long, plumaged in brilliant green with a black ear patch, widely gaped bill, rounded head, short tail and three black bars on each wing.
fp: The female is duller and has no black markings on its ear patch and wing coverts.

mp: The male has a blue crown, blue wings and tail with a broad black band on the tail.
fp: The female has a more greenish body with some rusty spots on the wing coverts and yellowish brown secondaries with narrow blue edging.

mp: Adult males have a glittering green to blue-green head and breast with a metallic violet-blue throat patch, bronzy green upperparts, and a blue-black tail.
fp: Adult females have a non-shiny blue-green head, a short white malar stripe, whitish underparts heavily spotted with green, and a black tail with white-tipped outer feathers.

mp: Adult males have a shaggy, mostly iridescent green crest with purplish black longest feathers, a gray face with a white spot behind the eye, shining bronze-green upperparts, and a violet-blue chin to upper belly.
fp: Adult females have a smaller crest, shining green upperparts, and gray underparts.

mp: Adult males have a glittering bluish green crown, emerald to bronze green nape and back, and a pure white underside with emerald to bronze green sides.
fp: Adult females are similar but have a dark green crown and a bronze green to golden green tail.

mp: It has a greenish or bluish head, black on the back, and a contrastingly colored, orange or red rump.
fp: Females have similar, though duller coloration.

mp: Mainly dark green with a blue-green rump, dark eye mask, buff stripes, and short white-tipped central tail feathers.
fp: Sooty gray below with an even longer bill and a much longer tail than the male.

mp: Adult males are mostly grass green with a wide white collar across the upper breast, white outer tail feathers with green tips, and brownish wings.
fp: Females are mostly grass green above with a smaller white collar, a rusty throat with green spots, and grayish underparts with green mottling and spots.

mp: The male has black lores, bright yellow eyelids, dark olive face and upperparts, black wings with white wing-bars, and a yellow centre belly.
fp: The female has yellow lores, a complete eye-ring, medium olive upperparts, wings washed olive with yellow wing-bars, and olive green underparts.

mp: Adults have emerald green upperparts, metallic blue-green underparts, and a metallic blue-black tail with white tips.
fp: Females are similar to males but have a tiny white spot behind the eye.

mp: Adult males are mostly yellowish olive with a crest of long feathers on their nape, pink to dull orange lores, dusky olive wings, and chestnut rump and belly.
fp: Adult females lack the crest but are otherwise like males, being mostly yellowish olive with pink to dull orange lores, dusky olive wings, and chestnut rump and belly.

mp: The male is 1.8–3 m in total length, including a train measuring 1.4–1.6 m, and has a wingspan averaging 1.2 m.
fp: The adult female is around half the total length of the breeding male at 1–1.1 m in length.

mp: The breeding male has a predominantly dark green back and neck, a dark gray crown, white cheeks, and pale grey and white scalloped underparts.
fp: The female has a barred rather than green neck but otherwise resembles the non-breeding male.

mp: The adult male has a yellow head and underparts with blue cheeks and a red band on the forehead, and is heavier with a larger bill than the female.
fp: The female has duller yellow plumage and more prominent red markings, as well as a smaller beak and lower weight than the male.

mp: Males have purplish-blue primaries, secondaries, and coverts, with bright turquoise feathers on the leading edges of their wings.
fp: Females lack blue but have more yellow-green on the head.

mp: Overall shining green with a rounded green tail where all but the central pair of feathers have white at their base, and a dusky gray area around the eye with a white spot behind it.
fp: Smaller than the male, with a whitish throat and breast thickly spotted with green, and outermost tail feathers with white tips.

mp: The adult male has a dark green crown, metallic green back, coppery bronze rump, and a deeply forked bluish black tail.
fp: The adult female has upperparts like the male but with a darker rump and a notched, non-elongated tail.

mp: The male has a bright green back, a bright green gorget with a usually inapparent blue border, a black belly, a green vent area, and a dark blue tail.
fp: The female has a duller bright green back, a bright green gorget, a black belly, a green vent area, a dark blue tail, and a longer, more strongly curved bill than the male.

mp: Adult males have a small bright yellow forehead patch, blackish lores, glossy dark greenish blue head and upperparts, and bright yellow lower throat to undertail coverts.
fp: Adult females have an olive crown, nape, upperparts, wings, and tail, with pale gray face, neck sides, and underparts, and olive-yellow chin, flanks, and undertail coverts.

mp: The male has glossy bronzy-green upperparts, green throat and underparts with a black central line, and shiny purple tail feathers with dark blue tips.
fp: The female has bronzy-green upperparts with a reddish tinge, white underparts with a black central stripe, and tail feathers with white tips.

mp: Adult males have green upperparts with a bronzy rump, a white throat with bluish green spots, a white breast, and a grayish belly with green spots on the sides.
fp: Adult females have emerald green upperparts and an unspotted white throat, but are otherwise like the male.
