mp: Adult males are mostly dull black with a white forehead and forecrown, a whitish rump, and a grayish black belly.
fp: Adult females are paler and grayer than males, with a darker crown, grayer rump, and a belly mottled with white.

mp: Adult breeding males are almost entirely black with orange and white shoulders, long wide tails, and a bluish white bill.
fp: Females are inconspicuous with feathers streaked tawny and black, pale patches on the chest and back, narrow tail feathers, and horn-coloured bills.

mp: The male has extremely long outer tail feathers with a broad white edge, while its upperparts are brown with spots and bars of grayish brown, tawny, buff, and cinnamon.
fp: The female has a much shorter, darker tail, while its upperparts are similarly brown with spots and bars of grayish brown, tawny, buff, and cinnamon.

mp: The male is 40–42 cm tall with a large erectile head crest of 20–30 cm and a large throat wattle of feathers, and generally has black colored shafts in its feathers.
fp: The female is slightly smaller at 35–37 cm, has a shorter head crest, and lacks or has a much smaller throat wattle.

mp: The adult male has a narrow glittering blue-green frontlet, dusky crown, dark bronzy green upperparts, a glittering rosy throat and upper breast gorget with a white pectoral band, and dusky buff underparts with round green spots.
fp: The female has dull brown throat feathers with rufous or bronze green inclusions and a belly with less spotting than the male's.

mp: Adult males have rich bright blue upperparts, black wings with blue or greenish blue edges, a black tail with greenish blue edges, a glossy purplish black face, dark purple chin and throat, and a rich bright blue lower breast with a purple belly patch.
fp: Adult females have mostly dark grayish brown upperparts with whitish feather tips.

mp: Adult males have pale gray head and upperparts, whitish underparts, a white eyering, a small pointed bill, a rufous rump, and a small rusty patch on their crown.
fp: Females have pale gray head and upperparts, whitish underparts, a white eyering, a small pointed bill, and a rufous rump.

mp: Adult males have a grey-brown face and front neck, a white back of the neck and face, and a dull orange nape.
fp: Females are smaller with slightly lighter coloured front neck and face compared to adult males.

mp: Males are larger and have a more pronounced red patch on the chest.
fp: Females have a slightly duller red patch on the chest.

mp: Male has pale underparts and head with a black cheek.
fp: Female is entirely black.

mp: The breeding male has a cobalt blue bill, completely black head and throat, chestnut breast and back, and greyish-brown underparts.
fp: The female is less colourful with a greyish-black bill, light brown face, dark crown and cheek stripe, and off-white throat.

mp: The adult male has a greyish-black head and mantle, a white supercilium, white scapulars and black wings, with a black tail with white margins and white underparts.
fp: The female is similar to the male except for having rufous patches on the flanks.

mp: Adult males are bright blue with a black line through the eye, black tail and wing edges, and bright white underparts and throat.
fp: Females are slightly duller, with off-white underparts featuring a pale orange or light buffy wash and wings tinged greenish.

mp: The male has a light brown head with black and white streaking, a greyish-brown back and wings with fine dark barring, and a cinnamon-buff breast with dark barring.
fp: The female is more brightly coloured, with a blackish head, a chequer-board effect on the mantle, and a white moustachial stripe above a black bib on the chin and upper throat.

mp: The male has a crest that is mainly orange.
fp: The female has a crest that is yellow.

mp: Adult males have a metallic purple gorget, a green breast and flanks, and a rufous belly with a white or buffy patch on either side of the rump.
fp: Females have a buffy throat and a green breast and flanks with some rufous mixed in.

mp: Velvet-black with elongated black filamental flank plumes, an iridescent blue-green crown, and a wide, triangle-shaped breast shield.
fp: Brownish with dark spots and buff bars below with a white brow.

mp: Males have a reddish bill with a yellow tip.
fp: Females have a plain yellow bill with black at the base of the lower mandible and a black stripe along the culmen.

mp: The male has a bluish-green lower edge to the black collar and a red upper mandible with a white tip.
fp: The female has an all black bill and only the black collar.

mp: The male has a slaty-black head and breast with a white border on the black bib separating it from the crimson underside, olive-brown to chestnut back, and black wing coverts with fine white vermiculations.
fp: The female lacks contrasting black and crimson, having a slightly darker head and breast shading into olive-brown on the back, with the male's crimson underside replaced by ochre.

mp: The breeding male is 25 cm long with very long central tail feathers, metallic green upperparts, blackish-green wings with small yellow pectoral patches, and yellow underparts flecked with green in eclipse plumage.
fp: The female is 15 cm long with brown upperparts, dull yellow underparts with indistinct streaking on the breast, and a square-ended tail.

mp: Males have long tail plumes that can add up to 18 cm to their overall length.
fp: The female is largely rufous-orange with a black head and nape, black flight feathers with rufous edges, and a thin, light blue eyelid wattle.

mp: A medium-sized pheasant with a peacock-like dark crest, bluish black plumage, reddish brown rump, black outer tail feathers, red iris, and bare blue facial skin.
fp: A brown bird with a short crest, blue facial skin, and spotted black-and-white below.

mp: Males have deeper blue lores and a longer crest compared to females during the breeding season.
fp: Females have bluish-green lores when they first appear in breeding areas and a shorter crest than males.

mp: The adult male has mottled olive brown coloration, a gray breast, a black head with white bands, red eye surrounds, and red legs.
fp: The adult female is slightly smaller and possesses duller coloration on the head and legs compared to the male.

mp: Males have a variable broad blue band across their chest on a white underbelly.
fp: Females have dull reddish-brown underparts and lack the distinctive breast band of the males.

mp: The male has a blue throat.
fp: The female has a whitish throat.

mp: The male has a thin black band around the neck.
fp: The female has a thin brown band around the neck.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black head, throat, and neck with bare blue-green to green skin around the eye and a chestnut patch behind it.
fp: Adult females have little or no chestnut behind the eye and their black breast band is usually wider than the male's.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with a slight crest, a partly hidden red patch, a large golden supercilium, glossy blue to black lores, ochraceous nape, bright moss-green back and rump, black wings with white edges, mostly black tail, white upper throat, bright yellow breast and belly with a wide black bar, and bright red to orange-red crissum.
The adult male has a grayish white forehead, face, and chin, with a dark purple breast changing to gray on the belly and blue-gray upperparts.
fp: The adult female is brown overall with a cinnamon face, and its darker wing bars are not as distinct.

mp: The adult male is glossy crimson-maroon with a black head, neck, and wings, and a chestnut-maroon tail.
fp: The female has a greyish-white underpart with black streaks and slightly darker bodies than the male.

mp: Males are generally paler than females.
fp: Females are generally darker than males.

mp: Males have a bright white throat, grey crown, and chestnut belly.
fp: Females resemble other brown female seedeaters.

mp: Males have mostly green upperparts with a blue crest, a glossy blue-green gorget, white underparts with a black line, and two outer tail feathers ending in large purplish black racquets.
fp: Females are green above but lack a crest or gorget, and their outer tail feathers are shorter than the male's and do not have racquets.

mp: The male has a black head with a grey neck-band, throat, breast and belly, chestnut upperparts and tail, black-tipped wings, and a bright blue bill.
fp: The female is smaller than the male, with a paler bill and a dark-grey head.

mp: Breeding adult males have a rust-colored body with a black face and mottled wings.
fp: Adult females have a barred brownish gray body, with two horizontal, dark-colored stripes running through the buff-colored face.

mp: The adult male is deep ultramarine blue with a dark mask, a large black upturned beak with a hook, and bright red iris.
fp: The female is similar in appearance but altogether duller than the male.

mp: The male has mainly black upperparts, white crown, forehead, supercilium, large white patches on shoulders and wings, white throat and underparts, and orange flanks and breast.
fp: The female is a duller version of the male, with brownish black upperparts and a grey or buff tone to the shoulders and underparts.

mp: The male has glossy green, reddish-bronze, or golden-green upperparts and head, a red belly and lower breast separated by a narrow white band, and a distinct red or orange eye-ring.
fp: The female is brown above with a pinkish to red belly and breast, often with a narrow or obscured white band, and has a partial white eye-ring.

mp: Adult males have a sharply defined black face mask with a pale edge covering the lores, ear coverts, chin and throat, with dark blue grey upperparts and pale grey underbody.
fp: Adult females are similar to adult males but slightly browner and have an indistinct mask.

mp: Adult males have a wide black mask, pale slate-gray crown, yellow-olive upperparts, and bright yellow throat and underparts.
fp: Females lack black or gray on their head, have dull yellow around the eye, and duller, browner upperparts with more subdued underparts.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely black with white edges on outer scapulars, a white interscapular patch, and white tips on wing coverts and tail feathers.
fp: Females have an olive-grey head and upperparts with a white interscapular patch, dark gray wings and tail with white tips, and pale olive-gray underparts.

mp: The breeding male is almost purely white, with only small areas of black on the wingtips and tail.
fp: The breeding female has a streaked back.

mp: The male's plumage is solid black, with white tips to the undertail coverts.
fp: The female's plumage is brown and streaky.

mp: Males have white throats and cheeks.
fp: Females are washed with grey on the throat and cheeks.

mp: The male has a white line behind the eye, a pink-purple throat with a white band below, dull green underparts, and a long deeply forked tail with green inner feathers and black outer feathers.
fp: The female has a whitish face with a blackish stripe behind the eye, whitish throat, chest and belly with cinnamon tinges on the sides, and a shorter forked tail.

mp: The male's outermost three pairs of tail feathers have broad white tips.
fp: The female's outermost three pairs of tail feathers have narrower and buffy tips.

mp: Males have a straight black bill, mostly green body, dull green chest, blue-black forked tail, and an indigo crown.
fp: Females are mostly green with darker green tail and wings, a light gray chest, a white spot behind the eyes, and green disks on the chest sides.

mp: Dark with blue or violet iridescence, white stripes on wings and tail, and long striped tail feathers.
fp: Brown and speckled with brown and white quills.

mp: The male is glossy blue-black above, with a red chest, a slight red under-tail, and a black centre stripe running down its white belly.
fp: The female is dark grey above, with a white throat, light grey underparts, and just a touch of pinkish-red under the tail.

mp: The male has glossy black plumage with a chestnut belly, vent, and rump, and white shoulder patches.
fp: The female is dark grey with a chestnut lower breast, belly, and vent.

mp: Males are mostly bright green with bright red underwings, blue primaries, and a yellow beak.
fp: Females are predominantly bright red with a royal blue underbelly and a black beak.

mp: Males have a pink flush to their face and underparts, with extensive white and pink areas in the wings.
fp: Females have fainter, almost unnoticeable pink.

mp: Adult males have overall pale grey plumage contrasting with black wingtips, black bands along the secondaries, and rusty streaks on the belly and flanks.
fp: Adult females have pale yellow-brown underparts with longitudinal stripes and spotted wing coverts, and uniform dark brown upper parts with a white rump.

mp: A medium-sized bird with a white belly, black back, white spots on the wings, white secondary flight feathers, and white outer tail feathers.
fp: Smaller than males and recognizable by their turquoise facial skin.

mp: A white and black bird with variable body plumage from pale grey to almost black, always featuring a white rump, outer tail feathers, and a white shoulder patch.
fp: Entirely dark brown apart from the white rump and outer tail feathers.

mp: The adult male has a red crown and nape, with yellowish-green upper parts, a red rump, dark brown wings and tail, and pale grey underparts.
fp: The adult female has a plain grey head lacking the red crown, with yellowish-green upper parts, a red rump, dark brown wings and tail, and pale grey underparts.

mp: Males have a rufous head and underparts, greenish-blue upperparts, black loral and nape patches, and a dark blue tail.
fp: Females have a black crown, paler underparts, and neck patches that join at the nape to form a bar across the back of the neck.

mp: The male has metallic blue ocelli on upperparts, green ocelli on its twenty-feather tail, and two spurs on its legs.
fp: The female is smaller and duller, with black ocelli on upperparts, unspurred legs, and an eighteen-feather tail.

mp: The adult male is metallic green on the crown, nape, upperparts and chest, with a bright red belly and vent separated by a narrow white band.
fp: The female is warm brown on the head, upperparts and chest, separated from its paler brown lower chest and red belly and vent by a narrow white band.

mp: Adult males have a wide black moustache, black streak through the eye, white cheeks, black upperparts with thin white streaks, a white patch between the shoulders, and yellow underparts with sparse black streaks.
fp: Adult females have buff to tawny buff streaks on the crown and lack the white patch between the shoulders.

mp: The adult male is drab brown above with white to buffy spots on the back and wing coverts, has a rufous chin, throat, and breast with indistinct darker streaks, and a white belly.
fp: The adult female is grayer above with heavier buff markings and has a paler breast with heavier streaks.

mp: The male has a deep violet forehead, crown, supercilium, and throat, with bright red to deep scarlet nape, mantle, and sides, plus bright blue tail coverts.
fp: The female is dull in colour, covered by deep olive green on the dorsal side and greyish-yellow on the ventral side.

mp: The male has a long greyish white, barred black and brown tail.
fp: The female is a chestnut brown bird with whitish throat, buff colour belly and white-tipped tail.

mp: The male is multicolored, bright green overall with a bluish neck, yellow forehead, red patch on the back of the head, and yellowish-orange thighs.
Males have a yellow crown, face, mantle, and throat; chestnut and black ear coverts; bright green nape and wings; blue rump, breast, and belly; and a black patch in the center of the underparts.
fp: Females are duller and lack the yellow mantle and black patch on the underparts.

mp: The adult male has a yellow and red beak and a black face, throat and breast.
fp: The adult female lacks the black and has a red-based grey bill.

mp: The male has an orangish buff head, throat and chest delineated by a conspicuous narrow band of white and dark brown.
fp: The female is more cryptic, being generally various shades of brown patterned with white specks.

mp: Males in full breeding plumage have a black crown and mantle, bright orange throat, orange-yellow eyebrow, black wings with a white patch, orange-yellow rump, and black tail.
fp: Females are completely dissimilar, with generally buff-brown coloration, rusty-colored wings, and a two-toned eyering.

mp: The male has a rufous head and neck, a black body and upper parts glossed with green.
fp: Females are all black.

mp: The male has bright red underside plumage and bare, green gape and eye flanges.
fp: The female has brown face and chest plumage, blue skin orbiting the eyes and duller red plumage below.

mp: Adult males have a gray head fading into a greenish back and wings, a white belly, a yellow throat and breast, a complete white eye ring, and a rusty brown patch on their crown.
fp: Females have a duller olive-grey head, less bold yellow on their throat, and lack the male's rusty brown crown patch.

mp: Males have a fiery orange neck patch, a crimson red crown, a muted orange vent, and a red breast patch bordered with a black stripe.
fp: Females are duller, though they can sometimes have a pale orange neck and breast patch.

mp: Breeding males have a black bill and head, yellow collar, grey belly, chestnut-brown lower tail coverts, olive back, and blackish flight feathers edged greenish.
fp: Breeding females have a yellow front of the head, olive green back, and a broad yellow eyebrow.

mp: The male has mostly white plumage with blue wings and tail, a turquoise crown, and a thick black stripe through the eye.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has blue on the lower back.

mp: The male was darker than the female.
fp: The female was lighter than the male.

mp: The male has dark black-brown plumage with a striking yellow eye and a dark coloured (greenish) head.
fp: The female has duller chocolate brown plumage, brown eyes and has a white face patch during breeding season.

mp: It has a red upper mandible.
fp: It has a black upper mandible and a higher presence of blue hinted facial feathers.

mp: Adult males have a larger bill knob, longer hackles, and greener underparts compared to females.
fp: Adult females have a smaller bill knob, shorter hackles, and browner underparts.

mp: It is dark steely indigo blue with some violet-blue on the forehead and darker lores.
fp: The female is duller with dark brown on the upperparts and dark grey below.

mp: The male has a paler grey crown.
fp: The female has a darker grey crown with a pale throat.

mp: The adult male has black upperparts with a white forehead spot, white wing bars, and a bright red breast with a white lower belly.
fp: The female is much duller, mainly brown with a pinkish breast.

mp: Males have darker plumage than females and are slightly larger.
fp: Females have lighter plumage than males and are slightly smaller.

mp: Adult males have white underparts, black upperparts, a white 'V' on the back, a long black tail with white outer feathers and tips, and black bill, eyes, and legs.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but are distinguished by having a rufous lower flank.

mp: The male has darker grey plumage compared to the hen harrier.
fp: The female has lighter plumage than the male.

mp: Breeding males display bright reddish-orange plumage with contrasting black on the crown, forehead, flank, and belly, while tail and upper wings are brown.
Adult males have a red patch above the bill.
fp: Adult females lack the red patch above the bill.

mp: The breeding drake has an iridescent, dark green head, white breast, and chestnut belly and flanks.
fp: The female is a dull, mottled brown with a long, broad bill grey tinged with orange on the cutting edge.

mp: Adult males have a gray forehead, black crown, gray back with black feather tips, and slaty gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a tawny crown, yellowish olive-brown upperparts, and dark brown wings with white spots.

mp: Males have red facial markings, specifically burgundy markings over their entire face.
fp: Females lack the red facial markings found on males.

mp: Adult males have a white supercilium, smoky brown crown and upperparts, black wings with white bars and dots, black tail with white tips, and black face, throat, and underparts.
fp: Adult females have upperparts like the male's, a grayish face, dirty white to buff underparts with variable dusky streaks and mottling on the breast.

mp: Male breeding plumage features distinct breast and head coloration, which young males soon acquire.
fp: Females are somewhat duller than males, most notably on the head, with greenish-yellow uppersides and duller yellow below.

mp: The male has a red crown and nape and a reddish streak on the cheek.
fp: The female has a black crown speckled with white, a red nape, and a dark cheek stripe with white speckling.

mp: The male is rich yellow below, sharply contrasted with greenish upper parts.
fp: Females are duller and have two prominent wing-bars.

mp: The adult male has a black and white harlequin face pattern, a buffy brown to olive brown crown with a tawny crest, and gray and brown upperparts with cinnamon stripes and black spots.
fp: The female has a buffy and black face, a tawny crest, brown upperparts with buff lines, and a wine red breast and belly with black bars and spots.

mp: Adult males have a black cap with red tips on the forehead feathers and small white spots on the rest of the cap.
fp: Adult females are identical to males but lack red on the forehead.

mp: Adult males have a black crown, long white supercilium, black eye band, white speckled cheeks, gray back, light rufous rump, and white throat and breast with black streaks.
fp: Females have a buff-streaked crown, olive-gray back, and duller buffier underparts that are less heavily streaked than the male's.

mp: Adult males have a dark back, chestnut upperparts, and are striped black and buff on the breast and sides.
fp: Females have a buffy submoustachial and throat, black malar stripes, and a dark brown crown with pale streaking.

mp: Adult males have a mostly olive head, olive green upperparts, brown wings with olive edges, and olive underparts with thin white streaks.
fp: Adult females are much more brownish than males and have little or no crest on the crown.

mp: Adult males have a wide black mask around the eye, olive-green head and upperparts, and yellow throat and underparts with an olive wash on the flanks.
fp: Adult females lack black on their face, have a mostly olive-green head with a thin yellowish supercilium, and upper- and underparts similar to the male's.

mp: Adult males have long nape feathers forming a crest, a blackish brown head and neck, chestnut mantle and underparts, and black wings with chestnut edges.
fp: Females lack the crest, are smaller, and have somewhat duller plumage compared to males.

mp: The male has a grey body with olive-green wings, two white wing bars, a tawny-orange head and breast, and a black patch through the eye.
fp: The female has yellow instead of orange on the head and breast, and a more diffuse black mask.

mp: The male has a dark grey head, pale grey breast, and red-tinged buff belly and rump.
fp: The female lacks the red tinge and has brown underparts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly dark slaty gray head and upperparts with lighter rump, dark slaty gray wings and tail, and somewhat paler gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a rufous-chestnut to rufous tawny crown, upperparts, and tail, with cinnamon-edged wings and buffy cinnamon underparts.

mp: Adult males have a deep yellow forehead, glossy blackish head and nape, glossy blue-black upperparts, and yellow underparts.
fp: Adult females have an olive-yellow forecrown, olive mid-crown, gray hindcrown and nape, olive face, and mostly olive upperparts.

mp: Male has slaty-blue upperparts with a large triangular orange patch on the mantle, lighter greyish blue upper-breast and throat, and a gradient from fiery orange to yellow on the lower breast to vent.
fp: Female is much duller, mostly drab olive brown overall, except for a pale orange rump and yellow belly.

mp: The adult male has bright grass-green upper parts, yellow underparts, and an orange belly patch.
fp: The adult female is duller green in colour.

mp: The male has a glossy black head and bib, an orange throat and breast, and a yellow belly with green mottling.
fp: The female lacks the dark head, having green upper parts and green and yellow streaked underparts.

mp: The male has a pinkish or lilac band on the upper breast with a broader orange one below.
fp: The female has a bright yellow breast and lacks the orange or lilac bands.

mp: The male has a bright metallic green head, throat, and mantle, with a metallic violet upper breast, bright orange lower breast fading to yellow on the belly, and a long blackish tail.
fp: The female has olive-greenish grey upperparts and olive yellowish underparts that are paler on the belly, with blackish wings and tail.

mp: Males have a dull olive-yellow head, rufous-chestnut upperparts, a yellow-orange lower breast, and a blue eye ring.
fp: Females have a grey-brown head and upperparts, with a grey breast that has yellow at the belly and vent.

mp: Male feathers are mostly a deep, warm, cadmium yellow with an orange overtone, strongest on the crown and breast, with black lores and throat, golden orange rump, and tail finely tipped with white.
fp: Female chats are mottled in grey-brown with underparts being a softer fawny yellow.

mp: Males usually have brighter orange patches on the abdomen.

The adult male has a black crown, wings, and tail with a black band across the midback, while the rest of the head, neck, breast, and upper back are orange, the rump is olive-green, and the belly is bright yellow.
fp: Females are olive-green with yellow underparts.

mp: Adult males have a deep orange-yellow crown, glossy blue-black head and upperparts with a purplish tinge, and deep orange ochraceous underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dark olive head and upperparts, with olive-yellow underparts that are paler and yellower on the throat, belly, and undertail coverts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly grayish olive head with an often hidden orange stripe on the crown, a grayish white throat, dull olive upperparts and flanks, and dull cinnamon-buff underparts.
fp: Adult females have no orange on their crown and are otherwise similar to males but with overall duller plumage and paler underparts.

mp: Males have olive-grey upperparts, yellowish underparts with faint streaking, and are brighter than females.
fp: Females are duller in colour than males.

mp: The male has a golden olive head and elongated bright orange body feathers, with bluish-green legs, bill, and orbital skin.
fp: The female is a dark green bird with a blackish tail and orange-yellow undertail coverts.

mp: Smaller than the saffron finch with a more contrasting orange front and dusky lores.
fp: Overall olive-gray with whitish underparts, and yellow to the wings and tail.

mp: The male has olive-brown upperparts, orange throat, breast and flanks, a white vent, and an incomplete white eye-ring.
fp: The female is similar to the male but is less bright.

mp: Males are bright orange and black with a glossy black head, chin, throat, and mantle, and bright orange-red underparts.
fp: Females are largely yellow with a grey upperside, yellow forehead, and almost completely bright yellow underside.

mp: The male has an orange head and body, black markings on wings and tail, a black region between eyes and bill, and a medium stripe across the upper breast.
fp: The female is duller than the male with a duller head and underparts, green mantles, and an orange-yellow wash.

mp: The adult male has a grey head with a buff supercilium, a streaked blackish back, a bright orange gorget, a black breast band, and otherwise yellow underparts.
fp: The female is duller, having a yellow throat and a much weaker breast band.

mp: During breeding season, the male has a black beak, black skin patches around the eyes, brown wings, and brilliant red to orange plumage.
fp: The female has drab brown plumage with dark streaks and a cream-colored belly year-round, resembling the off-season male.

mp: The adult male has a grey head, breast and upperparts, with a creamy-white belly marked by dark bars.
fp: Adult females occur in two morphs: a grey morph similar to the male but with a brownish wash on the breast, and a rufous morph that is reddish-brown above with strong dark bands.

mp: The male has a blue-grey head with a brown iris, two black bands in the tail, and three black under wing bands.
fp: The female has a brown head with a yellow iris, is slightly larger and darker than the male, and has three black tail bands and four narrower black under wing bands.

mp: Adult male in breeding plumage has a white face, throat and fore-crown, grey-brown hind-crown, hind-neck and back, white belly, narrow black band, and broad chestnut breast band.
fp: Female has generally grey-brown upperparts and white belly, with a pale face and white streak above the eye.

mp: Adult males have an off-white head, neck, and breast with gray mantle, orange band across upper mantle and flanks, black wings with white speculum, and bright salmon red legs.
fp: Adult females have a similar pattern but with a drab wash on crown and nape, less orange on flanks, darker scalloping on belly sides, and dull orange legs.

mp: The male is olive above with black remiges, a black tail with a white tip, blue-black iridescent throat and breast, and yellow underparts.
fp: The female lacks the iridescent throat, is greenish-olive above, and has a yellow supercilium.

mp: The adult male has black plumage, often tinted with blue and green, and red eyes.
fp: The adult female has brown plumage along the back with white spots and a cream-coloured underbelly with fine black stripes.

mp: Males possess shades of blue on their wings, blue streaks behind the eyes, and blue rumps.
fp: Females have no blue on the wings whatsoever but can have blue eye streaks as well as a blue rump.

mp: The male has a black head with a white forehead, black back and tail with a white wing bar, red breast and belly, and white lower belly and rump.
fp: The female lacks the white forehead and wing bar, has dark brown plumage instead of black, a duller red breast with more brown, and a smaller white rump area.

mp: The male has a black face with a white supercilium and throat.
fp: The female has brick-red underparts and lacks the white throat and head stripe of the male.

mp: The male is slightly smaller and duller in colour than the female.
fp: The female is more brightly coloured with red eyes, a white-flecked crown, face and breast, and chestnut shoulders with thin white streaking.

mp: The male has a black tail, ochre underparts, black head and neck with a green sheen, chestnut mantle, and white spots edged with black.
fp: The female is much duller with a rufous brow and ear coverts, a pale throat, and lacks white spotting on the body.

mp: A large bird with entirely black plumage, a white tail, a long thick pale cream-colored bill and casque, and blue-tinged whitish bare skin around the eyes and throat.
fp: Similar to the male but has a smaller bill and casque.

mp: The adult male has a black body with blue wing marks, a grayish speckled back and tail with blue peacock eyes, white face marks, and a red eye-ring.
fp: Females are mostly brown but with a white face.

mp: Breeding males have a white throat and underparts, a grey face and nape, and a black crown.
fp: Breeding females are largely gray with a pale bill and rusty tinged median coverts and scapulars.

mp: The male has a long white eyebrow, grey back, and a black and orange beak.
fp: The female resembles a green-winged saltator with a thicker bill, greener face, buff throat, and green back.

mp: The male is almost entirely black, with a small white wing patch.
fp: The female is a rich brown all over.

mp: The male has a white head and throat with chestnut brown body, tail, and wings, plus three long black wattles hanging from the beak base.
fp: The female has olive plumage with yellowish streaked underparts and a yellow vent area.

mp: The male has a black belly patch.
fp: The female has a black belly patch which is barred and is otherwise similar to the male but duller.

mp: Male has unspotted buff wing.
fp: Female has barred wing coverts, upperparts and upper belly.

mp: The male has bright blue upper parts, a red throat and breast, and white underparts.
fp: The female is duller blue with a brighter blue brow, shoulder, rump, and tail.

mp: Males have uniform blue-grey upperparts and a whitish belly and vent.
fp: Females have browner upperparts.

mp: Adult males have a grey head with a black mask, white underparts, and reddish-brown upperparts with dark bars.
fp: Females are duller and browner than males, with a less extensive black mask, less grey on the head, and buff-white flanks with black barring.

mp: Adult males are dark slaty gray above with a mottled gray face, paler gray supercilium, blackish crown and nape, and white underparts with fine gray barring.
fp: Adult females are similar but browner above with buffier underparts and browner tail bands.

mp: Males are solid deep blue with dark eyes, bill, and feet.
fp: Females are duller, with rufous-brown underparts.

mp: The adult male has a buffy white forehead, a rufous chesnut hindcrown, mostly shining green upperparts, a rusty lower back and uppertail coverts, grayish buff underparts, and a bronzy green tail with wide white tips and black bars.
fp: Females and immatures are similar to the adult male but their whole crown is brownish.

mp: Males have a striking black and white head and neck pattern, a red bill, and dark wings with a green speculum.
fp: Females are smaller than males, with orange underparts and throat.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black head with a partially hidden white patch in the center of the crown.
fp: Adult females have a slightly duller black crown and nape than males and a smaller white crown patch or none at all.

mp: Adult males have a glittering green frontlet, a dark purple-blue chin, and a glittering rosy pink gorget with an emerald green border.
fp: Adult females lack the green frontlet, have a blackish chin, and a whitish throat with green to dusky speckles and sometimes a few glittering rosy feathers.

mp: Glossy blue-black head, back, throat, and upper breast with bright yellow forehead, crown, and underparts.
fp: Olive-green above and yellow-olive below with a grayer breast patch and bright yellow undertail coverts.

mp: Males have a contrasting black cap that reaches just below the eye.
fp: Females have a grey cap the same colour as the back, sometimes with an irregular black post-ocular patch.

mp: Adult males have a mostly blue-gray head with black lores and a small black mask, blue-gray upperparts, and yellow underparts with a strong orange wash on the lower throat, upper breast, and flanks.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but overall duller, lacking the black mask and having little or no orange on the underparts.

mp: The summer male has a red bill, grey head and neck, and pale brown upper parts with pink breast, rump, and tail.
fp: Females are a very washed-out version of the breeding male.

mp: Adult males are mostly sooty gray with a blackish forehead and crest and browish black wings.
fp: Adult females are mostly blackish brown with a rufous forehead and crest, cinnamon-barred upperparts, and pale buff-barred underparts.

mp: The male has a rufous head crest, coppery green back, whitish rump band, green forehead and underparts, black-spotted rufous neck plumes, and golden rufous tail.
fp: The female lacks the crest and plumes, has green upperparts with a whitish tail band, paler rufous underparts, and a mostly bronze green tail with a dusky band.

mp: The male has a bright turquoise-blue face, grass-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a red shoulder patch on its blue wings.
fp: The female is generally duller and paler, with a pale green breast, yellow belly, and lacks the red wing patch.

mp: Males have bright turquoise feathers on their lower backs and rumps, and purple-blue underwing coverts and axillaries.
fp: Females have no blue markings, but their foreheads and faces are brighter yellow-green than males'.

mp: The male is a velvet black and yellow bird with a red iris, long black bill, rich yellow plumes along his flanks, and twelve blackish wire-like filaments.
fp: The female is a brown bird with black-barred buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have a pink rump.
fp: Females have a brown rump.

mp: Adult males in breeding have a white forehead, lower face, breast, and belly, with a black bar on the forecrown, chestnut crown and hindneck, brown upperparts, and two black breastbands.
fp: Adult females have a duller crown than males, with brownish rather than black areas and an upper breastband flecked with white throughout.

mp: The male of the nominate subspecies has bottle green upperparts, gray underparts, an emerald green throat, and a slightly forked glistening bronze tail.
fp: The female is bottle green above with an ochre-orange throat and upper breast spotted with olive green, whitish lower breast and belly with green spots, and outer tail feathers with whitish tips.

mp: Adult males have dark-blue plumage with bright-blue highlights on the head and upper-wings, and black on the face, wings, and tail.
fp: Females are brown in color.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely gray, with lighter underparts than upperparts and throat feathers that have black bases and gray tips.
fp: Adult females have olive-brown upperparts with a grayish tinge on the crown and nape, reddish yellow-brown tail and wing edges, and olive-buff underparts.

mp: Adult males are entirely black with a faint bluish gloss.
fp: Adult females have a brown crown, yellowish supercilium, brown upperparts with black streaks, and pale yellow underparts with dusky streaks.

mp: Adult males are mostly deep gray or blackish gray, sometimes with white tips on their outer tail feathers.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crown and gray face, with rufous brown upperparts and pale rufous brown underparts.

mp: Males have white heads and breast plumage with black legs.
fp: Females have reddish-brown heads and breast plumage with yellow-orange legs.

mp: The male has dark blue-black plumage over the head, throat, back, tail, and wings, with a washed out red belly and a white rump.
fp: The female is paler overall with orange instead of red underparts, slate grey instead of dark blue, and orange on the belly extending up the throat.

mp: Adult males of the nominate subspecies have a black crown and nape, a gray face, dark gray upperparts, and black wing coverts with white spots.
The adult male has a glossy green head, throat and nape, and a maroon breast band, with a yellow, orange, or white belly.
fp: The female has grey-brown upperparts and yellowish underparts.

mp: The male has three distinct morphs: black-bellied (entirely jet black with white rump and tail base), white-bellied (like black-bellied but with a white belly), and white-crowned (like white-bellied but with a white crown and nape).
fp: The female resembles the male but has black parts replaced by sooty black, grayish brown, or earthy brown, and a more buffish belly.

mp: Breeding males have brilliant iridescent blue and chestnut plumage with a black throat and nape, contrasting with grey-brown wings and a creamy white belly.
fp: Females have predominantly grey-brown plumage, a red-brown bill, and bright rufous lores.

mp: Males have olive upper parts, whitish underparts with smudgy streaking, buffy lower flanks, and a black hood, throat, breast, and upper flanks.
fp: Females are principally brown above and off-white below, with a buffy rump and flanks streaked with brown on the face, crown, and throat.

mp: Breeding males have velvety black plumage with a pair of green fleshy supraorbital caruncles above the eyes.
fp: Adult females are greenish with underparts striped with pale yellow-green longitudinal lines.

mp: Adult males have a small yellow forecrown, blue-black head and upperparts with a purplish gloss, and rich ochraceous to cinnamon-yellow underparts.
fp: Adult females have a mostly light olive-gray head with a faint olive-yellow supercilium, olive upperparts and wings, and yellowish underparts with an olive tinge.

mp: Adult males have a bright blue crown and upper nape with the rest of their plumage being deep and lustrous black.
fp: Adult females have grass-green upperparts, a mostly pale grayish green face and throat, and a dull green breast and flanks.

mp: Males have a blueish breast and belly.
fp: Females have a white-cream belly with a dark teal stripe running down the breast.

mp: Adult males are intense blue on all areas of the body, except for the black eye-patch and grey vent.
fp: Adult females are lighter blue.

mp: The adult male has a red rump and bill, and a blue throat patch.
fp: The female has a green patch.

mp: Males have a red face and crown, green to blue-green upperparts, red lower breasts, yellowish bellies with green streaks, and a red throat with a blue band.
fp: Females have green to blue-green upperparts, yellowish bellies with green streaks, a greenish cap, blue malars with a yellow edge, and a blue throat with a thin red band.

mp: Males have dull metallic green uppersides, pale gray lightly spotted chin and throat, dark metallic green belly, and an entirely black slightly forked tail.
fp: Females are dark metallic green to bluish green above and on the flanks with a pale gray throat.

mp: Males have iridescent purple sheen plumage, blue-green on the head, bronze on the lower breast, and a velvety black throat with a metallic green and blue triangular patch.
fp: Females have a pale eyebrow and buff underparts that are faintly barred with brown.

mp: It has a black head and a narrow bright yellow collar.
fp: The plumage is similar to that of the male but is less brightly coloured.

mp: The male has a scarlet throat and breast, uniformly grey underparts, grey-brown wings, a yellow lower back, and a bottle green tail.
fp: The female has dark olive upperparts and grey underparts.

mp: The adult male is entirely greenish-black or bluish-black except for his orange-red legs and conical white bill.
fp: The female resembles a female house sparrow, with streaked brown upperparts, buff underparts, a whitish supercilium and a yellowish bill, although she also has red legs.

mp: The male is a dark crimson with brownish-black tail and wings.
fp: The female is olive-brown with black spots.

mp: The male has glossy blue-black upperparts and a deep golden yellow forehead and underparts.
fp: The female is olive green above and greenish yellow below.

mp: The male has an iridescent violet head and back, and pure white underparts.
fp: The female has a thrush-like appearance with brown, boldly-streaked upper parts and white, heavily-streaked underparts.

mp: The male has an iridescent violet-blue crown, a metallic green body, and a slightly forked maroon tail with wide white edges.
fp: The female has green upperparts, whitish underparts with gray throat spots and green side spots, and maroon tail feathers with white tips.

mp: The adult male has a glittering violet-blue forehead and crown, dark golden-green upperparts, a steel blue forked tail, and brilliant green underparts.
fp: The adult female is entirely green above and dirty white to pale buff below, with a slightly forked tail featuring metallic green inner feathers and steel blue outer ones with white tips.

mp: Males have glossy violet head and upper parts, a brightly iridescent violet chin and upper breast, a white belly with broad black, green or violet bars, and a red eye-ring.
fp: Females have mottled greenish-bronze upper parts, a dark brown crown, white markings around the eyes, and a whitish breast with bronze-green bars and rufous markings.

mp: Males have bronzy green upperparts with a glittering blue forehead, coppery neck, emerald green gorget, and a deeply indented forked tail.
fp: Females have coppery green upperparts with a glittering green forehead, white underparts transitioning to buffy, and a less deeply indented forked tail.

mp: The male has an intense violet or blue head and throat with white spots behind each eye, a metallic bluish-green back, green breast fading to a grey belly, and black wings.
fp: The female is duller with a blue cap, green back, and grey throat, breast, and belly, while sharing the same wings, tail, and white spot behind the eye as the male.

mp: Males have a shining green crown and back with violet-blue rump, buffy spot behind eye, violet-blue gorget, green underparts, and very long iridescent metallic violet tail feathers with blue tips.
fp: Females have a glittering blue crown, whitish spot behind eye, white throat with green spots, cinnamon-rufous underparts, and a short unforked bluish green tail.

mp: The male has a blackish blue head, shining bronzy green back, orange-buff tail, and a green throat with an iridescent violet spot.
fp: The female has a green head, a buff throat with green spots, and a darkish green breast.

mp: Mainly gray with a lighter under-belly, white eye ring, yellow rump, undertail coverts, and a yellow breast patch.
fp: Slightly duller than the male, with less yellow on the breast.

mp: The adult male has bottle green upper- and underparts, a glittering bottle green gorget, and a purplish blue, slightly forked tail.
fp: The adult female has bottle green upperparts, a mottled green and white throat, breast, and belly, and outer tail feathers with whitish tips on their underside.

mp: Adult males have an olive-green crown and nape, a wide yellow supercilium, bright olive-green upperparts, and bright yellow underparts with faint blurry olive streaks on the flanks.
fp: Females are slightly duller than males with a fainter border to the ear coverts.

mp: The adult male has bronze-green upperparts, a mauve-purple gorget, mostly white underparts with buffy to pale cinnamon wash and green speckles, and rufous-edged black outer tail feathers.
fp: The adult female is bronze-green above with green central tail feathers, a whitish throat with dusky bronze speckles, and underparts similar to the male's.

mp: The male has a red bill with a cream tip and a black cutting edge.
fp: The female has a black bill.

mp: In summer, males have a black throat grading into the grey of the rest of the body.
fp: In summer, females can have either a white throat or a small dark patch on the throat.

mp: The male has a pink-red breast, belly, undertail, and forehead, with dark slate chest, back, wings, and uppertail, and a deep red bill tip.
fp: The female matches the male's pattern but has yellow instead of red, dark olive dark parts, and a yellow bill tip.

mp: Adult males have mainly black-grey plumage with red legs, bill, extended frontal shield and horn.
fp: Females are dark brown above and paler below, with plumage streaked and barred with darker markings.

mp: Males have black plumage with a white crissum, curly head feathers, and conspicuous crimson bill ornaments and wattles.
fp: Females have black plumage with a reddish-buff crissum, lack bill ornamentation, and have greyish flesh-colored feet and legs.

mp: Breeding males have a white shoulder patch, unfeathered yellow skin, and black forehead and throat wattles.
fp: Females resemble non-breeding males but have brown flight feathers and tail instead of black.

mp: Males have a wide red band from behind the bill to the ear coverts.
fp: Females lack the red band on the head found in males.

mp: The adult male has a glittering green gorget and chestnut underparts with a bold black stripe down the center.
fp: The adult female's throat is white with grayish and green spots and the rest of the underparts are pale rufous.

mp: Adult males have a bright violet crown, metallic green to bronze green upperparts, and brownish gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dull blue crown, pale cinnamon wash on underparts, and buff wash on outer tail feather tips.

mp: Adult males have a red crown, nape, and hindneck with a black supercilium extending to the red.
fp: Adult females have a whitish crown with a black supercilium separating it from the red nape.

mp: Adult males have a small yellow forecrown, glossy blue-black head and upperparts with a purplish sheen, bright yellow breast and belly, and blackish tail with white inner webs.
fp: Adult females have an olive-yellow forehead and face, grayish crown and nape, olive upperparts with a gray tinge, and mostly olive-yellow underparts with a white belly center.

mp: The breeding male has a white or nearly white forehead and crown, buff mantle, blacker wings, white underparts tinged with buff, and a black mask extending from the ear coverts to the bill.
fp: The female is a browner bird but retains the characteristic white lower back, with less marked seasonal changes.

mp: The male is much bigger than the female, with dark grey to dark brown body feathers and dark metallic green breast feathers.
fp: The female is smaller than the male, with dark grey to dark brown body feathers and dark metallic green breast feathers.

mp: The male has jet black plumage with striking iridescent scale-like golden-green breast shields and triangular silver feathers on its crown.
fp: The female is unadorned and has brown plumage.

mp: The adult male has a predominantly red head and neck with a bright yellow cheek patch and scarlet plumage.
fp: Females are duller overall with subdued red plumage flecked with green and a smaller dull yellow cheek patch.

mp: The male is dark olive-grey above with a chestnut nape, chestnut throat and breast edged with white and black bands, buff abdomen, white eyebrow, black mask, and white outer tail feathers.
fp: The female is plainer with a pale rufous nape, rufous-buff or pale grey throat and underparts, and lacks the distinctive banding of the male.

mp: The adult male has a grey back and head, brick-red underparts, and white malar streaks.
fp: The female is mainly brown above, with a greyer head, and whitish below with a pink flush.

mp: The male is very dark, grey and black with numerous white spots bordered with black and deep crimson patches on the sides and back of the neck.
fp: The female has pale brownish-grey upper parts finely vermiculated and spotted with black, with most feathers having black patches and central white streaks.

mp: The male has a black head, wings, and tail, and a pink body, dark pink below and pale pink to nearly white on the mantle.
fp: The female is similar but drabber, with a dark brown head and the pink tinged greyer.

mp: The male has a red crown.
fp: The female has a black crown.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead, crown, and upper nape, with a white face, reddish yellow-brown upperparts, and a black lower throat and breast.
fp: Females have a rufous-brown crown, a distinct white supercilium, and lack the black on the throat and breast found in males.

mp: The adult male has a black crown, upper back, wings and tail, with otherwise white plumage and orange legs.
fp: The female is olive-green with orange legs and resembles female golden-headed manakins.

mp: Adult males have entirely white plumage and a single black wattle with a few white feathers draping from the base of the maxilla.
fp: Adult females have an olive-green head and upperparts, olive-green wings and tail, and yellow underparts with olive streaks, lacking a wattle.

mp: The male is dark blue with a lighter blue brow, dark grey lores and face, and a white belly bordered by smoky grey.
fp: The female has olive brown upperparts, a rufous breast fading to white, a white face, and a chestnut tail.

mp: The adult male has a black crown, black lines on the white cheeks, a black throat patch, and a pinkish-red bill.
fp: The adult female has a grey crown, a brown and buff line below the eye, and black speckling on the throat.

mp: The male has a black bill.
fp: The female has a pea-green bill that becomes yellowish during the breeding season.

mp: Males have a bright green head and chest, olive-coloured wings, throat and neck, and a patch of maroon on the shoulders.
fp: Females are less colourful, lack the maroon shoulder patches, and have a frosted green breast.

mp: The male has a shiny black head, neck, tail, and mantle, with a white collar, orange throat, white underparts, and an orange rump.
fp: The female is duller with dark gray upperparts, black wings and tail, a white collar, black lores, white wing markings, and an orange rump.

mp: Adult males have a glittering green face and crown, a blue-violet gorget, and white underparts with green speckles along the sides.
fp: Adult females are similar but have a less glittering face and crown, and a white throat with green speckles.

mp: The male has dark bluish green upperparts, an iridescent reddish violet gorget, and a white belly with bluish green forked tail.
fp: The female is bronzy green above with a grayish mask, pale cinnamon throat, white belly, tawny flanks, and a rounded cinnamon-banded tail.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with rufous-chestnut edges, a white supercilium, mostly black face, rufous-chestnut upperparts, and white underparts with black scallops.
fp: Adult females have a dark reddish yellow-brown crown, pale buff supercilium, mostly plain white underparts, and pale buff flanks and crissum.

mp: Adult breeding males are mainly black with white flecking on the back and wings, and have a white bill.
fp: Adult females are mainly black with white flecking on the back and wings, and have a black bill.

mp: Males have a striking purple head cap.
fp: Females are almost entirely green feathered.

mp: Grey-green above and yellow below with a grey head and upper breast, black throat and mask bordered with white, and large yellow patches in the wings and tail.
fp: Brown with dark streaks, yellow outer tail feathers, and yellow fringes to the wing feathers.

mp: Adult males have a white forehead and supercilium, mostly dark bluish gray body, and black face below the white markings.
fp: Adult females have a cinnamon to yellow-buff forehead and supercilium, olive-brown upperparts, and white throat and underparts.

mp: Males have a small tuft of violet feathers on their upper flank.
fp: Females have white tufts on their upper flank.

mp: Males have blackish lores.
fp: Females are duller overall and generally have pale gray lores.

mp: The male has a black bill.
fp: The female has a horn-colored (light gray) bill.

mp: Males are vibrantly colored with distinctive violet-blue underparts and chest.
fp: Females are generally duller with pale underparts.

mp: The male has black upperparts, head, and breast with a white supercilium and large white wingbar.
fp: The female has black less intense than in the male.

mp: Males are red from forehead to nape with a narrow yellowish white supercilium, dark olive green around the eye, and a red malar band.
fp: The female has an olive forehead and crown and much less red at the malar.

mp: The adult male has a deep blue-grey upper body and a chestnut under body.
fp: The adult female is paler than the male.

mp: Adult males are black with red underparts, a white crown, a larger white pattern on the head, and brown or red spots under the wings.
fp: Adult females are black with red underparts and a white crown atop their heads.

mp: Adult males have glossy black plumage with a large white crown and a bright red throat.
fp: Adult females have glossy black plumage with a large white crown and a duskier throat that approaches purple.

mp: Adult males have a chestnut-brown crown and nape, bare blue skin around the eye, a blackish band from the lores through the eye, and white cheeks, throat, and breast.
fp: Adult females have the same plumage as males but with the addition of a cinnamon patch between the scapulars.

mp: Adult males have a bright coral-red bill with a dark tip, brilliant violet-blue head and throat, a small white chin patch, golden green upper parts, and a steel blue to blue black tail.
fp: Females have subdued green plumage, lighter golden green upper parts, and lack the violet blue head and throat of the male.

mp: The adult male has a black crown, wings, tail, and mid-back band, with a white head, neck, breast, and upper back, olive-green rump, and bright yellow belly.
fp: Females are olive-green with yellow bellies.

mp: The adult male has a coppery bronze forecrown, an erect white crest, bronzy green nape and back, glittering green throat with long wispy cheek tufts, and a cinnamon-rufous breast.
fp: The adult female is generally duller, lacks the crest and cheek tufts, has a dusky bronze face and forecrown, and a white throat and chest with bronzy green speckles.

mp: The male has a white head, neck, breast, and tail, with black remaining plumage, white crest, bare dark blue skin, and a blackish casque.
fp: The female is smaller than the male and has a black neck and underparts.

mp: The adult male is mostly black with a white crown that can be erected as a low crest.
fp: The female is olive-green with a grey head and throat, and grey-green or olive underparts.

mp: The adult male has a white forehead and crown, a white throat, and the rest of the head, neck, and breast are dull dark blue.
fp: The female is similar to the male, but the blue plumage fades into scaling.

mp: Adult males have a blue back, wings, and tail, light blue or greyish underparts with rufous undertail coverts, a black crown, face, and lores, and a white cheek.
fp: Females are more subtly coloured with a lighter blue back, crown, nape, and tail, olive primaries, and a yellow breast, belly, flanks, and face.

mp: Males have a metallic violet or bluish violet forehead, a mostly black face with a wide white stripe behind the eye, a dull black crown, bright metallic green to bronze green upperparts, and a violet blue chin and upper throat.
fp: Females have bills that are mostly blackish with some red to orange at the base, unlike the males' red bills with black tips.

mp: Adult males have a dark gray head, neck, back, and rump with a hidden white patch, blackish tail and wings with white tips, black throat and breast, white flanks, and a gray crissum.
fp: Adult females have a mottled pale olive-brown face, olive-brown upperparts becoming reddish yellow-brown on the rump, and dark brown tail feathers with light cinnamon-rufous edges.

mp: The male has a white face and breast bordered by a black band across the breast and nape to the hind crown, with silver-grey upperparts and pinkish-white eyes.
fp: The female has grey-brown upperparts, white or pale grey underparts with a fainter blackish-brown breast band, and brown eyes.

mp: Males have a white forecrown and forehead.
fp: Females have a reddish-brown forecrown and forehead.

mp: Adult males have a small patch of red, not always visible, on the crown.
fp: Adult females lack the red crown patch and otherwise resemble the male.

mp: Adult males have a grey and reddish body, a blue bill, and a largely white head with a black cap and neck.
fp: Adult females have a grey-brown body with a white face and a darker bill, cap, and cheek stripe.

mp: Males have a white head with a small crest, a white throat, and a contrasting black body.
fp: Females have a white forecrown and throat, with a greyish-brown breast, flanks, wings, and tail.

mp: Males have a distinctive white head, neck, breast, and belly, with slate grey wings and tail, and grey-black upper parts with iridescence.
fp: Females appear similar to males but their white colouration is less brilliant and more muddied.

mp: Adult males have white heads, mostly grey bodies, white bellies, and a bright yellow/orange bill with a black nail.
fp: Adult females have brown heads and necks with a small white line from the eye to the fore-neck and a greenish/yellow bill.

mp: Has a white head, slightly curved bright red beak, red legs and feet, and dark blue or violet-blue iridescent plumage with purple-copper luster on the wings.
fp: Smaller than the male with a much shorter bill, while sharing the white head, red beak, red legs, and dark blue or violet-blue iridescent plumage.

mp: It has a black body and white head with a red spot at the back of the head.
fp: It has a black body and white head.

mp: The adult male is glossy black, apart from white underwing coverts and a small white patch on the upperwing.
fp: Females are entirely rufous in plumage, somewhat paler below.

mp: The nominate male has a black cap down to the eyes and nape, bluish gray upperparts, a black tail with white outer feathers, and a white throat fading to pale bluish gray on the breast and flanks.
fp: The female has a dark gray cap, white lores, and a white supercilium.

mp: The adult male has black upperparts with narrow pale lines, a red forehead and crown, white underparts with a yellowish wash and cinnamon breast flush, red eyes, a yellowish bill, and greenish-grey legs.
fp: The adult female resembles the male but has a black spot at the base of the lower mandible.

mp: The adult male has a red crown.
fp: The adult female has a yellow crown.

mp: The male has black and white barring on the back and wings, with a black head, neck, and underparts.
fp: The female has a head, neck, breast, and upper parts barred or chequered in black and buff, with a black belly.

mp: The adult male is mostly glossy blue-black with a white erectile ruff on the throat and sides of the neck.
fp: Females are olive-green with a greyish throat.

mp: The male has grey upper back and areas behind the head.
fp: The female has a rufous mantle on her upper back and behind the head.

mp: Males are mostly glossy black with a white interscapular patch, white lesser wing coverts, and white-tipped median and greater wing coverts.
fp: Females have yellowish brown to chestnut crown, upperparts, and wings with no interscapular patch, olive-tinged gray face, and olive-brown underparts.

mp: The adult male has a light brown head and breast and a white belly.
fp: The adult female is darker brown on the back and belly.

mp: Glossy black with white underwing coverts and a conspicuous white shoulder patch.
fp: Olive upperparts, yellow underparts, and a grey head and neck.

mp: Mainly black above and white below, with a grey rump, white stripe over the eye, white wing-patches, and white on the outer tail-feathers.
fp: Has a similar pattern to males but is brown instead of black above and has fine black barring on the underparts.
