mp: The male has a sooty blue-grey head and nape, dark purplish-maroon neck and breast, sooty-grey mantle with a steely sheen, chestnut underwing coverts, rufous flight feathers, and yellow eyes.
fp: The female is a little smaller and duller than the male.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead and crown with the rest of their plumage featuring thin black and white bars.
fp: Females have a rufous crown with black-tipped crest feathers, barred upperparts and tail, a plain buffy white throat, and cinnamon-buff underparts.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely black with white edges on outer scapulars, a white patch between them, and a hidden white patch underneath.
fp: Females are mostly gray with white in the same places as the male and thin white streaks on their throat and breast.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely black except for a hidden white patch between the scapulars, small white spots on the wing coverts, and a wide white band at the end of the tail.
fp: Adult females have a bright deep rufous crown, upperparts, wings, and tail, with a black face, throat, and breast, and gray underparts with a reddish brown cast on the flanks and crissum.

mp: Adult males have gray upperparts with a hidden white patch between the shoulders, gray wings with white-tipped black coverts, a darker gray tail with a wide white band, black throat and upper breast, and paler gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have paler gray face and upperparts than males with white-tipped gray wing coverts, a white throat, gray sides and flanks, and pale cinnamon-buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have an entirely black head and upper breast with a thin yellow collar, green upperparts, and yellow underparts with black scallops.
fp: Females have a green head, little or no yellow collar, less black scalloping on the underparts, and a yellow eye-ring.

mp: The male has a distinctive red head, neck, upper breast, and mantle, black eye ring, scapulars, and wings, a distinctive pointed beak and brown legs.
fp: The female is primarily brown, with an orange part underneath the also-pointed beak.

mp: Adult males have a grayish face with a white supercilium, cinnamon-brown crown and upper back, and a white throat, breast, and belly with a band of black spots.
fp: Adult females have a buff band on the lower back and fewer spots on buff-tinged underparts.

mp: Males are bright blue with a black spotted back, bright purple throat and belly, and a blue band across the chest.
fp: Females are dull brown with some white mottling.

mp: The male has grey upperparts with some barring on the rump and lower-tail coverts, and faint or black and white barring on the belly or breast depending on the subspecies.
fp: The female's underparts are barred black and white, often extending up to the lower breast, with additional barred patches on the breast in some subspecies.

mp: The male has a green-blueish back, head, and upper breast, with a pinkish-red lower breast, pale grey finely barred wings, and a yellow bare facial patch.
fp: The female has a pinkish-red whole breast, bluish-green back and back of the head, pale grey finely barred wings, and a yellow bare facial patch.

mp: Adult males have a blackish gray head and upper breast, dark reddish yellow-brown upperparts and tail, brighter rufous wings, and a dark grayish brown belly.
fp: Adult females have a brownish black head and throat, upperparts and wings similar to the male, and dark yellowish brown underparts.

mp: Yellowish-buff with heavy black bars on its back, white throat, pale grey neck and breast, white belly, cream barred flanks, chestnut head and neck, and olive-green legs.
fp: Similar to the male but paler on the back.

mp: In flight, the male shows a small white spot towards the wingtip and white tips to the two outer tail feathers.
fp: The female is paler and lacks white spots on the wings or outer tail.

mp: Adult males have a deep purplish blue forecrown and crown with a narrow black stripe, a bronzy black face, and a long narrow gorget that is emerald green under the chin and purplish with a bluish tip.
fp: The adult female is similar to the male but duller overall and dingier underneath, with a smaller gorget that is mostly white.

mp: Males have bolder breast streaks, a darker-orange belly, are smaller in size, and display a thicker supercilium than females.
fp: Males have bolder breast streaks, a darker-orange belly, are smaller in size, and display a thicker supercilium than females.

mp: Adult males have a blackish gray head, upperparts, and tail with a mostly-hidden white patch between the scapulars, black wings with white dots, and slightly lighter blackish gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a chestnut crown and upperparts with buffy white spots on the wing coverts, a dark grey face, throat, and breast with thin white streaks, and an olive-brown belly and crissum.

mp: The male has white underparts with a black breast band and glossy blue-black head and mantle.
fp: The female is similar to the male but is duller above with a chestnut rather than black breast band.

mp: Adult males have an almost entirely glossy black head and upperparts, white throat and underparts with streaky black on the breast sides, and wide pale yellow edges on their tertials.
fp: Females have a chestnut crown, buffy lores and eye-ring on a mostly gray face, olive nape, back, and uppertail coverts, and blackish tail and wings with pale yellow and olive edges.

mp: Males have a black bib and overall darker plumage.
fp: Females are lighter and have bibs of either gray or white depending on the subspecies.

mp: Males are almost entirely blackish to dark gray with a white interscapular patch, gray flight feather edges, and white wing covert tips.
fp: Females have olive-tinged dark gray upperparts, reddish brown underparts, and yellowish brown wing coverts and flight feather edges.

mp: The adult male has largely black upperparts, including a black cap, while the underparts, neck, breast, and sides of the head are rich chestnut with large buff patches on the shoulders.
fp: The female is duller, brown and streaked on the back and crown.

mp: The male has velvety black upperparts with purplish uppertail coverts, a white spot behind the eye, an olive green gorget, and underparts that are a mix of dark gray and rufous with green dots.
fp: The female has shining grass green upperparts, purplish uppertail coverts, a white spot behind the eye, and buffy white underparts with green dots.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black head, black back, rump, and uppertail coverts, with bright yellow breast and belly.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have a dark olive or sooty olive back instead of black and a white spot on the lores.

mp: The male has a black head and most underparts, dark gray lower belly, rich chestnut upper parts, and a long white tuft behind the eye.
fp: The female has a gray face and most underparts, browner chestnut upper parts, a white throat, and a much smaller white tuft behind the eye.

mp: Males have predominantly black plumage with a scarlet red hood.
fp: Females have a mainly olive colored plumage and a red mask covering the forehead.

mp: A breeding male has a golden-green head, upperparts, chin, and throat, with black feather bases, a dark metallic blue upper tail, an orange breastband, yellow pec tufts, and white flank streaks.
Males have a black bib and overall darker plumage.
fp: Females are lighter and have bibs of either gray or white depending on the subspecies.

mp: The male is ruddy-brown, with no clear distinction between the underparts and the upperparts.
fp: The female has black barred upperparts.

mp: The male is brown with a bare maroon-grey skin around its eye, buff-colored tail, dark-brown iris, yellow mouth, black sickle-like bill, dark horn-like forecrown feathers, bronze neck plumes, and elongated purple-tipped flank plumes.
fp: The female is unadorned brown, smaller than the male, with a bill longer than the male's and dark-barred below.

mp: The male has black upper- and underparts, dark blue tail coverts, and a violet-blue throat and undertail-coverts.
fp: The female is bronze-green above, bluish-green on rump and uppertail-coverts, golden-green underparts and has a pale blue chin.

mp: Adult males are entirely black except for a small, mostly hidden, patch of white between the shoulders.
fp: Adult females are mostly sooty black with a rufous breast and upper belly.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and nape, a long white to pale gray supercilium, and a black streak through the eye, with gray upperparts and mostly gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a buffish forehead and black and white streaked crown, gray upperparts with an olive tinge, and white underparts with an ochraceous breast.

mp: The adult male has brown, mottled and barred blackish upper-parts, a rufescent throat and neck, dark grey breast, cinnamon to buff underparts, a blackish cap, and pale red or bright red legs.
fp: The adult female is similar to the male but is more heavily barred above.

mp: The male has dark gray upper parts with a red tinge, a usually invisible orange-red crest, a diffuse black mask, and a bright salmon orange throat.
fp: The female is similar to the male but duller and has a smaller crest.

mp: The male has a black head, throat and upper breast, with bright green upper parts and yellowish-green underparts.
fp: The female lacks the black head region, has a bright green back, throat and chest, and underparts streaked with yellow and green.

mp: Adult males have a mostly rufous-chestnut head with a long black crest, black back and wings with yellow flight feather bases, a dark gray to black breast band, and a pale gray belly.
fp: Adult females have a duller rufous head with a shorter black crest, brownish olive back, bronze-olive gray breast, and white belly with olive orange flanks.

mp: Adult males have leaden gray upperparts, a black throat, and mostly paler gray underparts with a grayish white belly.
fp: Adult females have whitish throats with black and gray speckles, mottled gray and white breasts, and buff-tinged bellies.

mp: The male has a black head and throat, white cheeks and superciliary stripe, grey upperparts and underparts, with white wing-covert tips and tail corners.
fp: The female is more drab with a less distinct head pattern, a retained crest, and brown-tinged back and wings.

mp: Adult males have a dramatic black crest, white crown and nape, black head, black upperparts with white streaks, black wings with white edges, and a yellowish-white belly.
fp: Adult females have a shorter crest than males.

mp: The adult male has a purple bare ring around its eye.
fp: The adult female has a blue-black eye ring, darker sides of the head, and duller chestnut colors.

mp: Adult males have a dark bluish gray crown, nape, and upperparts with a small white patch between scapulars, a mostly black face with a pale supercilium, and pale gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dark grayish olive-brown crown, nape, and upperparts, a blackish face, a white throat with small black spots, and light buff underparts with an olive tinge.

mp: The adult male has a scarlet crown and nape, black sides of the head, and a black girdle across the lower breast.
fp: The adult female differs from the male in that its crown and nape are black.

mp: Adult males have a deep rufous back, rump, and uppertail coverts, with the rest of the body almost entirely black, white wing covert tips, white flanks, and barred white undertail coverts.
fp: Adult females have deep rufous upperparts, mostly olive-brown underparts that are paler and buffier, blackish wings and tail with white covert tips, and variable dark streaks or mottling on the head and throat.

mp: Mostly purplish black with glittering golden green to bluish green on the lower back and rump, a white breast tuft, and a rufous tail with dusky tips.
fp: Colored like the male but duller overall with less iridescent lower back and rump.

mp: Adult males have red beaks.
fp: Adult females have gray-brown beaks.

mp: Adult males have a black mask, pale slate-gray crown, yellowish green upperparts, and bright yellow throat and underparts.
fp: Females lack black on the head, have gray-washed olive crown and ear coverts, and paler overall upper- and underparts than males.

mp: Adult males have a red to rosy red crown, back, rump, wings, tail, and underparts, with a glossy blackish head, neck, and wings.
fp: Adult females have a dull reddish crown and ear coverts on an olive face, olive upperparts and wings, a dull reddish tail, and red underparts.

mp: Smaller and duller than the female.
fp: Larger and brighter than the male.

mp: The male has a black head with a long, silver, slightly downcurved bill, bright yellow mouth, scarlet-red eyes, and jet black body covered with iridescent metallic blue-greenish scale-like feathers.
Adult males are mostly very dark gray with blackish head, neck, throat, and wing coverts that have narrow white tips.
fp: Adult females have a dull reddish brown crown, medium brown back and rump, and white underparts with a buff band across the breast.

mp: Plumage is blackish with white spots on the chest and wings, a white tail tip, a short white stripe above the eye, and a white spot on the side of the neck.
fp: Similar to the male but has fewer spots and is paler on the abdomen.

mp: Adult males are mostly slate gray with a black head, throat, and breast, a usually hidden small white patch between their scapulars, and faint white bars on their tail.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crest, nape, upperparts, and wings, with barred pale buff to white and blackish brown forehead, sides of head, underparts, and tail, and rufous flanks.

mp: Males have a dark brown throat, cinnamon red underparts, and often a dark band between the throat and breast.
fp: Females have a lighter throat than males and generally have longer wings.

mp: Males of the nominate subspecies are almost entirely blackish gray with white patches and narrow white wing covert tips.
fp: Females have rufous-tinged olive-gray upperparts, orange-rufous forehead, face, throat, and underparts, with a blackish tail.

mp: Adult males are generally blackish gray with a black crown, lighter back and belly, brownish wings with white-edged feathers, and white-tipped tail feathers.
fp: Adult females have a blackish gray crown and face, dark gray upperparts with a reddish brown tinge, brown wings and tail, and reddish brown underparts.

mp: The male has a white tip on its tail, which it displays by erecting it to show white markings.
fp: The female lacks the white tail tip and does not display the white markings.

mp: The male of the blackish subspecies is dark to very dark gray, while the Pacific subspecies male is black.
fp: The female of the blackish subspecies is dark gray, sometimes with an olive wash, while the Pacific subspecies female is gray with brown flanks.

mp: Males are crimson-red from crown to nape with brown feather bases showing through.
fp: The female has a brown crown with thin white feather tips.

mp: The male has a long black and white crest, a mostly dusky face with a buffy-white collar, olive green upperparts, and a thin white beard with a purplish blue center stripe.
fp: The adult female lacks the crest and beard, is overall duller, and has a white throat.

mp: Underparts vary geographically, some with rufous or dark bellies and a white crescent.
fp: Females have white belly.

mp: Males have white ear streaks and darker markings.
fp: Females have more tawny yellow ear streaks.

mp: Males have a dark blue cap and dark blue wings.
fp: Females have an aqua-green cap and wings.

mp: The male has dark green upperparts with a dark glittering blue forehead, golden green underparts, white leg puffs, and a long forked blue-black tail.
fp: The female has dark green upperparts without a blue forehead, bright cinnamon-buff throat and belly, pale buff fringes on undertail coverts, and a less deeply forked tail.

mp: Adult males have a blue collar across the upper breast to lower neck above the mantle.
fp: Adult females have some blue on the rear crown.

mp: The male has a purplish red head, neck, wing coverts, uppertail coverts, and breast, with browner lower breast, belly, flanks, shoulders, and back, and white vent and undertail coverts.
fp: The adult female is paler than the male, especially on its underparts.

mp: Males are multi-shaded with colors ranging from light yellow-green to dark blue-green, featuring deep blue feathers on the forehead and face, and red to rusty red-brown tails.
fp: Females are less vibrant blue, slightly smaller, and have a more rounded head.

mp: Males have orange breasts.
fp: Females have orange patches on their faces.

mp: Males have more red on their wing than females.
fp: Females have less red on their wing than males.

mp: The male has extensive blue on the head and a bluish breast.
fp: The female has reduced blue on the head compared to the male.

mp: Adult males have a deep glittering blue upper throat, face, and crown, metallic green upperparts, and a dark steel blue tail.
fp: Adult females have metallic green to bronze-green upperparts, a blue-black tail with greyish tips, and mostly dull white underparts.

mp: Adult males of the nominate subspecies are mostly very dark gray with a hidden white line at the bend of the wing.
fp: Adult females have a dark reddish brown crown, upperparts, and wings, with a blackish tail and blackish forehead, face, and upper throat.

mp: Male birds have a pale blue forehead and forecrown with a small red patch.
fp: Females look identical to the male except they do not have a red spot on their forecrown.

mp: The male has a metallic green to bluish crown and upper parts, blackish chin and upper throat, green lower throat and chest, and rufous underparts.
fp: The female differs from the male in that her lower breast and belly are ochraceous.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely darkish gray with a hidden white patch between the scapulars.
fp: Adult females have browner, paler gray upperparts and throat with thin white streaks, and deep cinnamon-rufous belly and flanks.

mp: Mostly dark gray with reddish brown flanks, vent, and crissum, and a variable amount of white on the crown.
fp: Paler gray washed with brown above with a black-barred brown belly.

mp: The male has dark plumage which shows silvery white streaks.
Up to 50 cm long, rufous brown and black spotted with an elongated crest, metallic blue-green breast sides, and tail feathers decorated with large blue-green ocelli.
fp: Smaller and duller brown than the male, with a brown iris and no spurs on its feet.

mp: The male has black wings marked with a white wing stripe.
fp: The female has black wings marked with a rufous wing stripe.

mp: Adult males have a deep black crown, pale eye-ring, olive-green upperparts, and bright golden-yellow underparts with irregular black scale-like markings.
fp: Adult females have a lighter dusky olive-green crown and their undersides are almost completely covered with black markings.

mp: It has reddish-brown upperparts, rufous throat, grey breast, whitish belly, and brown legs.
fp: The female has a distinct black barring and is ochraceous on its upperparts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly gray face, black throat with white spots, olive-brown crown and upperparts, and gray breast.
fp: Adult females have a pale brownish buff face and throat, yellowish olive-brown upperparts, reddish tail, and pale brownish buff underparts.

mp: The male has a large yellow, down-curving beak topped by a casque, with black head, upper parts, and underparts apart from reddish-brown cheeks, white rump, belly, and tail.
fp: The female is smaller than the male and has a black beak and casque, otherwise similar in plumage with black head, upper parts, and underparts apart from reddish-brown cheeks, white rump, belly, and tail.

mp: The male has a dull gold crown with a wide black patch through the eye, a black back with yellow streaks, and a cinnamon breastband with a yellow to olive belly.
fp: The female is similar but duller, with more yellowish markings on the wings and a black-spotted cinnamon throat.

mp: The male has a dark brown fore-crown and red hind-crown.
fp: The female lacks the red colour on the hind-crown.

mp: The beak is black.
fp: The beak is reddish or yellowish-white with a black tip.

mp: Males have a partially hidden white patch on the crown.
fp: Females lack the white patch on the crown.

mp: Males have dark gray upperparts, blackish gray wings and tail with wide white tips on the wing coverts, and medium gray throat and underparts.
fp: Females have a dark brown crown and face, olive-brown upperparts, blackish brown wings and tail with pale cinnamon-rufous tips, and dark tawny throat and belly.

mp: Adult males have black upperparts with a white collar, white unmarked cheeks, throat, and underparts, and a black tail with narrow white bars.
fp: Adult females are like males but have the addition of white spots on their scapulars and secondaries.

mp: Plumage is mainly green with a yellowish tone on the underparts, buff cheeks, face, and crown, and a dark blue patch on the top of the head.
fp: Similar to the male but with smaller head markings and paler facial colour.

mp: The male has a dark olive or blackish crown and a bright red nape, with whitish or buff streaked olive head parts.
fp: The female lacks the red nape, sharing the male's plain green upper parts and spotted underparts.

mp: Adult males have blue-grey crowns, napes, and hindnecks with darker mantles, white to pale buff-pink face and throat, and buff-pink belly.
fp: Females are smaller on average and have more wine on the breast, along with dark blackish-red bills.

mp: The adult male has blue upper-parts from the back of its head to mid-back, extending into the upper surfaces of the forewings.
fp: The female has a small area of blue on the nape.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and nape, a gray face with white lores and supercilium, mostly gray upperparts, and black wings and tail with white edges and tips.
fp: Females are similar to males but have dull buff edges on forehead feathers, a fainter eye streak, olive tinge to upperparts, and pale buff tinge to underparts.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely shiny black with a wide white band at the base of the primaries.
fp: Adult females have a brownish gray head and upperparts, a rufous-buff rump, and whitish underparts with heavy dusky streaking.

mp: Dark sepia with green iridescence on the head and back, and a chestnut breast.
fp: Dark brown all over.

mp: Males are red and black in coloration.
fp: Females are grayish-olive, sometimes with a red cap or red head.

mp: Male has velvety jet-black head with coppery-bronze sheen, silver-white tipped crest, iridescent eye ring, blue-green to purple nuchal bar, three long wire-like occipital plumes, and white flank feathers.
Adult males are mostly black with a mostly hidden white patch between scapulars, white tips on scapulars and wing coverts, and dark gray flanks and belly.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but their scapulars and wing coverts are entirely black.

mp: Males of the nominate subspecies are mostly slate gray with a slight brown tinge on upperparts, white-tipped wing coverts, and a deep red iris.
fp: Females have a mostly dark gray head, dark reddish yellow-brown upperparts with cinnamon-rufous wing covert tips, blackish gray tail, deep rufous underparts, and a dark brown iris.

mp: The adult male has a white stripe above the eye which ends in a tuft of feathers.
fp: The adult female has a grey stripe above the eye.

mp: Males have much longer crests and more intense coloration overall.
fp: Females have shorter crests, less intense blue colors, and a generally smaller size.

mp: Adult males have a bright blue crown and upper nape, deeper blue rump and uppertail coverts, with the rest of their plumage black.
fp: Adult females have green upperparts brightest on the rump, a dusky green tail, pale grayish face and throat, and a yellowish gray belly.

mp: Adult males have a black and white streaked forehead, black crown and crest, medium gray collar, black back with white bars, and white throat with black streaks.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crest and whitish sides to their head and neck.

mp: The male has a distinctive white forehead, eyebrows, throat and underparts.
fp: The female lacks white areas, showing dull greyish-white underparts and yellow eyebrows, cheek and throat.

mp: Adult males have a black and white streaked face, black crown, back, and rump with white streaks, a narrow white patch between the shoulders, and white underparts with black streaks.
fp: Adult females have buff streaks on the head, lack the white shoulder patch, and have pale buff underparts with thinner black streaks than the male.
The female is larger and more brightly-coloured than the male.

mp: The adult male has bronze-green upperparts, a chestnut tail, glittering green throat and upper breast, chestnut belly, and chestnut undertail coverts with greenish edges.
fp: The female is similar but has a slightly paler belly and white bars near the end of some throat feathers.

mp: The male has a black frontlet, face and throat, a rufous chest, and buff or white belly.
fp: The female has a rufous face, throat and chest, and a buff or white belly.

mp: Adult males have a green forehead, cyanine-blue crown and nape, shiny emerald-green face and throat, bright green back, bright yellow rump, and deep chestnut lower breast and belly.
Adult males have a rufous-chestnut crown, crest, and nape, black forehead, lores, face, and throat, dark olive-brown upperparts with rufous wing edges, and a rufous-chestnut breast.
fp: Adult females are like males but have short black bars on their back feathers and lesser coverts.

mp: The male has brown upper parts, a gray face, throat, and chest, orange-brown flanks and vent, an orange-red crown, and a white tuft behind the eye.
fp: The female has an orange-red head and chest, a whitish belly, and a smaller white plume behind the eye than the male.

mp: Has blackish-grey upperparts, heavily barred grey and brown underparts with chestnut-colored flanks, a white throat, and a red eye.
fp: Is browner than the male.

mp: The male has a black collar and bib, white cheeks, and a white circular area on the nape surrounded by a chestnut border.
fp: The female has duller plumage.

mp: The male has a brown crown and nape with dark speckles, a whitish supercilium, throat and neck with brown streaks, an upper breast that is chestnut with a blackish collar, and a lower breast that is brown.
fp: The female is smaller and a little duller than the male.

mp: Adult males have a pale gray face with a whitish supercilium, black crown and nape, greenish olive back, rufous-chestnut rump, and pale gray throat and breast.
fp: Adult females have an olive-brown crown, nape, and eyeline, a pale gray supercilium, and dark olive-brown wings with at most a trace of chestnut at the bend.

mp: Adult males have a chestnut head, brown back, rump, and wings with fine black vermiculation on the rump, and rufous throat and undersides.
fp: Adult females have a dusky brown crown and dark gray breast and belly.

mp: Mostly brown with white and black belly patterning, a black chin patch, and a prominent red comb above the eyes.
fp: Mostly brown with white and black belly patterning, lacking a black chin patch, and having a less prominent red comb above the eyes.

mp: Adult males have a black face and throat with a pale blue eye ring, metallic green crown, back, and upper breast, and black and white patterned flight feathers and tail.
Adult males have a dark gray crown with a white stripe, blue-gray upperparts, black wings with white edges, and whitish throat and underparts.
fp: Adult females have a slightly darker crown, grayish green upperparts, yellowish flight feather edges, a blacker tail, and a slight yellow cast on the belly.

mp: The male has a dark gray mantle, gray lower back with a brown wash, and a dark brown rump with dusky bars.
fp: The female is similar but the brownish wash extends to the head.

mp: A small, plain dark tinamou with dark brown upperparts, a blackish crown, slate-grey neck sides, whitish throat, indistinct dusky barring, and red legs.
fp: Darker than the male with coarser barring on wing-coverts and breast, and grey flanks.

mp: Males have a red crown with black feather bases that show through.
fp: The female has a dark olive-brown crown.

mp: The male has almost entirely white plumage with a black face and throat.
fp: The female has entirely black plumage.

mp: Adult males have a glossy black crown, white forehead and lores, pearl-gray cheeks, and light grayish underparts.
fp: Adult females have a dark chestnut-rufous crown, light buffy cinnamon face, and bright cinnamon-rufous upperparts.

mp: Males have a black hood, distinct blue bill, narrow head, pale brown backs and tails, white under-tail plumage bordered by black, and pink underbellies.
fp: Females are differentiated from males by not having pink underbellies.

mp: Males have brownish upperparts, green wings, tawny underparts, and long white-tipped inner tail feathers.
fp: Females are similar to males but have a paler throat and longer central tail feathers.

mp: The adult male has mainly grayish upperparts with a slate-gray head marked with a cinnamon crescent under the eye and supercilium, two white wingbars, and a chestnut patch across the center of the back.
fp: The adult female is paler than the male.

mp: Males are largely green with a yellow-green belly, bright lemon-yellow undertail, a narrow white and black band at the upper edge of the yellow belly, a white chin stripe, and silvery-green barring on the wings.
fp: Females are largely green with a green belly and yellow restricted to the undertail, and have duller, less obvious white and black bands, white chin stripes, and silvery-green barring on the wings.

mp: Adult males are entirely black except for white underwing coverts.
fp: Adult females have a black head, throat, and upper breast with cinnamon-rufous wings and tail.

mp: The male has bright scarlet cheeks, throat, breast, and upper abdomen, with a dark purple crown, lime green and red nape, greenish wings and back, and a purple lower abdomen.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a paler crown that has a greenish hue posteriorly.

mp: The male has dark shining green upperparts, an iridescent green gorget and upper breast, a glittering indigo blue belly, and glittering red and copper undertail coverts.
fp: The female has mostly white underparts with green dots on the throat and breast, and reddish bronze spots on the flanks and belly.

mp: Males in breeding plumage are brilliant blue and black above and variably bright yellow below, with extraordinary blue and green facial caruncles.
fp: Females are dull blue-green above, lack caruncles and are variably yellowish below.

mp: Adult males are bright blue with a black line through the eye, black tail and wing edges, and bright white underparts and throat.
fp: Females are slightly duller with off-white underparts featuring a pale orange or light buffy wash and wings tinged greenish.

mp: The male has yellow eyes.
fp: The female has dark brown or grey eyes.

mp: Males have golden-green to bronze-green crown and nape, emerald green throat and breast, and outer tail feathers with reddish bronze to rufous tips.
fp: Females resemble males but have white bases to chin feathers and bronze rather than rufous tips on the outermost tail feathers.

mp: Adult males have a warm sepia-brown crown, black face with pale gray supercilium, and mostly black throat and underparts.
fp: Adult females have a white face and throat with black feather tips and an orange to amber-brown breast.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and nape, a white supercilium, a thin black streak through the eye, and white ear coverts.
fp: Adult females have a rusty brown forehead, a black streak behind the eye, and a black crown and nape with white streaks.

mp: The male has a dusky red head with a prominent scarlet crest, red upper parts fading to brownish red, bright red throat and chest, and gray underparts.
fp: The female is similar to the male but duller, has less gray, and possesses a smaller crest.

mp: Adult males have a mostly pale olive head, upperparts, and tail with a blackish crown, dusky cheeks, and bright yellow throat and underparts.
fp: Adult females have a paler head with wider pale-yellow crown edges, a faint supercilium, and paler yellow underparts than males.

mp: The male has bright yellow upperparts, a concealed crest of dark-buff feathers, and brownish black lores and underparts.
fp: The female is plain olive brownish above and light brownish below.

mp: The adult male has glossy crimson plumage on the head, back, and breast with long, stiff feathers, and dark brown to black wings and tail.
fp: The female has a paler crimson head, throat, and underparts, with dark brown back, wings, and tail, and more flexible feathers.

mp: The male has olive green crown, back, wings, tail and flanks, a grey belly, black throat and face, with a white submoustachial stripe and grey stripe above the eye.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a white throat and belly instead of black.

mp: Adult males have a glossy bluish black crown, gray upperparts, black wings with white edges, and whitish to pale gray underparts.
fp: Adult females have a chestnut-brown crown with a wide black band below it, a white stripe above the eye, and a black stripe through the eye.

mp: The adult male has grey plumage, often darker on the head, with a blackish upper wing and rump, bare red facial skin, and a single broad white tail bar.
fp: The adult female has slightly higher weight and bolder ventral barring compared to the male.

mp: Males have gray upperparts, black bars on the tail, and underparts evenly barred grayish and white.
fp: Females resemble the Grenada form of hook-billed kite, with brown barring on the underparts that is less rufescent.

mp: The three outer pairs of tail feathers are tipped with white.
fp: The three outer pairs of tail feathers are tipped with buff.

mp: Males exhibit vibrant dark pink plumage with a contrasting lighter throat and eyebrow stripe.
fp: Females are subdued dark brown with conspicuous light-colored wingbars and lack streaking on the underparts.

mp: The male has a silvery forecrown and supercilium set off by a black mask, dark gray upper parts washed with brown, and an orange-red rump with dusky bars.
fp: The female is similar but has a smaller and duller diadem and darker brown wash on the upper parts.

mp: The male has mainly dark gray upperparts and paler gray underparts, with buff flanks marked by dark bars.
fp: The female is browner than the male.
The female has distinct plumage that differs from the male, separating the species from the blue jewel-babbler.

mp: The adult male has a glittering golden green forehead, a long dark rufous crest, glittering emerald green throat, and long white cheek tufts with shiny green dots.
fp: The adult female lacks the male's crest and cheek tufts, has a rufous throat with a grayish green lower border, and bronze tail with rufous tips.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and nape, pale grayish ear coverts, dark gray back and rump with black patches, and pale gray throat and underparts.
fp: Adult females have a rufous crown and nape and buffy underparts, but are otherwise like males.

mp: Males have a small tuft of violet feathers on their upper flank.
fp: Females have a small tuft of white feathers on their upper flank.

mp: The male has a glittering blue-green to golden green forehead, velvety black crown, face, and mantle, with a large cobalt-blue spot on the lower throat.
fp: The female has a green crown, face, and upper back with blackish feather tips creating a scaly effect, and a bright cinnamon buff throat with green spots.

mp: The adult male is almost entirely black with brownish or gray tones.
fp: The adult female is almost entirely black with brownish or gray tones.

mp: The males have a dark purple patch on the belly and tend to have a gray patch on both sides of their upper breasts.
fp: The females look similar but lack these patches.

mp: Adult males have a bluish gray crown.
fp: Adult females have an olive crown.

mp: The adult male has a central black line over the crown and nape, rufescent buff plumage with black margins, black lores and face, and white barred supercilial feathers.
Males are mostly glossy black with a partially hidden white patch between their scapulars and blackish gray underwing coverts.
fp: Females have a dark reddish brown crown, upperparts, and wings with a partially hidden white interscapular patch, brownish black tail, and buff throat and breast.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and back with white streaks, a white interscapular patch, rufous rump and flanks, and white underparts with heavy black streaks.
fp: Females have a cinnamon-rufous and black streaked crown, lack the white interscapular patch, and have rufous-buff areas where the male has white.

mp: The male has an iridescent golden green breast shield, elongated black plumes, three erectile spatule head-wires behind each blue iris eye, and golden brown nasal tuft feathers.
fp: The female is smaller than the male, with brown plumage and black barred below.

mp: Adult males have green speculum and longer central rectrices.
fp: Adult females have brown speculum and shorter central rectrices.

mp: Adult males have a black cap with tiny yellow spots on the forehead and tiny white ones on the rest of it.
fp: Adult females are identical to males but have whitish spots on their entire crown.

mp: The male has grey plumage with a brown nape and rump, brown barring on the flanks, and a blackish tail.
fp: The female's underparts are browner than those of the male.

mp: The adult male is predominantly green with red breast and cheeks, yellow ear coverts, and a yellowish crown.
fp: The adult female is similar but has a wider blue-black band on the otherwise green-yellow breast.

mp: Adult males have a mostly green head with a red forehead and lores, green upperparts, and a maroon tail with a green base.
fp: Females are almost the same as males but with much reduced red on the forehead.

mp: Males have a black crown, nape, and mask with a creamy supercilium, olive-brown back, and an upper chest that is dark chestnut fading to tawny.
fp: Females have a sooty crown (or olive-brown in one subspecies) and lack the dark chestnut coloration on the chest found in males.

mp: The male has a red rear part of the crown and a red nape.
fp: The female lacks the red crown and nape, having a black crown and nape instead.

mp: The male has an extensive dark emerald green face and throat, two very long tail wires and large white ornamental flank plumes.
fp: The female has an all brown plumage, is smaller in size, and has no ornamental plumes.

mp: Males have a blue and black plumage, with light royal blue crowns, black forehead and lores, deep turquoise-blue upper back, and navy blue throats and underparts.
fp: Females have blue and black plumage only on their heads, with the rest of the body being rusty brown and having a black tail tipped with white.

mp: Adult males are mostly dark gray with a white patch between scapulars, darker wings and tail, and black wing coverts with white tips.
fp: Adult females have a dark gray head and neck, dark reddish brown upperparts, barred throat, dark gray breast, and ochre-brown belly.

mp: Males have a bright purple throat.
fp: Females have yellowish-brown underparts, a dark greyish-black back, head, and tail, green chest patches, and a white postocular stripe.

mp: The male has a red head, nape, breast, and underparts, with dark green back and wings, and a purplish spot on the crown.
fp: The female is similar but has a yellowish-green lower back and yellow sides on the rump and flanks.

mp: The male is lighter-colored and smaller than the female.
fp: The female is darker-colored and bigger than the male.

mp: Adult males have a black crown, white supercilium, wide black eye band, speckled white cheeks, reddish yellow-brown upperparts, and rufous throat and underparts.
fp: Females are paler than males, with olive streaks on the crown, rufous wing covert tips, and no white interscapular patch.

mp: Adult males have a bright chestnut crown, upperparts, and flight feathers, black wing coverts with pale tips, a rufous-brown tail, and black face, throat, and breast.
fp: Adult females are similar but have a white chin and throat, a light gray belly instead of black, and a paler crissum.

mp: Adult males have a golden crown and nape with a red stripe, olive face, rosy rufous to maroon upperparts, olive tail and wings with white and black spots, and a whitish throat with streaked underparts.
fp: Adult females have olive upperparts, a pale grayish throat, and dull pale olive underparts with blurry streaking and a yellowish tinge on the belly.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and nape with wide reddish orange tips on the forecrown feathers and white spots on the rest.
fp: Adult females are identical to males but have white spots on the whole crown and lack red coloration.

mp: Males possess a blue patch around the lower section of the beak.
fp: Females have a pink patch around the lower section of the beak.

mp: The male has a red crown and nape.
fp: The female has a black crown and nape.

mp: The male is mostly black above with a yellow "V" on the mantle, a red crown and nape, yellow wingbars, and a yellow throat and breast brightening to gold or orange on the belly with black-spotted flanks.
fp: The female is black above but heavily streaked with gold, and its throat, breast, and belly are colored like the male's but have black spots throughout.

mp: The male has flame orange and golden yellow plumage, elongated neck plumes, and a yellow-tipped black tail.
fp: The female is an olive brown bird with yellow or golden around the stomach.

mp: Pale gray from the belly to the sides of the chest and neck, with a sooty back and cheek, an orange chest patch with dark red below, and a pink crown and mark across the flight feathers.
fp: Has more pronounced green on tail, rump and wings.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black head with a hidden red crown stripe, white throat, dark olive upperparts, and chestnut to cinnamon-rufous underparts.
fp: Adult females lack red on the crown, have a dark olive head with a gray throat, grayish olive flanks, and cinnamon-buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have a mostly gray face, black throat with white spots, brown-tinged dark gray crown and back, and reddish yellow-brown lower parts.
fp: Adult females have a mostly yellow-ochre face, throat, and underparts with darker mottling, and olive-brown upperparts.

mp: The male has a red crown with an orange forehead.
fp: The female has a black crown.

mp: Males have small white spots on the four outer primaries and white tips on their two outer tail feathers.
fp: Females have 3 to 4 smaller white spots on their outer primaries and lack white on their outer tail feathers.

mp: Predominantly black and white with an all-white breast, black wings and head, white throat, nape, shoulders, and rump, a bare skin eye-ring, and a bright blue wattle.
fp: Similar to the male but has white lores and chin.

mp: Males are mostly glossy black with a large patch of black and white feathers between their scapulars and blackish gray underwing coverts.
fp: Females have yellowish brown upperparts and wings with no interscapular patch, olive-tinged gray faces, and olive-brown underparts.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with irregular thin white bars everywhere but the throat.
fp: Adult females are mostly rich cinnamon with wavy black bars and darker cinnamon-rufous forehead and crest.

mp: Adult males have a red hindcrown and nape, along with an indistinct, narrow moustachial stripe.
fp: Adult females lack red on the head.

mp: Adult males have a glossy dark violaceous steel-blue body with black wings and tail featuring a faint bluish or greenish sheen.
fp: Females have a mostly black head and upperparts with a sooty crown and rump, plus a strong violaceous steel-blue gloss on the back and scapulars.

mp: The male has a dark green head and upperparts, a mauve belly, a bright yellow breast band bordered by white, and bold lime-yellow bare skin around the eyes.
fp: The female is almost entirely green with yellow fringes to the belly feathers.

mp: It has a brown head, blue crown, light blue ear covert, yellow breast, green body and blue tail, with red eyes.
fp: It has less brown than the male.

mp: Adult males have a rufous-coloured chin and throat, black lores, and are uniformly brownish-grey with a red iris and black stubby bill.
fp: Adult females have a pale grey throat, a white ring around the eye, lightly streaked underparts, and are uniformly brownish-grey with a red iris and black stubby bill.

mp: Adult males are glossy black with a slight bluish sheen on the head, upperparts, wings, and tail, and have pure white throat and underparts.
fp: Adult females have blackish crowns with chestnut-brown tips, a pale gray face and upper back, blackish wings with cinnamon-brown edges, and white throat and underparts.

mp: The adult male has bronzy green upperparts, a black tail with rufous edges, a pinkish red gorget, a white foreneck and breast center, and buffy to cinnamon underparts with green spangles.
fp: The adult female is bronzy green above with green central tail feathers and rufous-based outer tail feathers, a pale buff throat with grayish speckles, and underparts similar to the male's.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with a usually concealed white patch between their scapulars.
fp: Adult females have a blackish gray forecrown, lores, and face, with rufous-brown crown, upperparts, and wings, a white throat, and light cinnamon underparts.

mp: The adult male has a glossy black head and throat, a bright orange-yellow breast center, and a prominent gold ring around olive-green cheeks.
fp: The adult female is similar but has narrower, more greenish-yellow facial markings, a duller yellow breast, and duller green and blue shades on the back and wings.

mp: Males have a red crown with grayish black feather bases that show through.
fp: The female has a brown crown with a green tinge and whitish yellow spots on the rear.

mp: Adult males have a greenish gold crown and nape, green head and upper back, yellow-green lower back, blackish wings and tail with green edges, green chin and breast, and yellow belly.
fp: Adult females have an entirely green head and upperparts and are otherwise like males.

mp: The male has a small golden patch with black flecking on the crown, most noticeable in display.
fp: The female lacks the golden crown patch and is otherwise similar to the male with brown forehead, whitish cheeks and throat, and brown underparts with white spotting.

mp: The male is rufous brown with an elongated golden crest extending from its golden forehead, dark grey feet and buffish yellow underparts.
fp: The female is an unadorned olive brown bird.

mp: Mainly green with a rose red spot above the eye, an orange collar, grey upper wing coverts, and elongated racket-shaped central tail feathers.
fp: Similar to the male but lacks the red spot and orange collar, has greener upper wing coverts, and a shorter tail.

mp: The male has a slate-grey back, tail, wing, cap and back of the neck, and a bright yellow face, throat, breast and belly.
fp: The female differs from the male by having a dusky patch on the face.

mp: The male has yellow and dark green plumage with a lavender grey breast, large crimson ornamental flank plumes, and two long tail wires.
fp: The unadorned female has an olive-brown plumage with cinnamon-brown below.

mp: It has a red plumage on the crown.
fp: The red plumage on the crown is less extensive.

mp: The male has intense dark blue plumage with blacker tail and wings.
fp: The female is greyish-brownish with fine white streaks on the underparts, a greyish-blue rump, and white wing feather tips.

mp: Adult males have dark gray upperparts with a small white patch between their scapulars, blackish gray tail with wide white spots, and wings with a brown tinge and faint white spots.
fp: Females have olive-brown crown and upperparts, a minimal white interscapular patch, grayer rump, darker wings with pale yellowish olive tips, and olive-yellow underparts with dusky flanks.

mp: Adult males have a mottled whitish and gray face, dark grayish brown crown, yellowish red-brown back and rump, and black throat and breast with a gray border.
fp: Adult females have upperparts like the male's but with larger white spots on the wing coverts, and their throat, breast, and belly are mostly white with a blackish scaly appearance.

mp: Adult males have a gray head, neck, and mantle, with olive-brown upperparts, black wing coverts with white tips, and a black center on the throat and breast.
fp: Adult females have a paler gray head, streaked gray or olive-gray throat and breast on white, and a whiter belly than males.

mp: Adult males have a glossy black breast band, bluish black head, and white underparts.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have a chestnut or rufous breast band instead of black.

mp: Males have a prominent dark crown of feathers on the top of the head.
fp: Females have a fully rusty coloured head and markings on their backs and wings.

mp: Adult males have a mostly olive head with blackish lores, yellow flecks on the ear coverts, a thin pale eye-ring, and a partially hidden black crest in the middle of the crown.
fp: Adult females have little or no crest on the crown.

mp: Adult males have an olive-green crown, dull grayish face, olive-green upperparts with a yellower rump, and olive-yellow underparts.
fp: Females are smaller with duller, more yellow body plumage, grayer wings, and a more delicate bill, legs, and feet than males.

mp: Males have a yellow/green rump with a yellow tail.
fp: Females have a slight green/blue wash on their green cheeks.

mp: Males have a bronzed-green posterior, dark wings, nearly white outer tail feathers, a metallic emerald green gorget, and white underparts with a black streak.
fp: Females share a similar physique to males but are less brightly colored.

mp: Males are entirely yellow-green with paler underparts and head, and have elongated central tail feathers with bare shafts and black rackets.
fp: Females are generally darker and less yellowish, with shorter bare tail shafts.

mp: The male has a grey head, olive-green back, pale ashy grey throat and breast, yellow belly, and blackish crown.
fp: The female is slightly duller than the male and has a greyish crown.

mp: The male has a shining dark green forehead and crown, bronzy green upperparts, glittering bronze-green tail, and grass green underparts.
fp: The female has upperparts like the male, a white line behind the eye, pale grayish underparts, dark gray undertail coverts, and tail feathers with green bases, black near the end, and grayish tips.

mp: The male is a velvet black and green bird-of-paradise with black flank plumes, black curved bill, yellow mouth, blackish feet, dark brown iris, and iridescent greenish blue on its crown, throat, breast shield and central tail feathers.
fp: The female is a rufous brown bird with barred buff below.

mp: Males were glossy blue-black above.
fp: Females were brownish-gray.

mp: The male has a bluish gray head, back, and breast, a broken white eye ring, black inner tail feathers, white outer tail feathers, and a white throat and belly.
fp: The female is similar but has a paler gray coloration and possesses a white supercilium.

mp: Adult males have a black and white streaked face, black crown, back, and rump with thin white streaks, and a large white patch between the shoulders.
fp: Adult females have an orange-buff face, cinnamon-rufous crown and nape with black streaks, and mostly plain underparts with a buff tinge.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with a white central streak and supercilium, olive-gray upperparts with a speckled interscapular patch, and a rufous rump.
fp: Females have the same pattern but different colors, with a crown streaked with pale buff and a small or absent interscapular patch.

mp: The male has a blue crown, black-and-yellow underparts, a black head, and warm brown upperparts.
fp: The female has a brown crown and buffy-whitish underparts.

mp: Adult males have an olive-tinged gray crest, olive-brown upperparts, black lores, face, and throat, and dark olive-brown underparts.
fp: Adult females are like males but have short black bars with cinnamon-rufous edges on their upper back feathers and wing coverts.

mp: Adult males have a glossy bluish black head, bright grass green upperparts and tail, and bright yellow underparts with a deep orange triangular patch on the upper breast.
fp: Adult females have a green to greenish yellow head and throat, with bright grass green upperparts and tail.

mp: Adult males have a dark brownish crown, rufous-chestnut crest and nape, olive-brown upperparts with rufous wing edges, black face and throat, and a rufous-chestnut breast center.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but have buff-edged black tips on upperpart feathers and wing coverts, plus black and pale buff banding on their sides and lower breast.

mp: A grey-brown bird with a red bill and tail, and red bare skin around the eyes.
fp: Similar to the male but paler in color with a more extensive buff belly.

mp: Adult males have a red malar patch extending down to the throat and around the back of the head to meet the crest.
fp: Females have the red crest but no other red on their head.

mp: The forehead and crown are crimson-purple with a narrow yellow border, throat and back of head are white, nape and chest are light gray, stomach is bright yellow, back and wings are darker green with yellow edges, and feet are bright pink.
fp: The crown is a darker green color, and the wings and chest have yellow margins, while the rest of the appearance is largely the same as the male.

mp: The male has a large back marking over the crown down the face to the chin with a bluish-grey neck and a chestnut band on the lower chest separated from the white belly by a thin black band.
fp: The female is much more of a subdued brownish color overall, with no bold black markings and has a face lined with faint slate-gray markings.

mp: Breeding males have a blackish crown, blackish face, dark mottled breast sides, and a blackish bill.
fp: Breeding females are lighter in color with less streaking and have a pale pinkish bill.

mp: The male is dark grey with bleak streaks and a white forehead and supercilium.
fp: The female is brownish with dark streaks and greyish brow.

mp: The three outer pairs of tail feathers are broadly tipped with white.
fp: The three outer pairs of tail feathers are broadly tipped with buff.

mp: Males have bronze-green upperparts with a coppery hue on the crown and rump, dark gray underparts with a whitish scaly throat and breast, and leg puffs that are white on the outside and chestnut on the inside.
fp: Females are similar but duller overall and their leg puffs are entirely white.

mp: Adult males have an entirely black head, neck, and upper breast with a thin yellow collar, chestnut-tinged brown back, and yellow underparts below the upper breast.
fp: Adult females are overall duller with an olive wash on the head and body, and faint olive bars on the breast.

mp: The male has a black head, neck, and lower breast with a small white tuft behind the eye, brown upper parts, gray flanks, and a white belly.
fp: The female has an extensive rufous crown, brown back, and pale gray face, throat, and underside.

mp: Males have bright shimmery green upperparts, a large forehead tuft covering most of the bill, indigo blue breast, azure blue belly, and black markings on the head and wings.
fp: Females have smaller forehead tufts, paler olive-tinted upperparts, lime-green underparts with sky blue undertail coverts, lime green eye-rings, and lack black head markings except for a spot in front of the eye.

mp: Males have medium gray upperparts with an olive-brown tinge, blackish gray wings and tail with wide white tips on the wing coverts, and paler gray throat and underparts.
fp: Females have a brown crown and upperparts, blackish brown wings and tail with pale cinnamon-rufous tips on the wing coverts, a gray face, and pale tawny throat and belly.

mp: Adult males have a deep blue forehead and throat, dull dark blue-green crown, metallic green to bronze-green upperparts, and white underparts.
fp: Adult females have a blue crown, metallic green to bronze-green upperparts, and mostly white underparts.

mp: Males have black head and breast with velvety-blue iridescence, a coppery-orange gorget, and long purplish-black tail feathers.
fp: Females are mainly a dull brownish black.

mp: Adult males have dark gray upperparts with a hidden white patch, black lower cheeks, throat, and breast, and paler gray underparts.
fp: Adult females of the nominate subspecies have blue-gray upperparts, a whitish throat, and pale buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with a white central streak and supercilium, olive-gray upperparts with a speckled interscapular patch, rufous rump, and deep rufous belly and undertail coverts.
fp: Females have the same pattern but different colors, with a crown streaked with pale buff and a small or absent interscapular patch.

mp: The male has a glittering reddish purple forehead and gorget, iridescent green upperparts, whitish breast, mixed rufous and green belly, and a deeply forked tail with lyre-shaped outer feathers.
fp: The female has dull green upperparts, a pale gray chin and throat with small green spots, a whitish chest, rufous belly, and a rounded tail with a wide black band near the end.

mp: A very small black and white bird with a white underside, broad black breast band, black head with a conspicuous white loral spot, and bright yellow eye.
fp: Similar to the male but has a thin white supercilium.

mp: The male has rufous brown upperparts with blackish streaks, a rufous chin and throat, and a buff belly with large whitish spots.
fp: The female is similar but less rufous overall, with more heavily spotted underparts and buffy tail feather tips.

mp: The male is highly distinctive, with a broad blue-green band across a white chest.
fp: The female is very different, with an all-orange belly and overall duller, darker coloration.

mp: The upper parts are a mixture of brown, grey, buff and white, spotted with black, with a white stripe above the eye and a white semi-collar.
fp: Female birds are rather tawnier and brighter than males.

mp: Adult males are entirely sooty black.
fp: Adult females have mostly dark olive-brown upperparts with rufous uppertail coverts, wing bars, and streaked underparts.

mp: Adult males have a blackish brown crown, yellow forecrown, rufous-brown upperparts, dusky wings with two bold wing bars, gray throat and breast, and rufous-tinged gray belly.
fp: Adult females have buffier underparts than males, especially on the lower belly.

mp: The male is almost entirely cinnamon-orange with an iridescent fiery reddish yellow forehead and crown, and dark coppery gray wings.
fp: The female has bluish green upperparts with an iridescent bluish purple crown, pure white underparts with black and green disks, and slaty green wings.

mp: Adult males have brown upperparts with blackish and buff markings, whitish underparts with black barring, and a dark reddish-brown face with a buffy-white moustachial stripe.
fp: Females have a similar pattern but with pinkish-brown underparts, more uniform wings, and duller moustachial stripes.

mp: Adult males have a bright red malar patch and some red behind the eye and onto the crest.
fp: Females do not have any bright red on the head.

mp: Adult males have a large orange-red patch on the crown bordered in black on an otherwise bright olive head.
fp: Females have a smaller orange-red patch on the crown compared to males.

mp: Adult males have a black crown and back with thin white streaks, a rufous rump, black flight feathers with buff edges, and bright tawny orange flanks and crissum.
fp: Females are overall duller with fainter, sparser streaking, featuring a crown and nape streaked with rufous and black, olive upperparts, and a dull cinnamon-buff belly.

mp: Adult males have a black and white streaked face, black crown, back, and rump with white streaks, and white underparts with black streaks.
fp: Adult females have buff streaks on the head and upperparts, with buff underparts marked by black streaks mostly on the breast and sides.

mp: The male has a mouse gray head, back, and breast with white underparts, and a tail with black innermost feathers and white outermost feathers.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a paler face.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with small white spots on their crown, nape, upperparts, and sides.
fp: Adult females are mostly brownish black with a rufous forehead and crown, pale buff spots on upperparts, and buffy white underparts.

mp: The male has a yellow bill, whitish eye, blackish face, chin, and throat, with iridescent green crown, nape, upperparts, and breast, and rosy red belly and vent.
fp: The female replaces the male's green with slaty gray, has an olive tint to the breast, and a dark maxilla.

mp: Velvet black with silvery white forehead crest, iridescent purple blue nape, golden green breast plumes, and ornamental spatule head wires.
fp: Brown with dark head, yellow iris, and dark-barred yellowish brown below.

mp: Male shows more white with pale blue confined to the belly.
fp: Female has a white throat and pale blue breast and belly.

mp: Adult males have a medium gray crown, back, and rump, medium gray wing coverts with white tips, dusky flight feathers, a gray tail, pale gray underparts, and a black bill.
fp: Adult females have a medium brownish gray to olive gray crown, back, and rump, olive brown wings with pale buff tips, a gray or dusky tail, pale buff underparts, and a black maxilla with a gray mandible.

mp: Males have white tips on some other wing feathers in addition to the general brown upperparts with gray, rufous, and buff spots.
fp: Females have brown upperparts with gray, rufous, and buff spots, whitish or buff underparts with brown bars, and a narrow white patch on the throat.

mp: The central tail feathers have narrow pale tips that are white.
fp: The central tail feathers have narrow pale tips that are buff.

mp: Males are largely buff-colored with purplish-chestnut crowns, blackish masks, and blue-green-edged blackish wings.
