mp: The male has green cheeks and neck with a bluish tinge and a tail edged with a broad band of yellow.
fp: The female has all red plumage, royal blue primaries, yellow under-tail coverts, and a broad yellow band edging the tail.

mp: Males have a silver patch below their necks on each side of their bodies.
fp: Females lack the silver patches but have white on their lower body.

mp: Males are mostly glossy black with a partially hidden white patch between their scapulars and blackish gray underwing coverts.
fp: Females are mostly rufous-brown with a brown-tinged black head and a partially hidden white interscapular patch.

mp: The male has a metallic olive green crown and back with reddish edges, a rich reddish rump, blackish face, and a throat that is black becoming rufous on the neck, chest, and belly.
fp: The female is similar but has a paler rump and buffy olive underparts with a reddish tinge.

mp: Males have a hidden yellow patch on the crown.
fp: Females have a cinnamon-brown patch on the crown.

mp: The male has wide white tips on the three outermost tail feathers.
fp: The female has narrow buff bands on the tips of the tail feathers instead of wide white ones.

mp: Males have a black head, nape, chin, throat, and belly, with green upperparts, a yellow band on the lower neck, and yellow to rusty flanks.
fp: Females have the same bill pattern as males but with a shorter bill, and share the pale blue eye skin and yellow to tawny tuft behind it.

mp: Males have bronzy green upperparts and glittering green underparts, with a green tail featuring a wide white band at the base and white tips.
fp: Females are smaller with dull white underparts heavily dotted with golden-green, especially on the breast.

mp: Adult males have a wide orange-chestnut collar encircling the neck, upper breast, chin, throat, and most of the face, with sooty black plumage.
fp: Adult females are similar to males but some have a paler breast with brown mixed in.

mp: Males have distinguishably longer tails.
fp: Females have chestnut flanks.

mp: Adult males have olive-greenish upper parts, yellow underparts, yellowish-green rumps, yellow supercilium, and yellowish-green wing and tail feathers.
fp: Adult females have black streaking on darker greyish-green upper parts, more defined wing-bars, paler yellowish throats, and black-flanked breasts with streaking.

mp: Adult males have dark brown to black upper parts, a white or pale gray throat and belly, and a dark facial appearance contrasting with lighter underparts.
fp: Females exhibit a paler and browner coloration with dark-colored underparts and less distinct markings.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead with short white streaks, a black crown and nape, a long white supercilium, and a black streak behind the eye.
fp: Adult females have a buff tinge on their forehead, a black crown with white spots, and light buff breast and sides.

mp: The male has an entirely black head and throat.
fp: The female has yellow underparts.

mp: Males have a bill with a small hook at the tip and more prominent tooth-like spikes, and their plumage color averages brighter overall than females.
fp: Females have a duller plumage color compared to males, lacking the hooked bill tip and prominent spikes found in males.

mp: Males have a turquoise-green to emerald green throat, a greeny-bronze breast, a dark green belly, and dark undertail coverts.
fp: Females have duller upperparts than males, gray underparts, and a tail with white tips on the outermost two pairs of feathers.

mp: Adult males are usually dark gray above and lighter gray below, with dark reddish brown flanks and crissum with dusky bars.
fp: The female is similar to the male but paler with a dark brown wash.

mp: The adult male has iridescent blackish plumage glossed with blue, green, and purple, along with elongated horn-like head tufts and loose neck feathers.
fp: The adult female resembles the male but is smaller in size and duller in color.

mp: The male has a broad tawny or cinnamon collar on the hindneck, a small white patch on the throat, white bands on the wing, and white bands and tips on the tail.
fp: The female's throat is buff, the bands on the wing are buff, and the tail usually has no white.

mp: The adult male is dark gray above and lighter gray below, with a very light brownish wash on the flanks.
fp: The female is paler overall, with a brown wash on the rump and tawny flanks and crissum barred with black.

mp: Adult males have deep turquoise-blue upperparts, black wings with blue edges, a black tail with turquoise-blue uppertail coverts, and purple chin, throat, breast, and upper belly.
fp: Adult females are larger than males, with mostly dark brown upperparts featuring buffish white scalloped tips, dusky brown wings and tail, and pale buff underparts with grayish brown spots.

mp: The male has a predominantly green plumage with a turquoise tinted throat and shimmering golden green upperparts and underparts.
fp: The female lacks the throat patches, has less light plumage, and a more golden belly.

mp: Adult males have an olive crown with a mostly hidden yellow or orange patch in the middle.
fp: Females lack the yellow or orange patch on the crown found in males.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with irregular thin white bars everywhere but the throat.
fp: Adult females are mostly cinnamon with wavy black bars, rufous and black forehead and crest, and a black tail with thin gray bars.

mp: The male is gray, darker above and lighter below, with a rear that sometimes has a slightly light brown wash.
fp: The female is similar to the male but the brown wash on its rear is more often darker.

mp: Adult males have medium gray upperparts with a blacker crown, black wings, and a black tail with white tips.
fp: Adult females have a dark rufous crown and nape, gray face with white streaks, dark olive-brown upperparts, and tawny underparts.

mp: The male is entirely black.
fp: The female is dark gray above and somewhat lighter gray below with little of no brown on the flanks.

mp: Males have a black hood.
fp: Females have only a black cap.

mp: The male has a dark slate-grey crown, face and nape, a white throat, ochraceous-yellow belly and rump, and olive back and wings with a black line between the throat and belly.
fp: The female is duller with a buff belly and rump, no line between the throat and belly, and an olive-brown head, back and wings.

mp: Adult males have a black cap with a red patch on the forehead and top, white spots on the hindcrown and nape, and a face mostly dark brown.
Males have a glittering golden- to emerald green central crown, a velvety blackish supercilium, and a glittering violet-blue patch on the upper throat.
fp: Females are generally duller with less iridescence and lack the black supercilium.

mp: Adult males are almost entirely glossy blue-black with a small bushy crest.
fp: Adult females are mostly glossy blue-black but lack a crest and have a black-streaked chestnut throat.

mp: Males have a dark glittering green crown, shining green back, glittering blue gorget, bronzy green underparts with puffy white thighs, and very long deep violet to blue outer tail feathers.
fp: Females have a glittering blue crown, upperparts similar to males, white throat, breast, and belly with green spots, and a short slightly forked blue-green tail with white tips.

mp: Adult males have a white throat and chin with black streaks, and reddish brown plumage with large white marks on the breast, belly, and flanks.
fp: The female has paler brown underparts with less conspicuous white marks.

mp: The adult male has a velvety black head with a white loral spot and narrow supercilium, a white collar, velvety-black mantle and back, very black wings with a white wingstripe, black tail with white outer feathers, and a glossy black breast band on white underparts.
fp: The female is similar to the male but has a smaller loral spot and supercilium and a narrower dark grey breast band.

mp: The male has a broad, greatly elongated tail of twelve feathers with coverts up to 1.73 m long, giving a total length of 1.9–2.39 m.
fp: The female has a prominent marbled barring, more colourful dorsal plumage, a different crest with rigid plumes, and considerably shorter tails averaging 74–75 cm.

mp: The male has dark gray upper parts, medium gray chest merging to pale gray belly, reddish brown rump with faint bars, and cinnamon flanks and vent area with faint bars.
fp: The female has paler gray upper parts, a brown wash on the neck, brighter reddish brown flanks without bars.

mp: Adult males have a grayish mauve crown, grayish white face, iridescent purple to amethyst hindneck and shoulders, brown upperparts with purple wash, and white throat and breast with a purple tinge.
fp: Adult females are duller with purple gloss confined to the hindneck and shoulders, pale gray face and throat, brownish neck and breast with a purple tint, and brown eyes.

mp: Adult males have shining grass green upperparts, a glittering emerald green gorget with a violet blue patch on the breast, and grayish buff underparts with golden-green spots.
fp: Adult females are shining grass green above with mostly grayish underparts that have green spots on the chest and a rufescent belly center.

mp: The adult male has dark olive green upper- and underparts, a purple-violet gorget, and a slightly forked tail that is iridescent violaceous sky blue above and glittering yellow-green below.
fp: The adult female has dark olive green upperparts, a duller throat, whitish gray breast and belly spotted with olive green, and outer tail feathers with whitish tips on their underside.

mp: The male has pinkish underparts, a reddish-pink belly, and a reddish-pink collar.
fp: The female has white underparts, a clean white belly, and a black-and-white collar.

mp: The male has all gray upperparts with a black mask.
fp: The female has a less distinct black mask and fine black and gray barring on the throat and breast.

mp: The male has a creamy-white head and neck, a white upper chest, a reddish-brown lower chest and uppertail-coverts, and a creamy-white buff tail with a broad black tip.
fp: The female's plumage is black and its ocular skin is blue, while its tail and bill resemble those of the male.

mp: The male has an iridescent yellow-green breast shield, elongated black plumes, three erectile spatule head wires behind each eye, coppery-bronzed nasal tuft feathers and long, wedge-shaped tail feathers.
fp: The female is a rich brown bird with a blackish head.

mp: A large brownish-black megapode with a bare red facial skin, red comb, maroon rump, chestnut brown below, two elongated red wattles on the back of the head, and a long wattle on the foredeck.
fp: Similar to the male but has a smaller comb and no wattles.

mp: The forehead and crown are dull crimson, with a pale bluish-grey head, breast, and neck, green wings, and an orange belly separated by a white band.
fp: Females have less extensive red on the head and a greenish tinge to their grey parts compared to males.

mp: Predominantly green with a red bill, red throat spot, orange legs, dark red nape, and bright red rump and uppertail-coverts.
fp: Similar to the male but with the red on the throat reduced or absent.

mp: Males have reddish-pink bellies.
fp: Females have clean white bellies.

mp: Adult males have brightly coloured chicken-like combs on the forehead and single pendulous wattles hanging from the throat.
fp: Females are slightly smaller and bear less developed head ornamentation than males.

mp: The male has black underparts, an almost golden forehead, black wings with golden scapulars, and a pair of large circular pink wattles on the cheek.
fp: The female has olive green plumage and pale olive below.

mp: Males are mostly glossy black with a partially hidden white patch between their scapulars and blackish gray underwing coverts.
fp: Females have varied plumages depending on subspecies, including light rufescent brown, sooty black, or dark reddish yellow-brown upperparts with distinct facial markings.

mp: Males have a dark grey crown, black throat and lower breast with a chestnut band between them.
fp: Females have a duller orange flank, a grey center breast-band, and overall duller coloring with less contrast.

mp: The male has entirely white underparts.
The male has a blue-grey head, greyish white throat, pale cream breast, blackish belly, reddish brown hindneck, rufous back and rump, dark olive-brown tail, and a purple patch on the breast sides.
fp: The female has a rusty chestnut head, neck, and breast, with olive-brown upperparts and belly.

mp: Breeding males have gray-brown cheeks, a sooty-brown crown and underparts, mostly dark brown body with reddish-brown hints, white throat, black bill, and dull pink legs.
fp: Females often have paler feathers, a more brownish bill, and a more slender body shape than males.

mp: The male has dark green plumage with a yellow head and undertail coverts.
fp: The female lacks the yellow plumage found in the male.

mp: The adult male has a long black and white crest, a mostly black face with a wide white collar, bronzy green upperparts, and a long thin white beard.
fp: The adult female lacks the crest and beard, and has dull white underparts with dense greenish brown spots.

mp: Adult males have a black cap with a red patch on the forehead and white spots on the rest of it.
fp: Adult females are identical to males but lack the red on the forehead.

mp: Adult males are mostly glossy blue-black with a white ruff on the chin, throat, and neck.
fp: Adult females have olive-green upperparts, pale gray to grayish olive green throats, and pale yellowish bellies.

mp: Adult males have a black forehead, crown, and nape, olive-brown upperparts with rufous wing edges, and a white face, throat, and breast.
fp: Adult females have black-streaked chestnut on the crown, a rufous-chestnut nape, and buff-edged black tips on their upperparts and belly.

mp: Males have a narrow black breast band.
fp: Females have longer central tail feathers with paler tips.

mp: Males have a small golden-yellow patch on the forehead.
fp: Females lack the golden-yellow patch on the forehead.

mp: Adult male plumage is mostly dark grey above with brown and black mantle and scapulars, featuring a white tapered eyebrow and black and white streaked ear-coverts.
fp: Females are similar to males but have a rufous stripe bordering the upper edge of the eyebrow and dull white streaking tinged rufous on the centre of the upper breast.

mp: Adult males have a rufous crown, black nape, white face, olive back, black wings with white edges, black tail, and white underparts with streaky black sides.
fp: Females are overall duller than males, with dark gray neck and cheeks and wide olive edges on the flight feathers.

mp: The male has an ash brown crown, dark metallic bronzy green upper parts, a small white chin spot, a glittery green throat and chest, and a reddish chestnut belly and vent area.
fp: The female has a paler and ochraceous belly compared to the male.

mp: The adult male has relatively dull plumage consisting of brown, buff, and rufous colors with black barring, and a brilliant white crest.
fp: The female possesses more dull coloration, including narrow buff barring and pink cinnamon coloration on the underside.

mp: The male is mostly blackish above and slightly lighter below, with reddish brown flanks and vent with black bars, and a white patch on the crown.
fp: The female is paler than the male, washed with brown above, and more reddish on the flanks.

mp: Adult males have a black head with a large white patch from the bill through the ear coverts, a rich chestnut nape and upperparts, black underparts, and blackish flight feathers with a wide white bar.
fp: Adult females have a browner crown than males and some brown on their underparts, while sharing similar upperpart coloration and iris color.

mp: Adult males have a mostly gray-brown face, a black throat with white spots, gray-brown crown and upperparts, reddish tail and flight feathers, and blackish brown wing coverts with cinnamon-tinged white tips.
fp: Adult females have a mostly light olive-brown face, a cinnamon throat, and light olive-brown underparts with a variable cinnamon tinge in the center of the breast and upper belly.

mp: Mainly black with a blue rump, yellow belly patches, and a conspicuous white forehead patch.
fp: Gray and black with a pale yellow belly and a white eye ring, lacking the male's white forehead patch.

mp: Males are entirely black with an obvious white mark from the forehead down between the bill and eye.
fp: Females have dark brown underparts and an obvious white mark from the forehead down between the bill and eye.

mp: Adult males are mostly blackish gray with a white patch between their scapulars and white-edged outermost primaries.
fp: Adult females have a cinnamon-rufous crown, reddish yellow-brown upperparts, and mostly white underparts with a gray tinge.

mp: The adult male has black plumage with a white rump, upper tail coverts, and white patches on the sides of its breast.
fp: The adult female closely resembles the male but its black feathers have brown tinges.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with a small white patch on their shoulder.
fp: Adult females have a black head, neck, upper mantle, and upper breast, with rufous upperparts and cinnamon-tawny underparts.

mp: Adult males are mostly black with white spots on the wing coverts and underwing coverts, and a blackish gray lower belly.
fp: Adult females are entirely deep reddish brown.

mp: The adult male is all shiny black except for white shoulders, with a black bill and black or dark brown feet and eyes.
fp: The female bears a pied plumage, with black upperparts contrasting with white shoulders and underparts.

mp: Adult males are mostly dark gray with a hidden white patch between the scapulars, dark gray wings with white tips, and a blackish gray breast.
fp: Adult females have a reddish brown crown, nape, upperparts, wings, and tail, with gray sides, throat, and underparts marked by bold white streaks.

mp: Adult males have a mostly glossy purplish black head and body with white tail and most wing feathers.
fp: Adult females have an ash-gray head and upperparts, darker gray wings and tail with white outer edges, and paler gray underparts with darker mottling.

mp: Male white-tailed swallows have brighter blue and white plumage, with blue-black coloration.
fp: Females have duller coats with less vibrant coloration, tending to have more blue-grey plumage.

mp: Adult males are mostly gray with a white supercilium, ear coverts, chin, and throat, and wings darker than their back.
fp: Adult females have a dark olive-brown crown, rufous nape and throat, olive-brown upper back, and rufous flight feathers.

mp: The male has blue-black upperparts, a white throat and upper breast, and yellow lower breast and belly.
fp: The female is duller, with olive-brown upperparts.

mp: Males have lighter rufous brown belly and flanks.
fp: Females tend to have dark reddish brown flanks and lower belly.

mp: The male has a chocolate brown body with a white head and breast.
fp: The female is a shade of brown with no white on the body.

mp: Adult males are mostly glossy blue-black with a white chin, throat, and upper breast forming a downward point.
fp: Adult females have dull olive upperparts and mostly grayish white underparts.

mp: Adult males are blackish brown on the crown, upperparts, and underparts, with a white throat, neck, and upper breast, and black-brown tail with wide white tips.
fp: Adult females are browner than males with sometimes a paler lower back and rump, duller white throat, and reduced or absent white tail tips.

mp: The male has a striking chestnut belly.
fp: The female lacks the striking chestnut belly.

mp: Adult males have a mostly glossy purplish black head, body, and tail, with a mostly white wing featuring purplish black coverts, some red on the tertials, and black tips on the primaries.
fp: Adult females have an ash-gray head and upperparts, darker gray wings and tail with white outer edges on some feathers, and paler gray underparts with darker mottling on the breast.

mp: Adult males have pale grayish brown upperparts with blackish spots and brown streaks, a white supercilium, and whitish wings and tail.
fp: Adult females have buffy underparts and lack white in their plumage.

mp: Males of the nominate subspecies are almost entirely gray with lighter underparts, a white interscapular patch, and narrow white tips on wing coverts and tail feathers.
fp: Females have olive-gray upperparts, browner wings and tail, cinnamon-edged wing coverts, and tawny-buff underparts with an olive tinge on the flanks.

mp: Adult males have a mostly black and white speckled face and neck sides, reddish brown crown and nape, grayish brown back with black spots, and rufous brown tail.
The male has white on the wing strip, chin and throat, with a pale rufous breast and upper belly.
fp: The female has browner olive grey upperparts, a pale reddish brown wing stripe and underparts.

mp: The male has a rufous head, a yellow pouch, and yellow around the eye.
fp: The female has a black neck and head, a smaller bill and casque, and blue and yellow around the eye and on the chin.

mp: Adult males are mostly gray with darker upperparts, a white patch between the scapulars, and a lower back with white-edged black patches.
fp: Adult females have a warm brown crown and upperparts, a gray face and underparts, and a white throat.

mp: Males are a darker shade of blue or purple.
fp: Females are a brownish color.

mp: The male has a black head, throat, wings and tail, with a blue bill, dark iris and dark greyish tail.
fp: The female is almost entirely black except for the white collar around its neck.

mp: Adult males have a mostly gray face, dark gray upperparts with a white shoulder patch, blackish gray wings with narrow white tips, and white underparts with a light gray tinge.
fp: Adult females have upperparts like the male but lack white wing tips, and have light reddish yellow-brown underparts with a paler throat and gray flanks.

mp: The male has black upper parts with a bluish sheen and yellow underparts.
fp: The female is duller than the male.

mp: The male has a pearly-grey crown and pure white plumage with a yellow beak.
fp: The female has pale brownish-grey upper parts, greyish-white underparts, and a yellow beak.

mp: Males are blue on the top of the head with a red area on the crown.
fp: Females have a smaller area of blue on the head and no red.

mp: Adult males have silky sulfur-yellow underparts contrasting with darker honey-brown upperparts, dark brown crown and face with an iridescent coppery sheen, and enlarged bifurcate nasal wattles.
fp: Females lack the enlarged wattles and are duller overall with brown upperparts.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with a white central streak, a white supercilium, gray upperparts with white patches, and mostly plain yellow underparts.
fp: Females have the same pattern as males but with different colors, featuring upperparts heavily marked with dusky and buff.

mp: Adult males have a black crown with white spots, bright lemon yellow supercilium and underparts, and black malar moustache.
fp: Adult females are overall paler than males, with light buff crown center and wing covert tips.

mp: Adult males have a shiny emerald-green head with a yellow eye-ring, a wide yellow collar, bright yellow rump, and bright yellow breast center.
fp: Adult females are duller and plainer than males, being mostly grass-green including their tail.

mp: Adult males have a mostly dark olive head with a hidden golden-yellow crown stripe, slaty face, white throat, and underparts ranging from sooty olive to cinnamon-rufous.
fp: Adult females lack yellow on the crown, have a dark olive head with a gray throat, and cinnamon-buff underparts.

mp: Adult males have a slate-gray to dark brown or blackish crown with a bright yellow to orange-yellow stripe along its middle, bright olive-green nape and back, and pale to medium yellow underparts with an olive wash on the breast.
fp: Females are smaller than males and have a paler gray crown and mid-crown stripe and slightly paler upperparts.

mp: Males have red crests.
fp: Females have yellow crests.

mp: Adult males have a golden-yellow crown and nape, bright olive upperparts, and a paler yellower olive face, throat, and breast with a pale yellow belly.
fp: Adult females have a duller and less yellow head and breast than males, with similar other features.

mp: The adult male has a black crown with a buff margin, buff head with black-tipped feathers, pale buff throat, reddish-buff breast with black spots, and greyish-bronze upperparts.
fp: The female is larger and more brightly coloured than the male, featuring a bright rufous nape collar during the breeding season.

mp: Adult males have a grayish white supercilium, black crown and nape, olive back, bright yellow lower back and rump, and pale gray throat and breast.
fp: Adult females have an olive-brown crown, nape, and eyeline, a gray supercilium, and dull olive-brown wings.

mp: The plumage is largely dusky olive with orange forehead and lores, a deep orange rump extending to sulphur yellow, and yellowish chin and throat.
fp: Females have less extensive yellow on the face and the rump is yellow and lacks the orange.

mp: Adult males have a small dark red patch in the center of their crown, a pale blue back, and the rest of their plumage is black.
fp: Adult females have olive-green upperparts with browner wing coverts and flight feathers, and paler green underparts.

mp: Males have a mostly gray head, dark yellowish red-brown upperparts and tail, black throat and upper breast, and a white belly center.
fp: Females have paler upperparts than males and mostly reddish yellow-brown underparts with a white belly.
